Scientists have identified crucial windows of opportunity to target aggressive brain cancer with chemotherapy, potentially revolutionising treatment for glioblastoma.

New research suggests that rather than delaying chemotherapy for several weeks post-surgery, the treatment could be most effective in the immediate minutes and days following an operation to remove a glioblastoma tumour.

This is because the blood-brain barrier – a protective layer of cells that typically restricts drug access to the brain – is "disrupted" during two distinct periods shortly after surgery.

Currently, a four to six-week delay between surgery and the commencement of chemotherapy and radiotherapy is standard practice, largely considered necessary for patient recovery.

However, experts believe these early findings, though still preliminary, could fundamentally reshape patient care.

open image in gallery Swimmer Archie Goodburn has called on the prime minister to invest in brain cancer research ( PA )

The researchers suggest that future medical strategies could "exploit" these temporary windows, allowing for a more direct and potent attack on any remaining cancerous cells immediately after surgical removal.

It comes after Scottish swimmer Archie Goodburn made an emotional plea to Prime Minister Andy Burnham to establish a national brain cancer lead.

The 25-year-old, who was diagnosed with brain cancer when he was 22, described how trials around the world are not being seen in the UK which is “unfair and unjust”.

Speaking on BBC Breakfast, Goodburn was in tears as he said: “Please invest and make the difference. I’m on my knees begging for not just my own life but those who are affected and the families all around the country.

“This has to change, it has been going on for too long and the suffering is unbearable.”

The Prime Minister responded to the emotional plea by inviting Goodburn to meet him.

The authors of the new study, published in the journal Science Translational Medicine, said that the effects of glioblastoma removal surgery on the blood-brain barrier, and the impacts of chemotherapy, “have not been systematically studied” in the past.

Researcher’s from The University of Manchester performed mice studies to mimic the clinical procedure of removing a tumour and used a formulation which does not typically enter the brain unless there is disruption to the blood-brain barrier.

The research team found that the surgery disrupts the blood brain barrier “revealing the opportunity for early treatment unitisiation within specific temporal windows”.

The windows are 15 minutes and 48 to 72 hours post surgery.

They said that by “exploiting” these time frames, they “effectively suppressed tumour recurrence”.

Dr Thomas Kisby, co-lead on the study at The University of Manchester, said: “For the first time, we’ve shown that glioblastoma surgery briefly exposes a vulnerability we can exploit.

“If treatment is timed during specific windows we identified, it is able to halt the disease significantly before it regrows.

“We suggest that the hours and days immediately after surgery may hold the key to stopping glioblastoma from returning.

“It also raises the possibility that other established medicines could be redeployed in smarter, more strategic ways.”

Co-lead of the study, Professor Kostas Kostarelos, from The University of Manchester and the Catalan Institute of Nanoscience and Nanotechnology in Barcelona, added: “This research has the potential to open a new frontier in post-operative cancer care.

“After surgery, brain tumours often grow back from the tissue surrounding the area where the tumour was removed. We propose using the latest targeted treatments, including nanoparticle-based medicines, immunotherapy, and gene therapies, to treat this high-risk area and improve patients’ chances of long-term survival.”

open image in gallery Experts believe early findings, though still preliminary, could fundamentally reshape patient care ( Getty/iStock )

Dr Gerben Borst, honorary consultant oncologist at The Christie NHS Foundation Trust, said: “One of the greatest challenges in treating glioblastoma is eliminating the microscopic cancer cells that remain after surgery.

“These findings suggest that a better understanding of the body’s natural response to surgery could help us deliver anti-cancer drugs more effectively, rather than relying solely on the development of entirely new and costly medicines.

“While this research is still at an early stage, it provides important insights into how drug delivery to the brain could be improved.

“Further research, including clinical trials, will be needed to determine whether this approach benefits patients. This work has the potential to provide a practical and rapidly translatable strategy for improving the treatment of glioblastoma.”

Professor Robert Bristow, director of the Manchester Cancer Research Centre, added: “Glioblastoma is the deadliest form of brain cancer, so these research results are incredibly exciting and promises a potential breakthrough in the work to stop the tumour cells growing back after surgery.”

Commenting, Dr Simon Newman, chief scientific officer at The Brain Tumour Charity, said: “This vital early-stage study illustrates the complexity involved in developing drugs to treat brain tumours because they must first cross the restrictive blood-brain barrier in order to target the tumour.

“Discovering that the blood-brain barrier may be more porous following initial surgery and that this may provide a therapeutic opportunity for drugs to access their target shows potential.

“The next step would be to ensure that these laboratory studies are translated through to clinical trials.

“The Brain Tumour Charity funds translational research including multiple studies looking at how to overcome the drug delivery hurdle. We are also proud to support the EPIC-GB clinical study which assesses which drugs can cross the blood brain barrier in patients.”

What is glioblastoma, what are the symptoms and are there any treatments?

Glioblastomas are considered the deadliest and fastest-growing brain tumours. Around 3,200 people are diagnosed annually in the UK. Only 160 survive for five years or more.

This cancer grows quickly, forming tumours that penetrate various brain regions.

Symptoms include headaches caused by a build-up of pressure; personality changes and memory problems. People may also have trouble speaking or understanding what is happening, extreme tiredness and depression.

Patients may also experience seizures and sight problems.

Common treatments include surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy.

Britain's retail sector faced continued challenges in July as persistent heatwave conditions deterred shoppers, with high streets particularly affected, new figures suggest.

Total UK footfall declined by 2.1% year-on-year, an improvement from June’s 3.4% drop, according to British Retail Consortium (BRC)-Sensormatic data.

High street footfall was down 3.8% annually, better than June’s 6.2% fall. Shopping centres also saw a 1.4% year-on-year decrease, an improvement on the 2.5% drop recorded the previous month.

England registered the weakest performance across the UK nations, with an overall footfall reduction of 3%.

London experienced a significant 5.3% decline, highlighting the ongoing difficulties larger urban centres face during periods of extreme heat, Sensormatic noted.

BRC chief executive Helen Dickinson said: “The heatwave continued to bear down on retail footfall in July, with high streets worst affected.

“London was hit particularly hard as soaring temperatures made tube and train travel less attractive, with some commuters and shoppers opting to stay home.

“Nonetheless, it was still an improvement on the previous month’s figures, when record-breaking sunshine saw footfall fall by an even bigger margin.”

High street footfall was down 3.8% year-on-year in July ( PA )

She said: “Climate change continues to deliver more and more extreme temperatures in the UK.

“Retailers are responding by investing in both mitigations – such as more air conditioning and more efficient refrigeration units – and in sustainability initiatives aimed at reducing carbon emissions.

“Unfortunately, business rates often punish stores for such investments, showing the need for government to look again at this broken system.”

Andy Sumpter, from Sensormatic, said six of the first seven months of this year performed worse than the same period last year.

He said: “The exceptionally hot and historically dry weather is likely to have been a significant factor, discouraging shopping trips and particularly impacting high streets.

“While the UK has yet another new prime minister, retail is yet to experience any meaningful ‘Burnham bounce’. For retailers, the focus remains on converting these more selective visits into meaningful spend as the summer progresses.”

Parts of the country are set to be hit by thundery showers, but southern England is once again likely to miss out on most of the much-needed rain before a potential new heatwave.

Temperatures are are expected to be on the cooler side on Thursday, the Met Office said, after a spike at the start of the week. There will also be a marked North-South split in conditions.

British farmers, meanwhile, are facing a "completely brutal" year, with analysis suggesting the 2026 harvest could be the worst on record due to extreme summer weather.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

News.title: The best luxury hotels in the Cotswolds
News.content:
From gracious old farmsteads and magnificent manor houses to an ancient coaching inn creaking with Tudor character, the top luxury hotels in the Cotswolds combine a wonderful sense of history with contemporary style and outstanding modern British cuisine. Whether near picturesque Broadway in the north of the region or close to Bath in the south, location is a key attribute to them all: some offer serene escapes in acres of their own rolling parkland; others sit amid superb gardens; and several take over classic honey-stone villages that look as if they have been beamed in from a halcyon era of the past.

They all excel in providing creature comforts, whether crackling fires by kick-back sofas, canopy beds with soft throws, or suites with terraces and hot tubs. Facilities are top-notch too, ranging from beautiful bars and quiet terraces to blissful spas with inviting pools and even an opportunity for equine adventures. News.title: El Nino could cause explosion of rabid seals, animal health experts warn
News.content:
This year’s El Nino weather event risks propelling an outbreak of rabid seals around the world, the world’s animal health body has warned.

Countries in South America and Australasia are being urged to look for signs the deadly infectious disease has reached their waters, only two years after it was first confirmed in South Africa.

The 2024 discovery of rabies in South Africa’s Cape fur seals was the first significant outbreak ever found in marine mammals and has been described as a “significant shift in rabies ecology”.

More than 100 cases have been confirmed in South Africa and Namibia since then, raising fears that aggressive rabid seals could infect humans, pets and other wildlife.

Changing patterns in fish stocks caused by the El Nino phenomenon now potentially risk widening the spread, as uninfected seal populations migrate for food and come into contact with rabid colleagues.

Scientists believe warming sea temperatures off Antarctica could send seal populations northwards into Southern African waters, where they could be exposed to rabies.

They could then return to their home waters, taking the virus with them and infecting other seal populations.

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

Sports.title: ‘Never heard a bigger load of rubbish’ – Ex-British tennis No1 slams Man Utd legend Paul Scholes in scathing rant
Sports.content:
GREG RUSEDSKI slammed Paul Scholes in a scathing rant – then challenged him to a game of tennis.

The former British No1 even hit out at the ex-Manchester United midfielder’s take as the “biggest load of rubbish in my life”.



Scholes, 51, ruffled his feathers during an episode of The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast with co-hosts Paddy McGuinness and Nicky Butt.

During the show, he claimed football is a more physically demanding sport than tennis.



Scholes – who played 718 times for the Red Devils between 1994 and 2013 – moaned about tennis: “Every two minutes you go and have your nice little glass of orange juice.

“You can play it when you’re 50, tennis. Play it when you’re 70, tennis.”



Then he added: “Football is much more demanding than tennis.”

But Rusedski was having none of it.

The Canada-born tennis star, winner of 15 career titles and former world No4, fired back in a brutal response.

And now he wants Scholes to walk the walk after talking the talk.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Sports.title: Rodri WANTS to join Barcelona in major blow to new Man City boss Enzo Maresca with Real Madrid missing out on Spain star
Sports.content:
RODRI wants to join Barcelona in a transfer blow for new Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca.

Spain’s World Cup winning captain is keen on a move back to his homeland after seven years at the Etihad.



And Barca are in pole position to beat Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid for the midfield maestro.

Rodri, 30, is in the final year of his City contract with no sign he is ready to extend his current deal.



Real, who have agreed a £115.8million deal with RB Leipzig for Yan Diomande, 19, were willing to pay £43m for Rodri’s signature.

But no agreement has materialised and Barca have stepped up their interest.

Barca midfielder Frenkie de Jong is expected to be out of action for a lengthy period after a medial knee ligament tear.

And a move to the Nou Camp would appeal to midfield ace Rodri given the bad blood he has with Real from when he won the Ballon d’Or in autumn 2024.

City, managed by Maresca after the Italian replaced Pep Guardiola this summer, had to give careful consideration to their own contract offer to Rodri – given the fact the defensive midfielder missed much of the last two years due to injury.

England midfielder Elliot Anderson has arrived for £116m but City could yet go to sign a replacement for Rodri if he leaves.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Morocco’s World Cup star Ayyoub Bouaddi is keen on a move from Lille to City although the French club are holding out for around £85m.

Meanwhile, winger Jeremy Doku has become the latest player to commit his long-term future to City.

The Belgium international has penned a five-year deal which will keep him at the Etihad until 2031 with the option of a further year.

Phil Foden, Abdukodir Khusanov and Josko Gvardiol have already given new boss Enzo Maresca a boost by signing up for the long-term.

And Doku’s contract is expected to be officially confirmed when he returns to training at the City Football Academy next week.



The 24-year-old has become one of the most dangerous wide men in the Prem since arriving from Rennes in a £55 million deal three years ago.

His game developed under Pep Guardiola’s coaching and he was a key player last year as City won the domestic cup double.

Maresca is expected to rely heavily on getting the ball to wingers in his first season in charge so Doku is likely to be an integral part of his plans.



City could look to the transfer market if the likes of Rodri and Savinho depart.

However they are in no rush to do more business in the current window.

As well as the record signing of Anderson, they signed Antoine Semenyo and Marc Guehi in January and believe their recruitment has been strong this year.

Elsewhere, James Trafford became the third-most-expensive goalkeeper of all time as he left City after just one year to join Leeds in a £45m deal.

Sports.title: Man Utd forced into tense reunion with £325,000-a-week Rashford… but if anyone can make it work, it’s Carrick
Sports.content:
THERE is usually great fanfare when a prodigal son returns home.

You think of the excitement among Tottenham fans as Gareth Bale rejoined from Real Madrid in 2020, or when Wayne Rooney made his Everton comeback at Goodison Park after 13 years away.



It’s fair to say Marcus Rashford’s unlikely return to Old Trafford has an altogether different vibe.

Because 18 months ago the prospect of a reunion with Manchester United looked about as likely as taking the eggs out of a baked cake.



And to be honest, he seemed pretty relieved about that.

By the time he was packed off to Aston Villa in February last year, his relationship with then-manager Ruben Amorim had not so much soured as rotted to the core.

He was snubbed by the Portuguese, who claimed Rashford’s attitude was so poor that he would rather select his 63-year-old goalkeeping coach Jorge Vital as a United sub.

It was quite a fall from grace for the England star, whose reputation had been near impeccable to that point.

But he answered the criticism with good performances on loan at Villa and Barcelona.

His exit at Old Trafford looked so set in stone that he had no qualms handing over his No 10 shirt to Matheus Cunha last summer.

And yet it is looking increasingly likely he will be back this season, meaning the United board find themselves in a very awkward position.

Because it wasn’t as straightforward as Amorim forcing him out — the club wanted him gone and his huge wages off their books.

He signed his mammoth £325,000-a-week contract, making him the club’s top earner, off the back of a stunning 2022-23 season when he netted 17 goals in the Premier League and looked right back to his best.

The Red Devils gave him the new deal a year before Sir Jim Ratcliffe purchased his stake in the club and took control of footballing operations.

The billionaire immediately went about making himself the most unpopular man in Manchester by making savage cuts, with hundreds of staff members made redundant.



Clearly, Ratcliffe and his new board resented the amount of money that Rashford was on from the very start, and they made it pretty obvious they were going to try to get rid at the first opportunity.

It was even leaked to the media by the club in the weeks before he left for Villa that every United manager had had issues with Rashford, not just Amorim.

When you have grown up in Manchester, supported United all your life and been in the academy since the age of seven, it’s not a huge surprise he was left bruised and disillusioned.

We saw something similar play out last year with captain Bruno Fernandes, the club’s second-highest earner, who went on the record saying the club wanted him gone.



Now, with a move to another side looking increasingly unlikely, the board are going to have to spin it back and say it was Amorim who wanted Rashford gone. Nothing to do with us, guv.

It all sets the stage for a potentially tense reunion — but the reason it could work is the man in the dugout.

Since Michael Carrick took over in January, the entire mood around United has shifted.

He immediately made Fernandes feel appreciated and he went on to produce one of the best second halves to a season in Prem history.

If anyone has the empathy, skills, and respect of his players, to rebuild the bridges burnt by Amorim and the board, it’s Carrick. He’s shown he can do it already.



There is little doubt Rashford, 28, is still a hugely talented player and, when he’s on song, he has a lot to offer at the highest level.

So the United hierarchy doesn’t have much choice but to put the politics of the last couple of difficult years aside and try to reintegrate him.

Luckily, they have the right man in charge to do it.



No Vin situation

Sorry to break it to Arsenal fans, but there wasn’t a chance in hell you were signing Vinicius Jr.

It was pretty clear from the off, especially for a cynic like me, that the Gunners were being used so the Brazilian could negotiate a pay rise at Real Madrid.

So it has come to pass, with him reportedly agreeing a brand spanking new contract at the Bernabeu.

It would have been the shock of the century had he not stayed at Real.

The arrival of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle should soften the blow for Arsenal.



But if their listless pre-season defeat by Real Betis is any guide, they still have work to do this transfer window.

Marc on the world stage

Being knocked out by the Argies in the World Cup semi-final was a very bitter pill to swallow for every England fan.

But we can at least console ourselves with the knowledge that we, as a country, are living rent-free in their heads.



The Argentine FA has announced July 15 will become ‘National Football Teams Day’, to commemorate their victory in Atlanta.

Not only did they embarrass themselves on the pitch in the final defeat by Spain, they’re now embarrassing themselves off it.

Big jump in prices

One of the most dispiriting aspects of Jumps racing — a sport millions of us love — is that the same faces seem to win everything.

If it’s not Willie Mullins or Gordon Elliott in Ireland, it’s Dan Skelton in England — and our reigning champion trainer continues to get stronger.

All-conquering owner JP McManus this week sent Skelton a new batch of future stars, including a £428,000 buy called Walkonseas.

Smaller owners and trainers are being priced out nowadays as the rich keep getting richer.

It means fewer and fewer yards can compete — and the game is all the poorer for it.

Sports.title: ‘It’s tough’ – Matthias Jaissle breaks silence on Guimaraes’ Arsenal transfer but insists Newcastle have ‘no excuses’
Sports.content:
MATTHIAS JAISSLE has “no excuse” not to bring success back to Newcastle despite the exodus of star names.

The German, 38, officially took charge on Wednesday – the same day a £75million fee was agreed with Arsenal for skipper Bruno Guimaraes – after arriving from Ah-Ahli in Saudi Arabia.



The Brazilian is the third big name departure after Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, though club chiefs are adamant Lewis Hall will not follow them despite Manchester United’s interest.

Jaissle said: “We lost a couple of really important players, but that’s also a chance.



“You can see it in a negative way, that there’s a lot of challenges and we can search for excuses, but that’s not our idea. We see the chance in these things.

“Give me a bit of time to really get to know the players, work with them. That’s the most important thing.



“We have a clear vision of where we want to go, and we want to be successful – of course, everyone wants to be that.

“It’s about hard work now in the pre-season and making progress.”

Newcastle have brought in a host of exciting young talents to replace the big hitters – but some are tipping Toon to be battling down the bottom rather than challenging at the top.

Even legendary record scorer Alan Shearer admits it will be a “challenge” for the new man following a bruising summer.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Jaissle added: “I didn’t hear the talk (about relegation) because I try to avoid reading these things. I’ve mentioned it a couple of times but this is the challenge.

“There are so many transitions at the moment, many players left, big, big players, legends for the club left.

“But we need to see it as a chance, not having too many excuses now, just thinking forward (of) what we can influence.

“Control the controllables, I used to say, and we are sure there will be progress.”



Jaissle has been with his squad in La Manga since Saturday but admitted he had no involvement in the decision to sell Guimaraes.

Though he says fans can expect some incomings to fill the huge voids left.

He revealed: “One day I met him [Guimaraes] quickly, but the decision was already made.

“It was a nice conversation, a fantastic player, but also a great human being.

“It’s tough, but for him also the next challenge, and we need to deal with it at a later stage.



“We trust the players who are here already, but we will also see some changes.

“I have some clear ideas but I want to give the players who are here a chance. They can show up. It is a new challenge for them and we can wait.

“We have, for sure, the capacity to do something on the market and our sporting director is aware of that.

Sports.title: Man Utd icon Nicky Butt BANNED from local tip after ‘raging’ row with staff
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER United great Nicky Butt claims he has been banned from his local tip after a row with staff.

Butt, 51, was “raging” when his Range Rover was deemed to be a commercial vehicle as the seats were down.



But the former midfielder went ahead and dumped his “smelly bags” at the centre near his home in Cheshire, chased by an attendant with a walkie-talkie.

He said: “There’s this guy at the gate bit, and he flags me down and goes, ‘Put your windows down I need to look in the back of your car’. I’m going, ‘What for?’.”



The Class of 92 hero continued: “I’ve got a lot of crap from the house, bit of cardboard . . . I missed the bin man last week, so I’ve got a few smelly bags. So I put the windows down, obviously my seats were down and apparently I’m not going in because it’s a commercial van. So I’m raging, literally.

“I’m putting a bit of cardboard in the tip.”



Butt then claimed the attendant accused him of trying to sneak in items.

The dad of two told The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast: “He said to me, ‘Your windows are blacked out because you’re sneaking stuff into it, into the tip’. And I went, ‘No, it’s standard, mate’.”

He then decided to drive into the site, believed to be the Woodhouse Lane Recycling Centre in Altrincham.

He said: “I thought, well, I’m there now, I’m gonna go for it. So I’ve got up the ramp, I see this bloke getting up . . . trying to chase me up the hill, but he’s got his walkie-talkie out.



“So I’ve literally got up the top, throw all the bags out, and I’m going back down the hill, and he’s going mad at me. Anyway, I’m banned from the tip.”

Butt won six Premier League titles, three FA Cups and the Champions League with United before moving to Newcastle in 2004.

He then finished playing in China, and was CEO of League Two side Salford until quitting in 2024.



The Sun contacted him for comment.

Sports.title: World Cup team ‘suddenly’ paid by Fifa after EIGHT MONTHS of asking – days after accusing Infantino of ‘blackmail’
Sports.content:
JORDAN have suddenly received all of the money owed by Fifa after an eight-month wait.

The drama came as the funds arrived just TWO days after their FA chief accused the governing body of “blackmail”.



Prince Ali bin Al Hussein confirmed on X that the outstanding bonuses from December’s Fifa Arab Cup had finally been paid on Thursday morning.

The Jordan FA president thanked Fifa for delivering the cash owed to the national team’s players and coaching staff.



He stressed that the payment had arrived nearly a year after Jordan reached the Arab Cup final in Qatar.

But Prince Ali insisted the development would not change his stance on the controversial Fifa president Gianni Infantino.



He said: “It does not change my clear position concerning the leadership of Fifa.

“My FA and I will not endorse president Infantino, nor will we vote for him.”

The dramatic payment came just 48 hours after Prince Ali launched a blistering attack on Fifa and claimed Jordan had been pressured to back Infantino.

He alleged that during this summer’s World Cup he was verbally told endorsing the Swiss chief would “go a long way” towards helping his cash-strapped association.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

He said: “For months, Fifa has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters – until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

“But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.”

Jordan had been waiting since December for the prize money earned by reaching the Arab Cup final, despite repeatedly asking for the funds.

Prince Ali also criticised the difficulties facing his country during their first World Cup.



That included supporters being denied US visas, expensive tickets and tax costs for players and staff.

Infantino, 56, is fighting to retain control after abandoning his controversial plan to allow private investors to buy a stake in the World Cup enterprise.

But he vowed to remain in office, while the FA, Welsh FA and Uefa have withdrawn their support ahead of next year’s presidential election.

In the X post, he wrote: “Thank you to the Fifa administration for suddenly this morning delivering what was owed to our players and coaching staff, for the Jordan National team’s accession to the final of the Fifa Arab Cup in Qatar last December.

“This was funding that should have been received eight months ago.



“While this is a good development for our players, it does not change the serious concerns we in the football world have regarding the Fifa leadership.

“Nor does it change what our FAs have been subjected to in the past.

“It is symptomatic of those exact difficulties that we all face, and that are usually linked to the Fifa presidential elections.

“And it does not change my clear position concerning the leadership of Fifa.

“My FA will not endorse president Infantino, nor will we vote for him.”



At the 2026 Fifa World Cup, Jordan did not manage to overcome any of their three opponents – Argentina, Algeria, and Austria – in Group J.

Sports.title: New Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle denies CHAOS at club after big-name exits as he repeats key word five times
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE have endured a summer of chaos with three star players and the manager out of the door.

But if the exodus has left the Toon Army fearing the worst, the buzzword within the club is “transition”.



New boss Matthias Jaissle used it five times in a ten-minute interview with the media in La Manga – after firstly refusing to use the recent big-name exits as an excuse not to succeed.

Fresh from losing captain Bruno Guimaraes, as well as the departures of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, Eddie Howe’s replacement Jaissle was ice cool as he sat on a stool in a La Manga club house to answer questions.



The 38-year-old German faces a baptism of fire and has his work cut out to get Newcastle into shape in time for the Premier League season opener against Liverpool in 16 days time.

But while Howe no longer had the energy for the fight anymore, Jaissle had no doubt in the sweltering 34C heat he would have his squad ready for the Reds.



He said: “I’m confident to do the best out of that short amount of time.

“Of course it’s another challenge, because there’s not too many days left until the first match against Liverpool, but that’s now the phase.

“You cannot change anything, I cannot ask the squad director to turn the time back again.

“So, again, all together, the whole staff, we tried to encourage them in the first meeting already, that now it’s even more important that everyone raises the standards, and the same we expect from the players, to find that unity and that DNA of how we want to play football already in the first match.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Toon’s performance director James Bunce described the short turnaround to install the new man’s ideas as “speed dating with no time to waste”.

But no matter what work goes on, many feel Howe hit the glass ceiling by lifting the Carabao Cup and qualifying for the Champions League in 2025, especially given the financial handcuffs imposed by SCR rules.

It has forced Toon into flogging several star names. Recruitment has focused on bringing in a host of promising, though some unproven, prodigies to bolster the ranks.



From the outside looking in, the glory days appear to be way off. But Jaissle, despite his tender years, says leading a young team to the top is his speciality.

He said: “It was a really, really successful story under Eddie. There’s huge respect for what he was building and now there are many, many changes. But, that’s a chance and we want to build on that chance and start growing.

“In Salzburg I had a couple of challenges but we were so successful. Then in Al-Ahli in Saudi Arabia, I took over a club that was just promoted and we were also quite successful there.

“So I can manage when there are a lot of challenges within the club and the transition and working with young players. This is the approach and also why I’m here now.”

Jaissle does arrive with silverware on his CV. He won the double in his first season at Salzburg and retained the league the next while reaching the Champions League knockouts.



Two years later he helped transform Al-Ahli into one of Asia’s top sides, leading them to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns and a Saudi Super Cup.

Managing in the Premier League against some of the game’s greatest coaches is a whole different ball game.

And trophies are very much on the agenda on Tyneside.

He said: “This is something I don’t have on my CV, but that’s normal in football. At one point it has to be your first step and I’m now at that moment after being successful in Saudi Arabia and Austria. Everyone was dreaming about being a part of the Premier League and now here we are.

“I have always big ambitions. That’s the key element for every coach, otherwise I would be not here.



“That’s the same here now in Newcastle, but it’s always easy saying where we want to go and on which place we want to end up. For me, it doesn’t make too much sense in football because it’s difficult to plan things in advance.

EDDIE HOWE'S RECORD AT NEWCASTLE EDDIE HOWE will forever be a Newcastle legend after leading the Toon to their first trophy in 70 years. But that Carabao Cup win, and two Champions League qualifications, weren’t enough to keep everyone happy on Tyneside. Here is Howe’s Newcastle record: Premier League 2021-22 – 11th (19th when he took over) 2022-23 – 4th 2023-24 – 7th 2024-25 – 5th 2025-26 – 12th Trophies won Carabao Cup 2024-25

“As you probably know, therefore, it’s for me the most important thing that you just do your best every day and get the best out of the players, try to improve them, support them, give them also the courage to grow, and that’s now the phase where we’re in in the pre-season, and therefore I’m really much looking forward.”

Both a member of the Saudi Public Investment Fund, who own 80 per cent of the club, and Jamie Reuben, who owns the rest, were on camp at the Hotel Grand Hyatt La Manga Club.

Newcastle CEO David Hopkinson, whose aim is to be “in the debate about being the top club in the world” by 2030, and sporting director Ross Wilson were too.



They all want a return on the £9.5m compensation fee paid for Jaissle. But with such a young squad, the Toon Army may be in for a few more rough moments before the Mags are flying high again.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But bullish Jaissle, who used the magic word one final time, cannot wait to get going.

Jaissle added: “This is now a transition phase, but I’m really excited now to finally officially be here in the camp already. I’m even more looking forward to seeing them back home in Newcastle and start that journey.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino offered shock lifeline as under-fire FIFA chief's World Cup final plan pays off
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino offered shock lifeline as under-fire FIFA chief's World Cup final plan pays off

Gianni Infantino has been under severe scrutiny as of recent due to his controversial plans to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors, with calls for his resignation flooding in

View 2 Images CAF have backed Gianni Infantino (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

The Confederation of African Football executive committee has "unanimously reconfirmed" support in Gianni Infantino, after widespread calls for the FIFA president to lose his job. The 56-year-old executive sparked outrage last week with proposals to sell a stake of the World Cup to private investors.

‌



The move, which was dubbed the 'FIFA Forward Enterprise' was swiftly met with widespread criticism, with UEFA vowing to boycott the tournament outright should plans have proceeded. The backlash ultimately prompted Infantino to shelve his proposals, which he dubbed to be an act of consolation rather than concrete plans that World Football were planning on rolling out.

‌



However, that hasn't prevented the Italian from seeing calls for his axing in the days since, with furious football fans and governing bodies outraged by the notion. Having held an emergency meeting in Rabat, executives instilled their faith in Infantino, sharing a scathing public statement which hit out at "attacks on its integrity."

‌



It read: "As previously communicated, the FFE proposal, which would have been subject to the approval of the FIFA Member Associations and the FIFA Council, is now off the table.

Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed READ MORE :

"With the project withdrawn, it was agreed that FIFA will no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation.

"There are always lessons to be learned, and FIFA will continue to improve its processes in light of this experience. In this instance, however, it is important to stress that, although mistakes were made, everything that was done was done in full compliance with the FIFA regulatory framework."

‌



And now, CAF have reaffirmed their commitment to Infantino with a statement of their own, in a major boost to the likelihood of the head of World Football retaining his job. It read: "The CAF EXCO also unanimously reconfirmed its support for FIFA President Gianni Infantino and thanked him for his support for African Football, over the years.

The 18-year-old attacking midfielder joins the Red Devils from Fortaleza CEIF, who play in the Colombian Categoria Primera A. Orozco is a Colomba Under-18 international and highly-rated for the future.

‌



Orozco's move was made official last month when he turned 18, though United did not immediately confirm the transfer. The statement announcing his move to England, shared on Thursday night, confirmed the talented teenager will initially link up with United's academy.

‌



Reports outlining the agreement struck by United to bring Orozco to Old Trafford emerged last year, with the youngster later confirming he visited Carrington back in December.

Man Utd forced to fork out millions as Marcus Rashford benefits from contract loophole READ MORE :

Marcus Rashford primed for Ruben Amorim reunion after Man Utd transfer twist READ MORE :

Speaking to ESPN Colombia about the move, he said: "I know my strengths are my physicality and my technique.

"I have those qualities and, with the gift God gave me, I don’t think it will be too difficult. But everything is about adapting. I’m very young and that’s what I’ll need to do."

‌



He added: "I expect to learn a lot of English. When I was there, I realised just how, how important it is.

"I want to arrive and learn as quickly as possible. That’s what’s required so I can show my level and everything I’m capable of. I want to adapt to everything that comes my way as quickly as possible."

‌



While Orozco is set to link up with the academy, United have strengthened in midfield at a more senior level.

Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have been signed from Chelsea and Aston Villa respectively as part of United's plans to overhaul their engine room with the possibility that a further midfielder will be signed before the transfer deadline.

Sports.title: Mohamed Salah's staggering new salary revealed as Liverpool hero agrees special clause
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah's staggering new salary revealed as Liverpool hero agrees special clause

Mohamed Salah has joined Trabzonspor on a two-year contract having left Liverpool as a free agent this summer, and will pick up an eye-watering salary in the Turkish Super Lig

View 2 Images Mohamed Salah is a Trabzonspor player (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Mohamed Salah is in line for an annual salary of £14.5million with Trabzonspor - and that's before lucrative, performance-based bonuses. The 34-year-old only signed a two-year extension with Liverpool last April, but mutually agreed to part ways with the club this summer as he looks to the next stage of his career.

‌



As a result, a number of clubs were linked with making a move for the Egypt star with interests coming in from the likes of Saudi Arabia and Italy. In the end, however, Salah opted to sign the dotted line for Trabzonspor in a deal which will see him through until 2028.

‌



There, Salah will pick up a salary of £14.5m each season, made up of an £8.5m wage and £6m from signing fees, as revealed by Trabzonspor on a public disclosure platform. He will also see a boost in the form of bonuses, should he hit performance-related KPIs over the course of the season.

‌



Salah has also agree a clause which will see hum pocket a 20 per cent cut of any revenue generated by Trabzonspor relating to his likeness. It means that the forward will likely be in line for a huge sum from shirt sales bearing his name and number, as well as special-line items released relating to him.

Liverpool's firm stance on Djed Spence transfer as Reds battle defensive injury crisis READ MORE :

Mo Salah wears new shirt and mobbed by fans as Liverpool icon jets in to seal transfer READ MORE :

Speaking about the move after being welcomed by tens of thousands of fans in Trabzon, Salah shared his commitment to his new club. He said: "I am very happy to be in this incredible atmosphere.

"I don't recall ever seeing anything like this before. There are 25,000 people here —it's incredible.

‌



"I've never seen anything like it. I have achieved success everywhere I've been, and I want to achieve success at Trabzonspor as well."

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

However, Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher remains unconvinced that Salah has made the right decision by signing a deal with Trabzonspor, claiming that he is far too good to be plying his trade in a league outside of Europe's big five.

‌



View 2 Images Mohamed Salah left Liverpool at the end of last season (Image: Getty Images)

Speaking with Football Ramble, he said: "I never believed he was going to go to Saudi, because number one, he's too good for that. I think he can be playing in Serie A.

"Turkey for me feels a level too low. I was convinced he'd end up at an AC Milan or Juventus or somewhere like that, maybe his wages were a problem.

‌



"Looking at him, I don't know him, obviously have never spoken to him. But he's like [Cristiano] Ronaldo, he's so driven, his numbers mean so much to him.

"I thought, he can still do this in Turkey by the way, but I thought he'd want to play at a real prestigious club. Obviously his wage demands have put a few people off but I thought he might almost curb those demands a little bit to almost get a better club.

"To go to an AC Milan or Juventus or whoever it may be, play at the San Siro, still playing in big games, still playing in Europe. Turkey just feels like...I just think he's better than that."

Sports.title: Why Yan Diomande decided against Liverpool transfer after meeting Andoni Iraola
Sports.content:
Why Yan Diomande decided against Liverpool transfer after meeting Andoni Iraola

Liverpool were strongly linked with Yan Diomande, but the winger ultimately chose to join Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid and the reasoning behind that decision has now come to light

View 2 Images Yan Diomande has completed a move to Real Madrid after meeting with Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool's transition season under new boss Andoni Iraola may have played a part in Yan Diomande deciding against a move to Anfield. The 19‑year‑old is said to have met Iraola before choosing his next step - a meeting that ultimately preceded his decision to join Real Madrid instead.

‌



The Reds had explored a deal earlier in the summer and were firmly in the mix for the youngster, but refused to meet RB Leipzig's €130m (£111m) valuation. Their £85m bid was rejected, and the club opted not to return with an improved offer.

‌



Champions League winners Paris Saint‑Germain were also interested, with reports suggesting Diomande had agreed personal terms, but they too fell short of Leipzig’s asking price. Madrid had an £85.4m offer turned down as well, before eventually striking a deal worth up to €140m (£120m).

‌



Darwin Nunez in line for unexpected Liverpool reunion after transfer twist READ MORE :

Liverpool's firm stance on Djed Spence transfer as Reds battle defensive injury crisis READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FC FACEBOOK PAGE! All the latest news and analysis from Anfield on the Liverpool Echo's dedicated LFC Facebook page

Madrid's agreement for Diomande is built around an initial €125m (£107m) fee, with a further €15m (£12.8m) in add‑ons, with the midfielder signing a seven‑year contract. He becomes the sixth arrival of Jose Mourinho's summer rebuild at the Bernabeu, following Ibrahima Konate, Denzel Dumfries, Bernardo Silva, Marc Cucurella and Carlos Espi.

However, Madrid were not initially in the market for a winger. The expectation had been that Nico Paz would return via a buy‑back clause after impressing at Como since leaving in 2024.

‌



That opened the door for Liverpool, who were viewed as Diomande's most likely destination and the prospect of replacing club legend Mohamed Salah was said to appeal to the Ivorian. But after meeting Iraola, Diomande is said to have felt Liverpool were heading into a transition season, prompting him to look elsewhere, according to The Athletic.

He ultimately chose to play under Jose Mourinho and chase a third consecutive Champions League title instead, as Real's new manager prompted a switch in transfer policy.

View 2 Images Yan Diomande met with Andoni Iraola but opted against a move to Liverpool (Image: Shaina Benhiyoun/SPP/Shutterstock)

‌



"The final piece was Jose Mourinho," confirmed Nathan Campbell, Roc Nation's head of global football recruitment and Diomande's agent. "He spoke to him in fluent French, which was massive for him.

"We didn't realise Mourinho spoke fluent French, because he hasn't been at a French club. But the time of day that he took the call with Yan and the fact that he spoke fluently in French with him - about his ideas, the project, and how he would fit into the team - showed that he valued that conversation.

"That was a massive point. The key to convincing him."

Article continues below

The Athletic adds that Diomande was given a detailed career plan, outlining both individual and team‑based development pathways - including case studies such as Vinicius Junior and how his trajectory has evolved at the Bernabeu.

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer saga reaches conclusion as Real Madrid star strikes agreement
Sports.content:
Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer saga reaches conclusion as Real Madrid star strikes agreement

Arsenal had been growing in confidence over their chances of pulling off a blockbuster swoop for Vinicius Junior but the attacker now looks set to stay at Real Madrid

View 2 Images Vinicius Junior has been heavily linked to Arsenal (Image: Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

Vinicius Junior and Real Madrid have reached an agreement over a new contract for the attacker, bringing an end to Arsenal's pursuit of the Brazil international.

‌



Speculation over Vinicius' future has been rife in recent months with the player's current contract expiring next summer and numerous reports indicating that he and the club were apart by some distance in negotiations, with Real said to be refusing to improve their most recent offer.

‌



Arsenal's interest in the multi-time Champions League winner emerged amid that uncertainty, with the Premier League champions ready to go all out to clinch a statement signing.

‌



But despite claims that the player was open to the idea of joining Arsenal, Real Madrid confirmed that Vinicius had reached signed a new contract on Thursday - less than 24 hours after a crunch meeting with club officials on Wednesday.

Arsenal given green light to sign £30m striker after Vinicius Jr transfer update READ MORE :

Liverpool's firm stance on Djed Spence transfer as Reds battle defensive injury crisis READ MORE :

Vinicius' decision to renew his contract with Los Blancos will bitterly disappoint Arsenal and their head coach, Mikel Arteta, who had seen the 26-year-old as the calibre of signing required to take the club to the next level.

Arsenal's search for an elite left forward will now resume again with two key targets, Morgan Rogers and now Vinicius, unattainable in this window.

‌



Arteta has been open about wanting to take Arsenal to another level and "create a dynasty" after ending a 22 year wait for a domestic title. The Gunners also reached the Champions League final last season, losing on penalties.

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta and Arsenal will have to move on to other targets (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

“I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” Arteta said following Arsenal's 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in a pre-season friendly.

‌



“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Sports.title: Darwin Nunez in line for unexpected Liverpool reunion after transfer twist
Sports.content:
Darwin Nunez in line for unexpected Liverpool reunion after transfer twist

Darwin Nunez endured a difficult first season with Al-Hilal in Saudi Arabia and it is understood he could be available to leave during the summer window for as little as £17m

View 2 Images Speculation over Mohamed Salah's next club has been rife for months (Image: OZAN KOSE, AFP via Getty Images)

Mohamed Salah could soon be joined at Trabzonspor by Darwin Nunez, with Salah's former Liverpool team-mate also a transfer target for the ambitious Turkish Super Lig outfit.

‌



Salah announced back in March that the 2025-26 campaign would be his final one as a Liverpool player after reaching an agreement with the Reds to cancel the final year of his contract. Speculation over the 33-year-old's next move has been rife in recent weeks before Besiktas emerged as a potential destination for Salah.

‌



However, the Egypt attacker has now signed a lucrative two year contract with Trabzonspor to become the club's marquee summer signing, and was unveiled in front of fans on Thursday.

‌



With a €17million (£14.5m) a season deal for Salah now signed off, Trabzonspor seemingly have no plans to stop spending and are already targeting Nunez.

Liverpool's firm stance on Djed Spence transfer as Reds battle defensive injury crisis READ MORE :

The i Paper report that Nunez is another attacking player Trabzonspor are keen on. He is well known to Salah after playing alongside the veteran at Anfield for three years before he was sold off to Al-Hilal of the Saudi Pro League.

While it remains to be seen if Nunez would be interested in joining Salah in Turkey, the Uruguay international could move this summer.

‌



Tottenham are said to also hold an interest in Nunez, who joined Liverpool in a package worth £85m including add-ons; a club-record fee at the time. He is now understood to be valued at around £17m, such has been the striker's fall from grace over the last two years.

View 2 Images Darwin Nunez is also a target for Trabzonspor (Image: Getty Image)

Nunez scored 40 goals in 143 appearances for Liverpool but should have had more goals to his name across that period. He fell out of favour during the 2024-25 campaign, during which Arne Slot led the Reds to the Premier League title. Nunez started just eight games in the league that season.

Article continues below

Since moving to Saudi Arabia, Nunez has once again struggled for consistency. He scored just six goals in 16 appearances as Al-Hilal were pipped to the Saudi title by Cristiano Ronaldo's Al-Nassr.

Sports.title: Arsenal given green light to sign £30m striker after Vinicius Jr transfer update
Sports.content:
Arsenal given green light to sign £30m striker after Vinicius Jr transfer update

Arsenal have already began to turn their attention elsewhere after missing out on Vinicius Junior, who is set to extend his Real Madrid contract

View Image Kaua Elias is on Arsenal's radar

Arsenal have reportedly ramped up their pursuit of Kaua Elias after learning that Vinicius Junior is set to sign a new deal with Real Madrid - a major blow for the Gunners, who had been quietly optimistic about pulling off a sensational move for the winger. Their interest effectively nudged Madrid into accelerating negotiations, with talks taking place this week following his return to training.

‌



Until recently, Madrid were adamant they wouldn’t revisit or improve their latest offer. That stance has now hardened further, with Jose Mourinho naming Vinicius among six 'untouchable' players this summer - a clear message that the Brazilian is completely off‑limits.

‌



While the final details of his extension are still being ironed out, all indications point to the talismanic forward staying at the Bernabeu. With that avenue now closed, Arsenal have shifted their focus to Elias, who strengthened his rising reputation on Monday by leading Shakhtar's emphatic 5-1 win over Kudrivka.

‌



Mikel Arteta gives blunt response to Bruno Guimaraes question after Newcastle transfer agreed READ MORE :

7 transfer targets Arsenal could miss out on with Vinicius Jr set to stay at Real Madrid READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The youngster bagged a header, a left-footed strike and a right-footed finish in a thoroughly commanding second-half performance. Arsenal were amongst the clubs present to witness Elias' impressive display, according to The Sun, with Manchester United, AC Milan and FC Porto also monitoring the striker.

Scouts from both Arsenal and United are reported to have provided 'extremely glowing evaluations' of the 20-year-old. Elias' attraction is evident - he's comfortable on both feet, commanding in aerial duels and assured in front of goal - a profile that aligns with Arsenal's recruitment strategy.

‌



The Ukrainian champions are said to value him at approximately £30million, and the expectation is that Arsenal are now considering an official offer.

The report adds that Arsenal have been tracking Elias for several weeks, with his recent hat-trick essentially providing the club with the impetus to intensify their pursuit. United, meanwhile, are also looking to bolster their attacking options this summer, especially with Joshua Zirkzee's future uncertain amid Serie A interest.

Milan and Porto remain in contention, but Arsenal and United are regarded as being in the strongest position financially - both able to trigger the player's release clause and present an attractive package.

‌



Elias himself is believed to be receptive to a switch to one of Europe's top leagues, assuming he's offered a sporting project that corresponds with his development and long-term aspirations.

Since his arrival from Fluminense in 2025, the Brazilian has registered 12 goals and three assists across 39 outings for Shakhtar - a record that's enhanced his standing as one of the most complete young attackers coming through from South America.

Sports.title: Is red-hot Norrie now favourite to win Montreal? Brit dumps out third seed De Minaur
Sports.content:
Five years on from winning his biggest title in Indian Wells, Britain's Cameron Norrie has found his form to dump out third seed Alex de Minaur and reach the fourth round of the National Bank Open in Montreal.

Down 7-5 5-2 with De Minaur on match point, Norrie turned the tables by winning 11 out of the next 13 games to beat the Australian 5-7 7-6 (7-5) 6-1.

Norrie, who has climbed above Arthur Fery to No 36 in the live rankings will become the new British No 1, but the former Wimbledon semi-finalist has ambitions of collecting the second Masters title of his career with Frenchman Arthur Fils up next.

Asked whether he now sees himself as one of the favourites to win the title, Norrie replied: "Everyone is so tough. I'm playing the next highest guy Fils - he's one of the best players in the world when he's confident and playing well but I'm just so happy.

Sports.title: Hearts humbled by Benfica as Hibs secure vital win; Motherwell held in Helsinki
Sports.content:
Hearts endured a predictably bruising evening in Lisbon as their hopes of progressing to the Europa League were all but ended by a 6-1 thrashing at the hands of Benfica.

After a largely demoralising summer, which began with being pipped to the William Hill Premiership title by Celtic in May, 1,300 embattled Jambos travelled to the Portuguese capital for one of the most formidable fixtures in the club's recent history, braced for a fourth consecutive defeat under new head coach Wouter Vrancken.

And that was exactly what transpired as Marco Silva's Benfica opened the scoring in the third minute, led by three at the break and then added another three in the second half to remove all sense of jeopardy from next Thursday's second leg at Tynecastle.

While the Portuguese giants are on course to face the losers of the Champions League tie between Aarhus and Sabah Baku in the Europa League play-off round, Hearts are staring at a likely Conference League play-off against Rapid Vienna, who lead Paide 4-1 after the first leg in Estonia.

Hibernian will take a valuable lead to North Macedonia for the second leg of their Conference League third qualifying round clash after overcoming Shkendija 2-1.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hibernian head coach David Gray says his side will get even better as they beat Shkendija in the first leg of their Conference League third-round qualifier.

Hibs had gone in front in the 73rd minute through Owen Elding, only for the visitors to level less than three minutes later courtesy of Marko Gjorgjievski.

However, Warren O'Hora notched a 90th-minute winner when he bundled in a Jordan Obita corner to leave Hibs in a good position to reach the competition's play-off round when they make the trip to Skopje for the second leg.

Image: Warren O'Hora (L) celebrates after scoring to make it 2-1 to Hibs at Easter Road

Motherwell's impressive start under Alfred Johansson continued as they secured a 1-1 draw away to HJK Helsinki in the first leg of their Conference League third qualifying round tie.

The Lanarkshire side's new Swedish boss briefly looked on course for his fourth consecutive victory at the helm after Tawanda Maswanhise's penalty gave the Steelmen the lead just after the hour mark.

Image: Tawanda Maswanhise put Motherwell ahead in Helsinki

However, 36-year-old former Celtic and Norwich City striker Teemu Pukki equalised for Finnish side HJK within seconds of coming off the bench.

Motherwell, who lost Alex Lowry and Regan Charles-Cook to injuries in the closing stages, will return home believing they have a good chance of setting up a glamour play-off showdown with Europa League runners-up Freiburg later this month.

Sports.title: Barron scores hat-trick as Hull FC end losing run with win over St Helens
Sports.content:
Super League: Harvey Barron scores treble as Hull FC end losing run with win over St Helens

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of St Helens against Hull FC in the Betfred Super League Highlights of St Helens against Hull FC in the Betfred Super League

Winger Harvey Barron scored a first senior hat-trick as Hull FC ended a seven-game losing run with a 32-18 comeback win at St Helens.

Barron's treble boosted the Black and Whites' hopes of avoiding the Super League wooden spoon while casting further doubt on Saints making the end of season play-offs.

Hull had not previously won at the BrewDog Stadium in 10 games and nine years and sat just two points off bottom club Huddersfield Giants.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Player of the match Aidan Sezer conceded it's been a tough season after Hull FC ended their seven-match losing streak against St Helens Player of the match Aidan Sezer conceded it's been a tough season after Hull FC ended their seven-match losing streak against St Helens

However, in this battle of the interim coaches, Andy Last got the better of counterpart Eamon O'Carroll, who last weekend oversaw Saints' first defeat at York in more than 80 years.

Hull trailed 14-10 approaching half-time but Barron struck almost on the hooter and completed his career landmark hat-trick after 47 minutes before substitute Cade Cust crashed over three minutes later.

Those 16 points in 11 minutes stunned Saints, still reeling from last month's exit of Paul Rowley after less than a year as head coach.

Despite a first away victory on Saints' territory since August 2017, Hull stay 13th although they are now level on points with Bradford Bulls.

St Helens have never failed to reach the play-offs but they remain seventh with all teams above them to play in the coming days.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hull FC interim head coach Andy Last said it felt fantastic for his side to end their losing streak Hull FC interim head coach Andy Last said it felt fantastic for his side to end their losing streak

They led three times in the opening 40 minutes but conceded their advantage each time and were fortunate to be level at 14-14.

The game's first mistake after barely two minutes saw full-back Logan Moy's knock-on punished by winger Lewis Murphy, who finished in the corner.

FC were behind only five minutes as Zak Hardaker's pass sent in Barron for the first of his treble.

Hastings edged Saints in front again with an 18th-minute penalty for Tom Briscoe's high tackle.

Prop Herman Ese'ese had a second Hull try ruled out for a double movement while he and Barron were repelled in quick succession before the visitors' deservedly hit the front.

Stand-off Jake Arthur's double cut-out pass freed Lewis Martin to finish in the left corner to make it 10-8.

Barron was denied again by last-gasp cover tackling and it was against the run of play when Jack Welsby raced 30 metres to touch down.

With 37 seconds remaining Saints captain Hastings dropped out. Thirty four seconds later Barron seized on Aidan Sezer's angled kick to cross again, waiting anxiously before video referee Chris Kendall overturned Liam Rush's on-field decision of 'no try'.

Tries for Barron and Cust, both converted by Hardaker, virtually put the contest out of reach.

By the time Harry Robertson scored a consolation try, Hardaker's 70th-minute penalty sealed the deal for Hull FC, who finished off with a further try from ex-Saint James Bell.

Jenna Foubister of Wigan celebrates their victory over St Helens

In the Women's Super League, Wigan Warriors saw off rivals St Helens 44-6 in the first match of the new Super Four format.

The defending champions outclassed St Helens with Ellise Derbyshire and Eva Hunter scoring a brace with further scores from Anna Davies, Molly Jones, Remi Wilton, Jenna Foubister and Mary Coleman at the BrewDog Stadium.

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

Sports.title: Fiery finish and record crowd as MI London condemn Spirit to elimination
Sports.content:
A Sikandar Raza masterclass inspired MI London to come away with the spoils to jump up to second in the table and condemn London Spirit to an early departure from The Hundred.

Nothing less than a win would do for Spirit in the local derby and after their mauling at the hands of SunRisers Leeds on Tuesday, they made three changes but still came up short in front of a record group stage crowd of 27,721 at Lord's.

MI London called on Raza to replace their star leg-spinner Rashid Khan, who was away on international duty with Afghanistan. The Zimbabwean all-rounder played his part in a disciplined bowling display, with the visitors expertly keeping the ball away from the shorter boundary side. As a result, Spirit's innings struggled to gather momentum, flickering rather than igniting despite a composed half-century from Lhuan-Dre Pretorius.
