The South African's innings was ended by an outrageous boundary catch from Will Jacks, who overbalanced on the edge, threw the ball up and then dived full length to complete the dismissal one-handed.

Raza said: "Four days ago I was in Sri Lanka and I'm not really sure what day or date it is but it's nice to be part of The Hundred and have a debut like that. I couldn't have asked for a better start - really I just closed my eyes and swung as hard as I could!

"It was nice to get a few out of the middle and you need to remember the complexion of a game can completely change in 10 balls."

David Willey bristled and muscled his way to 31 but the earlier dismissals of power-hitters Liam Livingstone and Dewald Brevis meant that Spirit were always struggling to post the kind of score they would have liked.

Only the late resistance of Jamie Overton and James Coles prevented Spirit from falling short of a competitive total, with Coles producing his first innings of real substance for the side. Their aggressive hitting in the closing stages lifted Spirit to a serviceable 160-5, leaving MI London needing to complete the highest successful run chase in The Hundred men's competition at Lord's to secure victory.

Matt Fisher, earlier in the day picked in England's Test squad, saw his first ever ball for Spirit disappear back over his head for six from the bat of Jacks but he had his Surrey team-mate's wicket next ball, Adam Milne pouching the skier.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tom Curran appeared to clash with a few former England team-mates after hitting the match winning runs for MI London

Nicholas Pooran, making his first appearance at Lord's, wasted little time finding his rhythm, but Mason Crane - brought in for Adam Zampa - delivered a superb opening spell. The leg-spinner dismissed former skipper James Vince with his very first ball and conceded just three runs from his first ten deliveries.

Pooran and captain Sam Curran began to accelerate the chase, but in an increasingly heated contest, Willey provided a moment of brilliance, completing a stunning run-out after releasing the ball mid-air while diving. The dismissal of the Trinidadian, however, only brought Zimbabwean all-rounder Raza to the crease and handed MI London a dangerous left-right combination.

Raza wasted no time making an impact, launching his first, fourth and seventh deliveries for six as he transformed the chase. His explosive 41-run stand with Curran, coming from just 18 balls, left MI London needing 29 from the final 20 deliveries.

The momentum shifted again when Curran picked out deep point off Overton for 33 and Sherfane Rutherford fell for a golden duck. But James Coles then conceded 18 from his only five balls, including a colossal 105-metre six from Raza that nearly cleared the ground. Although Raza departed with 10 balls remaining, Ollie Pope calmly finished the job to seal victory.

The two London sides exchanged words as they left the field after a fiery and occasionally fractious encounter. For Spirit, however, the defeat ended their hopes of progressing further in the competition.

Sports.title: Kerr and Matthews help MI London women to belated first win of season
Sports.content:
Melie Kerr's defiant half-century and decisive death bowling from Hayley Matthews helped MI London to a belated first win of the season against capital rivals London Spirit.

Previously winless MI London somehow recovered from the depths of both 23-5 and 64-8 to defend 122 and win by three runs.

New Zealand superstar Kerr single-handedly dragged her side to their defendable total with a brilliant unbeaten 69, and Spirit fell short, despite taking it to the last ball.

Image: Alexa Stonehouse of MI London celebrates with her teammates (ECB Images)

Kerr said: "It was pleasing to get a win today and a great game for the crowd in the London derby, and really nice to be on the winning team! We showed a bit of maturity and mental toughness, the wicket was tricky and once we got past 100 everything was a bonus, so 120 was great."

Following Kerr's effort with the bat, the MI London bowling attack scrapped for every wicket, with Spirit's batters unable to break the shackles and when the South African pair of Marizanne Kapp and Nadine de Klerk went late on, the game was up despite a couple of late Deandra Dottin boundaries.

Spirit, who have lost six in a row at HQ, lost the chance to move up the table, MI London joining them on six points with this thriller coming after an equally exhilarating tie in the reverse fixture at the Kia Oval.

Spirit's attack made early inroads after they won the toss, restricting the visitors despite Kerr's brilliance, which was largely responsible for 55 runs coming in the last 25 balls.

Kapp and Katie George bowled 10 each up front, at which point the score was 14-2, but it was the introduction of Charlie Dean after 30 balls that derailed MI London. She also bowled 10 straight through, picking up 3-6.

Kerr and Chinelle Henry, who had saved MI London with a stand of 55 at the Kia Oval, counter-attacked before the West Indian pulled De Klerk straight to deep square.

Kerr stood firm, striking her first competition six in her 26th game in The Hundred, hitting a second to dent Dean's figures and then smiting her for two more for good measure, the fourth brilliantly deposited over cover.

Sports.title: The Vinicius Junior dream is over - so what do Arsenal do now?
Sports.content:
No Morgan Rogers, no Vinicius Junior - what do Arsenal do now in their bid to improve their forward line this summer?

The dream to sign Vinicius Junior from Real Madrid is over after the Brazilian signed a new contract, despite Arsenal's attempts to try and convince him to move to north London.

Arsenal's sporting director Andrea Berta works in a particular way where he lines up several deals per position, getting ducks in a row and then deciding on which player to go for. If one falls through, he moves to the next best deal.

Arsenal knew Vinicius Jr would have been a complicated signing to make - and insisted he was one of a number of attacking options for the Gunners this summer.

But with former No 1 target Rogers joining Chelsea for £117m, then Vinicius committing to Real - Arsenal's attacking transfer options are slimming down.

What do the Gunners do now as they bid to improve their chances of retaining the Premier League title?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jay Bothroyd looks at alternative options to Vinicius Jr Arsenal can't seal the signing of the Brazilian

Go for another winger

Arsenal have shown a clear desire to improve the left-wing area this summer.

Over the last few years, neither Leandro Trossard nor Gabriel Martinelli managed to nail down that position and while the former ended the season as a key first-choice player, the fact he was sold to Besiktas early in the window was pretty telling about how they felt about the 31-year-old.

Arsenal have signed Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge, but are still in need of a top-quality winger - one very much in the Vinicius Junior mould - to really take that area of the pitch to the next level.

"We need these kind of players," said left-back Riccardo Calafiori this week about the importance of Arsenal signing genuine top-level talent. Mikel Arteta said top signings are needed to "attack every title" this season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Riccardo Calafiori speaks on Arsenal being linked with Vinicius Jr and why the club needs players like him to push on for another Premier League title

Arsenal have shown an interest in Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola, who has two years left on his contract with the French and European champions - and is showing no signs of wanting to sign a new one.

However, Barcola is valued at £145m by PSG and the price tag may prove to be an issue. Yes, Arsenal would have probably paid around that amount for Vinicius Jr, but the Gunners have been very clear they will not overspend on a player, not a position.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Dharmesh Sheth suggests Arsenal might now target PSG's Bradley Barcola after Vinicius Junior opted to remain at Real Madrid beyond this summer

For example, they valued Villa's Rogers at a certain price but when Chelsea arrived with a £117m offer, they chose not to match that as it was too high, even though he was the club's No 1 target.

A move for Barcola could come down to whether Arsenal and sporting director Berta feel PSG's valuation is right for the Premier League champions.

Liverpool have also shown an interest in Barcola and the opportunity to move to Anfield is said to appeal to the player.

Arsenal also held an interest in RB Leipzig winger Yan Diomande, but he has joined Vinicius Jr at Real Madrid in a £120m deal.

Stick with what they've got

Arsenal may decide that the left-wing area is lacking in top-class options, now Rogers and Vinicius Jr are unavailable. They may just stick with what they've got.

Do Arsenal go for a player like Marcus Rashford or Rafael Leao, who have both been strongly linked with moves away from Manchester United and AC Milan respectively? Both of those players are being branded as the next-best options in the market right now - yet both would represent big risks.

All throughout his Arsenal career, Mikel Arteta has been very insistent that the Gunners should only sign genuine quality, rather than just someone to make up the numbers. If Berta's next left-wing target are third or fourth-choice options behind Rogers and Vinicius, are they really worth going for?

New signing Tzolis is very highly-rated in the Arsenal camp. "I think you're going to love the player. A player who is very direct, he's got the goal between the eyes," said Arteta after he got off to a goalscoring start against Girona.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive Arsenal's 4-1 win over Spanish side Girona in their latest pre-season friendly

If Tzolis gets anything close to the 51 goal contributions in 52 games last season for Club Brugge then that patience could pay off for Arsenal. But it is a risk, given the Belgian Pro League is rated by Opta as the eighth-best league in the world, one spot behind the EFL Championship.

Then there is also the case of Martinelli, whose future sits in limbo with one year left on his Arsenal contract.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking from Arsenal's trophy parade, Gabriel Martinelli says there are 'no words to describe this moment' Watch the Champions Live From N5 parade live on Arsenal club channels.

The Brazilian got just one Premier League goal last season for Arsenal, albeit an important one against Manchester City. While he fared better in the Champions League with six strikes, the fact Arsenal are not rushing to give the 25-year-old a new deal before it expires shows they are willing to entertain his departure this summer.

Yet while Martinelli could easily be sold this summer, he does have experience of guiding Arsenal to a Premier League title - something the current left-wing market may not be able to provide right now.

It may not go down well with Arsenal fans, but Martinelli might be worth keeping for now.

Target other positions

Of course, Arsenal could improve their attack this season without improving the left wing.

The Gunners hold a strong interest in Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez, who wants to leave the LaLiga club.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Diego Simeone admitted in April that Arsenal were interested in Julian Alvarez

Signing Alvarez could result in Gabriel Jesus' Arsenal departure - and having three No 9 options in the Argentine, Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres is a formidable trio.

However, the issue with Alvarez is that he wants to join Barcelona. There is currently a stalemate as Atletico Madrid do not want to sell him to Barcelona, and would rather let him go to a club outside of Spain if he is to leave.

Arsenal need to convince Alvarez that north London is the right move for him, away from his dream destination.

Arsenal also hold an interest in Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi, but not only have the Cherries issued a 'not for sale' sign on the Frenchman this summer, he is also out for three to fourth months with injury, so would not be of great use to the Gunners right now.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at every Premier League goal scored by Bournemouth's Eli Junior Kroupi

Arsenal could also use the money they would have spent on Vinicius and Rogers to improve their defence, with William Saliba out for an extended period due to a back injury.

The Gunners have been interested in a move for Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa, who is valued at around £60m.

While Arsenal have missed out on a blockbuster signing in Vinicius Jr, the Premier League champions still have improved on their squad. They have replaced Christian Norgaard with a clear upgrade in Bruno Guimaraes, while Tzolis represents a younger - and possibly a more promising - version of Trossard.

But will the Gunners strike again in the transfer market at the top end of the pitch, to strengthen their title defence chances even further?

Sports.title: Uefa maintains World Cup boycott still stands despite Fifa’s backing for Infantino
Sports.content:
Uefa has doubled down on its threat to boycott Fifa-run competitions and reiterated its loss of confidence in Gianni Infantino’s presidency.

The latest damning intervention from European football’s governing body came as criticism of Infantino continued to rain in from several angles. The global players’ union, Fifpro, condemned “a profound abuse of presidential power” while the South American confederation, Conmebol, usually a strong Infantino ally, was moved to chastise “repeated unilateral actions taken without resorting to dialogue”.

It is Uefa’s continued stance, though, that may damage Infantino most severely. In a statement it said Fifa’s public backing of Infantino on Wednesday night “changes nothing” and explained it was not convinced repeats of the past nine days’ crisis will not occur.

Last week Uefa’s 55 member associations agreed to boycott Fifa tournaments if Infantino did not withdraw his privately funded Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme and, although the plan was scrapped last Friday, it said the terms necessary to avert the boycott have not been met.

“Uefa’s associations were very clear about the conditions attached to their non-participation in Fifa competitions,” it said. “First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn and, secondly, assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.

“These conditions have not been met. In addition, Uefa made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino’s presidency. That position holds. Yesterday’s announcement that some people employed by the Fifa president (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing.”

It heightens the turmoil enveloping football’s governance. If no accord is reached before the Under-20 Women’s World Cup, which begins in Poland on 5 September, that would be the first tournament subjected to a Uefa-led boycott.

Uefa remains hopeful it can exploit divisions within Fifa’s leadership despite the Infantino-led show of unity following Wednesday’s meeting of some of its management board in Rabat.

There were several notable absentees, however, and it is understood that Arsène Wenger declined an invitation to travel to Morocco in his capacity as Fifa’s chief of global development because of a desire to distance himself from Infantino. The former Arsenal manager had launched a scathing attack on the World Cup sell-off plans, saying it was “absolutely necessary and beyond question” that they were scrapped.

In contrast to Wenger, Fifa’s chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, who had described the proposals as “the project of one person”, was not invited to the summit in a development that will raise further questions over his future. Additionally Jill Ellis, the chief football officer, and Sarai Bareman, the chief women’s football officer, were not present in Rabat.

While Fifa has sent apologies to the Fifa council and member associations for their exclusion from the FFE process, it is believed that those sentiments failed to sway a large percentage of council members.

A handful of Uefa federations have withdrawn letters of support for Infantino’s re-election for a fourth term, although the early rush to make such declarations has slowed. The Football Association has now written to Fifa formally retracting its backing.

Uefa’s repeat of its boycott threat was followed by a scathing release from Fifpro. Before the World Cup Fifpro signalled its intention to work with Fifa by signing a memorandum of understanding but that has proved the briefest of truces.

Alongside the criticism, Fifpro wrote to Fifa making a series of demands, including giving players voting rights on the Fifa council, which is supposed to be the main decision-making body but has often been bypassed by Infantino.

“Fifa Forward Enterprise is gone, but the abuse of power that produced it is not,” Fifpro said. “Governance reforms, not a cover-up, are urgently needed. The withdrawal of FFE was inevitable. But withdrawing the proposal does not erase what it revealed.

“A plan capable of permanently altering the ownership and governance of the Fifa World Cup … was conceived in secrecy, negotiated behind closed doors and brought to the brink of agreement before the Fifa council, the member associations, players and football’s recognised stakeholders even knew it existed. That is not merely a governance failure. It is a profound abuse of presidential power.”

Conmebol, three of whose members are in line to host matches at the 2030 World Cup, had waited more than a week to comment publicly. While its disapproval was clear it stopped short of pushing for immediate change.

In a statement it said the Conmebol council “unanimously expresses its concern regarding the repeated unilateral actions taken without resorting to dialogue or to the institutional mechanisms established to address situations of this nature”.

While Uefa is leading efforts to unseat Infantino before Fifa’s election in March, Conmebol pointed out the timeline for the process has already been set. “Accordingly, Conmebol will not support any action or procedure that disregards or departs from those institutional mechanisms,” it said.

Earlier on Thursday the Jordan Football Association president, Prince Ali bin al-Hussein, said Fifa had paid bonuses owed from last December’s Arab Cup but clarified he would still oppose Infantino.

The money appears to have materialised after Prince Ali accused Fifa of “blackmail”, saying the governing body had threatened to withhold funds if Jordan refused to back Infantino’s re-election.

“Thank you to the Fifa administration for suddenly this morning delivering what was owed to our players and coaching staff, for the Jordan national team’s accession to the final of the Fifa Arab Cup in Qatar last December,” he wrote.

“This was funding that should have been received eight months ago … It is symptomatic of those exact difficulties that we all face, and that are usually linked to the Fifa presidential elections. And it does not change my clear position concerning the leadership of Fifa: my FA and I will not endorse president Infantino, nor will we vote for him.”

Meanwhile on Thursday, the executive committee of the African confederation (Caf) unanimously confirmed its support for Infantino. In a statement it said: “The CAF executive committee unanimously endorses the joint update by the Fifa president and secretary general on the FFE and will continue to focus on making African Football amongst the best in the world and adhering to governance and transparency global best practices.”

Sports.title: Arsenal hopes dashed after Vinícius Júnior extends Real Madrid contract to 2032
Sports.content:
Vinícius Júnior has ended summer speculation over his future by agreeing a new six-year contract with Real Madrid. Arsenal had been heavily linked with a move for the Brazil international, who had entered the final 12 months of his deal at the Bernabéu.

A tumultuous 2025-26 campaign in which Real failed to win a trophy and initial uncertainty after the arrival of José Mourinho in Madrid alerted the Premier League champions, but Vinícius has now committed his long-term future to the Spanish club.

“Real Madrid and Vinícius Júnior have agreed on the extension of our player’s contract, which links him to the club until 30 June 2032,” a club statement read.

“Vinícius Júnior joined Real Madrid in July 2018 at the age of 18. In his eight seasons wearing our jersey, he has played 375 matches, scored 128 goals, and won 14 titles: two Champions Leagues, three Club World Cups, two Uefa Super Cups, three La Liga titles, one Copa del Rey, and three Spanish Super Cups.

“His contribution to all these titles has been pivotal due to his gameplay, assists, and goals.”

Vinícius wrote on Instagram: “Eight years at the Bernabéu are too few … six more years, and for ever!”

The 26-year-old had hinted at extending his association with Real during an in-house interview on Tuesday where he spoke about Mourinho wanting him to be “happy” and “joyful” after a difficult spell.

A shock last-16 World Cup exit in America with Brazil also added to a frustrating 12-month period for Vinícius, but with his future settled the former Flamengo prospect will aim to help Real get back to competing for major honours again under Mourinho.

Sports.title: One potential breakout star for each Premier League club this season
Sports.content:
Arsenal: Marli Salmon

Dowman is old news by now, so we’re going to look at someone four months older than him. Much like the fish of the same name, Salmon has risen quickly. The defender became the fourth-youngest player to represent Arsenal last season when he came off the bench against Club Brugge in the Champions League in December at the age of just 16 years and 102 days.

Salmon made four appearances for the first team last season, while also featuring 14 times for their Under-21s in Premier League 2. He won an impressive 71.8% of his duels in PL2 (56 of 78); of defenders to contest at least 50 duels, only two players had a better success rate. Salmon – who can play right-back or centre-back – has signed a pre-agreement to commit his future to the club when he turns 17 later this month, and it would not be surprising to see him given more opportunities by Mikel Arteta.

Aston Villa: Brian Madjo

Aston Villa signed Madjo from Metz in January for about £10.5m but were not able to register him. He is available now and has been involved regularly during pre-season. The giant 17-year-old centre-forward’s movement and power are reminiscent of Erling Haaland.

He has caught the eye in Villa’s recent friendlies, scoring four times. Pre-season only counts for so much, of course, but you can only score against what’s in front of you.

Bournemouth: Veljko Milosavljevic

After the departure of Marcos Senesi, Bournemouth have a position in the centre of defence up for grabs and Milosavljevic could be the man to claim it. Milosavljevic joined the club last summer from Red Star Belgrade. Although he didn’t feature prominently, making just seven appearances in all competitions, the 19-year-old is clearly a promising defender.

He made more clearances than any other Bournemouth player on his Premier League debut in September, before going on to make his full international debut for Serbia in October. Marco Rose may want more experience at centre-back, especially given how youthful some of Bournemouth’s other defenders are, but Milosavljevic will hope to take another step forward this season.

Brentford: Antoni Milambo

Milambo had a difficult introduction to English football last season. Signed from Feyenoord for around £21m last year, he suffered a season-ending ACL injury on international duty in October. He was obviously set back but will be confident he can force his way into Keith Andrews’ thinking this term.

He became Feyenoord’s youngest ever player in 2021, when he made his debut as a 16-year-old, but Milambo rose to prominence in 2024-25 as a forward-thinking, box-to-box midfielder who was technically good and could be a threat in attack. No other Eredivisie player under the age of 21 bettered his 14 goal involvements in all competitions that season. He could be a dynamic asset in the very useful midfield Andrews has built.

Brighton: Zadok Yohanna

Yohanna will need a little patience as he’s still quite raw but, if he is given opportunities at Brighton this season, he will catch the eye. The 19-year-old Nigerian has joined from AIK for around £21.5m, a record sale for Swedish football, despite playing just 13 league games for the club. It was enough to convince Brighton, who have been impressed by his direct style and fearless dribbling.

A left-footed winger who plays on the right side of the attack, Yohanna was attempting more dribbles per 90 minutes than any other player in the Allsvenskan this year before his move was confirmed in June. He also tallied the most take-ons driving into the box (six), take-ons in the box (15) and the joint-most take-ons followed by a shot (three), despite playing significantly fewer minutes than many other players. His end product needs work, but he will get bums off seats.

Chelsea: Reggie Watson

Chelsea always have a conveyor belt of young talent waiting for a chance – the issue is many seem to get lost in the crowd. But, after losing Rio Ngumoha to Liverpool a couple of years ago, the club have apparently made a greater effort to keep hold of emerging homegrown talents, and one of those they were especially keen to tie down was Reggie Watson.

A towering defensive midfielder, Watson, 16, has impressive physical attributes but is also tidy on the ball, appears to have good spatial awareness and plays with considerable personality for one so young. It’s easy to see why he’s been tentatively compared with Rodri.

Xabi Alonso has also spoken about being “really impressed” with his impact in pre-season. Given the uncertainty around other midfielders – such as the fitness issues of Roméo Lavia and Dário Essugo – Watson could get minutes this season.

Coventry City: Kai Andrews

With survival being the name of the game for Coventry City season, giving minutes to young players may not be Frank Lampard’s top priority. There is one youngster who could force his way into Lampard’s plans, though: Andrews. The 19-year-old midfielder made 10 appearances for Coventry last season before joining Hibernian on loan.

While Andrews failed to make his mark in Scotland, he ended the campaign on a high as he made his first start for Wales in a friendly against Romania. He acquitted himself well in the match, making nine passes in the final third, the third most of any player, and winning two fouls. Andrews will need to decide whether to stay at Coventry and fight for a place or go out on loan for regular minutes.

Crystal Palace: Joél Drakes-Thomas

Drakes-Thomas became Crystal Palace’s youngest Premier League player last season and will hope to play a more prominent role this campaign. The wideman made his Palace debut in the Conference League when he was just 16 years old and he shone against Finnish side KuPS. He attempted seven crosses during the match, the most of any player, and he created two chances, the joint-most. The appointment of Pierre Sage has signalled the start of a new era at Selhurst Park, and Drakes-Thomas has the ability to be a figurehead of any future success.

Everton: Tyrique George

George looked promising at Chelsea, but his first few months at Everton after initially joining on loan in February were something of a settling-in period, as he started just one game for David Moyes’ side. With a full pre-season under his belt, George could burst into life this season.

Quick, dynamic and eager to run at full-backs, the 20-year-old could be the one to benefit most from Jack Grealish returning to Manchester City after his loan. George has started three of Everton’s four pre-season friendlies in the absence of Iliman Ndiaye, who is reportedly the subject of interest from abroad. With Grealish gone and Dwight McNeil dropping down the pecking order, George has a big opportunity.

Fulham: Farhaan Ali-Wahid

The 19-year-old will be hoping to make his debut for Fulham this season, having already impressed for their Under-21s. He signed his first professional contract with the club last summer and went on to score 10 goals in PL2. The left winger also added seven assists, proving he can create as well as find the net himself.

Only Chelsea’s Shumaira Mheuka (19) and Liverpool’s Kieran Morrison (18) recorded more goal involvements than Ali-Wahid (17) in the PL2 last season, while just 10 players created more chances from open play than his 26. He was nominated for the PL2 Player of the Season award and the new Fulham manager, Álvaro Arbeloa, has been picking him in pre-season.

Hull City: Charlie Hughes

Hughes was Hull’s defensive lynchpin last season. The 22-year-old centre-back started 36 games in the Championship and played every minute of their successful playoff campaign. He has a remarkable willingness to put his body on the line. Last season, he made 1.54 blocks per 90 minutes, the most of any regular player in the Championship. He also made more clearances per 90 minutes (7.62) than any of his teammates (1,000+ mins). Hull may struggle in the Premier League, but Hughes could be a diamond in the rough.

Ipswich Town: Tudor Mendel-Idowu

Mendel-Idowu, who spent most of his youth development at Chelsea before a year at Anderlecht, was snapped up by Ipswich in the summer of 2024, though he is yet to make his first-team debut. The winger is an intelligent fellow; he appeared on a TV show called Child Genius when he was eight years old and went on to become a King’s Scholar at Eton College.

He has not only thrived in academia, but also on the pitch. He recorded 15 goal involvements in 17 PL2 games for the Ipswich’s Under-21s last season (nine goals, six assists); only three players managed more in the league. On top of that, only three players created more chances from open play than his 33, and just two won possession in the final third more than him (21).

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Leeds United: Jayden Lienou

Chances were at a premium last season for young players under Daniel Farke. The youngest player to play for Leeds was 21-year-old Facundo Buonanotte, who had already made his debut for Argentina, and even he only played a fleeting role in the second half of the season.

But Lienou may just be winning Farke’s trust. The 18-year-old defender started all but one of Leeds’ PL2 games last season and won possession 5.4 times per 90 minutes, the second most in the side. He was the only youth-team player to feature in Leeds’ first three pre-season games, and he was called into the senior Wales squad by Craig Bellamy in June, showing he is impressing coaches for both club and country.

Liverpool: Trey Nyoni

With a new manager comes a new opportunity to impress, and Trey Nyoni has taken that chance in pre-season. The midfielder had to be patient after joining Liverpool from Leicester in 2023. Arne Slot gave him limited minutes last season, with Nyoni making 14 appearances in all competitions, only two of which were starts, both in the League Cup. With Andoni Iraola now in the dugout, the 19-year-old has been able to stake his claim and has been Liverpool’s standout midfielder in pre-season.

One of the most impressive aspects to his game is his verticality. Nyoni wants to get the ball forward as often as possible, though he’s not careless in possession. In his three friendlies this summer in the US – against Sunderland, Wrexham and Leeds United – Nyoni attempted 154 passes, completing 141 of them (92%). Just looking at forward passes, he completed an impressive 44 out of 54 (81%). With Curtis Jones potentially leaving, and most of Liverpool’s transfer funds seemingly going on attackers, the path may open up for Nyoni.

Manchester City: Ryan McAidoo

McAidoo has shone in City’s extremely competitive academy. The winger impressed in the PL2 last season, with only Reigan Heskey (15) registering more goal involvements than him (12) for City. McAidoo made his first-team debut last season, and he marked the occasion by scoring the ninth goal in City’s 10-1 drubbing of Exeter City in the FA Cup.

More recently, the 18-year-old caught the eye with his one-v-one ability in City’s pre-season friendly against Inter. He also had the second-most touches in the opposition’s box (13). Enzo Maresca raved about McAidoo’s performance, calling him “the type of winger I love”.

Manchester United: JJ Gabriel

Gabriel is undoubtedly the biggest hope in Manchester United’s academy. He apparently nearly left at the end of the 2024-25 season until senior club figures stepped in and his reputation has only continued to grow since. Then, aged 14, he had already become the youngest player to represent United’s Under-18s, scoring twice on his debut. After turning 15 in October, he was soon involved in first-team training.

Nevertheless, his focus remained the Under-18s, for whom he scored 23 goals – a tally bettered by only one player – in the 2025-26 U18 Premier League campaign, winning the competition’s Player of the Season award.

A skilful attacker who can play out wide or through the middle, Gabriel is brave, expressive and confident. He showed these traits when he came on as a late substitute in United’s pre-season friendly against Atlético Madrid at the weekend.

The record for youngest Premier League player is out of reach, but Gabriel has a good chance of becoming United’s youngest player in the Premier League; that honour currently belongs to Angel Gomes (16 years, 263 days).

Newcastle United: Park Seung-soo

For all the good he did at Newcastle, some supporters think Eddie Howe could have done more to bring young talent through. Now he’s gone and Newcastle are in a transition period, several of their young players will fancy their chances of stepping up. Park, 19, is one of them. The South Korean left-winger was signed last summer and spent the season adapting to English football in PL2. He averaged 4.7 dribble attempts per 90 minutes in that competition and caught the eye with his energetic displays and tidy footwork.

With Anthony Gordon gone, there may well be chances available on the left flank, especially if new signing Bazoumana Touré does not get off to a flying start. Park has impressed in pre-season and a step up to top-flight football might not be far down the line.

Nottingham Forest: Kalum Thompson

Thompson signed for Nottingham Forest from Northern Irish club Linfield last July and, despite being 16 at the time, he went on to spend the majority of 2025-26 playing for the club’s Under-21s. The left winger was the youngest player to feature for Forest Under-21s last season and yet only four players – three of whom are now 20 – tallied more minutes than him (1,090).

The 17-year-old won the club’s scholar of the year prize at the end of the season. A tricky and purposeful player, Thompson’s 4.7 dribble attempts per 90 ranked highly in the PL2 and his six goal involvements were the most of any Forest player.

Sunderland: Nilson Angulo

Although Angulo reportedly cost £15m in January and is already 23 years old, he just about fits into the potential breakout player category. After joining from Anderlecht, Angulo’s impact at Sunderland wasn’t exactly explosive. There were flashes of his flair but he was clearly still pretty raw.

Nevertheless, those first few months gave him time to adapt and, after a fairly encouraging World Cup with Ecuador, he’ll now hope to kick on. He has the ability and he has an athletic build which should help him once his game has been refined a little more.

Sunderland will hope the Angulo of Anderlecht comes to the fore a little more this season. Prior to his move last season, he’d attempted more dribbles (111) than any other player in the Belgian Pro League, while only Christos Tzolis (17) – now at Arsenal – bettered his 11 goal involvements. If he keeps progressing, Angulo will be a very useful weapon for Régis Le Bris.

Tottenham: Lucá Williams-Barnett

Spurs seem to have exciting young talents breaking through every other season, and now it’s Williams-Barnett’s turn to see if he can make his mark. Williams-Barnett started last season playing Under-18s football but quickly broke into first-team contention. He made one senior appearance but featured on the bench semi-regularly throughout the campaign.

He was one of Spurs’ standout players in the PL2 despite only playing 10 games. Williams-Barnett recorded an astounding 1.25 combined goals and assists per 90 in the PL2, ranking him fourth among all players (500+ mins). The 17-year-old attacking midfielder also created 0.8 big chances per 90 last season, again ranking him fourth (500+ mins). He has featured heavily in pre-season, building great momentum which he can hopefully take into the season.

Sports.title: Top Ugandan footballer killed by robbers armed with paving stones
Sports.content:
The Ugandan football community is in mourning after the death of a player who was fatally injured during a robbery in the capital, Kampala, on Tuesday night.

David Owori, who captained Sports Club Villa, a Uganda Premier League club, and represented the national team, was attacked after resisting an attempt to steal his mobile phone and other belongings near his home in Makindye division.

Racheal Kawala, a spokesperson for the Kampala Metropolitan police, said he was found unconscious by ​passersby, who took him to a nearby hospital. He was ​transferred to another hospital, where he was pronounced dead on Wednesday.

Witnesses said attackers hit the footballer with paving stones before robbing him and fleeing, leaving him unconscious, the BBC reported.

Owori, 27, was a right-back and midfielder for SC Villa. He helped the team win a record 17th Uganda Premier League title in 2024.

He started his senior career in 2016 at the Uganda Premier League side Vipers Sports Club and had stints in Europe with Vélez CF in Spain and Utsiktens BK in Sweden.

He played for the national team in the qualifiers for the 2021 Africa Cup of Nations.

SC Villa said: “It is with profound sorrow that we announce the untimely passing of our captain, Owori, who had been receiving treatment at Case Clinic following an attack by suspected thugs. Our deepest condolences and prayers are with his family.”

The Federation ​of Uganda Football Associations said: “David was not just a footballer. He was ​both a leader and an inspiration to a generation. As ​Captain of SC Villa, he led with courage, humility and passion. In the Uganda Cranes jersey, he carried the hopes of a nation.”

It added: “We have lost a son, a leader and a star. His light on and off the pitch will never be forgotten.”

The Ugandan parliament observed a minute of silence in Owori’s honour on Wednesday.

In June Sydney Gongodyo, a Ugandan rugby international, ​died after a mob attacked him in Kampala, mistaking him for a thief, police said.

Uganda’s National Council of Sports said: “Sadly, ​Ugandan sport has been hit with many such ​tragedies lately, and we hope for justice and a lasting solution.”

Sports.title: Kerolin failed to report for pre-season at Manchester City before Barcelona switch
Sports.content:
The Brazil forward Kerolin failed to report back for pre-season training at Manchester City in July before her transfer to Barcelona had been agreed.

Barcelona announced their signing of the 26-year-old on Tuesday but it was not until Thursday evening when Manchester City first made any reference to the transfer, eventually confirming they had received a WSL record fee for a sale more than 48 hours later.

Several staff and players at Manchester City were disappointed at what were perceived to be efforts by Kerolin to force a transfer to Barcelona and that her time at the club ended on a surprisingly sour note. She did not join pre-season with the Women’s Super League champions, which began in late July, despite previously having been felt to have been on good terms with the squad.

The deal, worth an initial €1.2m (£1m), represents the largest transfer fee received by a WSL club, and it could rise with add-ons to approximately £1.25m, although this has not been officially confirmed. It is one of the largest transfer fees in women’s football.

City said of Kerolin: “She grabbed 14 goals and six assists during that time, helping City to a WSL and FA Cup double in her solitary full season in England. And upon her transfer to Barça, City have received a WSL-club record transfer fee of €1.2m.

“Everyone at Manchester City would like to thank Kerolin for all her efforts at the club and wish her the very best in her future career.”

Kerolin was part of the City side that lifted their first WSL title in a decade last season and also helped them win the Women’s FA Cup. But within weeks of those celebrations many of her City colleagues have been stunned after she did not say goodbye in-person. Kerolin’s representatives have been contacted for a response.

High-profile examples of such transfer standoffs have been seen in men’s football, but incidents in the women’s game have been comparatively rare.

City have no objections to the transfer in principle but sources have said the team were taken aback by the former North Carolina Courage star’s absence from pre-season fitness testing. For Kerolin, it is a dream move to the European champions, who beat OL Lyonnes in last season’s Women’s Champions League final.

City and Barcelona will meet in a friendly at the Joie Stadium on 15 August as the reigning champions of England and Spain step up their pre-season preparations.

Sports.title: Barcelona step up Rodri interest after Real Madrid talks with Manchester City star stall
Sports.content:
Barcelona have stepped up their attempts to hijack Real Madrid’s move to sign Rodri from Manchester City.

While City have not given up hope that Spain’s World Cup-winning captain will sign a new contract after he entered the final year of his deal, they are thought to be willing to allow him to leave for about £60m. Despite weeks of talks with Rodri and his representatives, Real have yet to reach an agreement and Barcelona are hoping to take advantage.

It is understood that Rodri spoke to their manager, Hansi Flick, and sporting director, Deco, about a potential move on Wednesday and indicated he is keen to return to Spain. Barça, who will be without midfielder Frenkie de Jong for several months after the Netherlands midfielder sustained a knee injury, are now expected to make contact with City to negotiate the structure of the fee for the 30-year-old, who won the Golden Ball for the World Cup’s best player.

Real, who have signed RB Leipzig’s Yan Diomande for a club record fee of £115m, have also agreed a lucrative six-year contract extension with Vinícius Júnior to ward off interest from Arsenal. They may have to offload players first if they are to sign Rodri as well. Aurélien Tchouaméni and Eduardo Camavinga are possible departures, with Manchester United having been linked with the France midfielders.

Rodri has had minor surgery on his back and will miss most of City’s pre-season programme. They have signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m and remain in negotiations with Lille over a deal for the 18-year-old Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Meanwhile, Barcelona have been frustrated in their efforts to persuade Atlético Madrid to sell Julián Alvarez. After Robert Lewandowski’s departure, Barcelona have targeted Alvarez all summer, but Atlético continue to insist the Argentina striker is not for sale at any price.

Deco was in the Spanish capital to meet Alvarez’s representatives on Wednesday. All eyes will be on whether the 26-year-old former City forward will return to pre-season training on Monday or attempt to force through a transfer. Arsenal also retain an interest in him.

Ferran Torres – who scored the winning goal for Spain in the World Cup final against Argentina – has entered the final year of his contract at Barcelona and said he is waiting for them to begin talks over extending his deal. “All I know is that I have to be in training for Barcelona on 12 August. Let’s see what happens.” Asked what Barcelona needed to do to keep him, he said: “Show me they want me, come to negotiate.”

Meanwhile, James Trafford sealed a club-record move to Leeds after completing a medical at Elland Road. Leeds have agreed a £40m fee plus add-ons with City for the 23-year-old, who will become the world’s fourth most expensive goalkeeper.

Sports.title: Alessia Russo: ‘When you join the club, you take on a part of Arsenal and the love’
Sports.content:
Arms hooked over the bar at the front of the bus, sunglasses on, a drink in one hand and the other pointed towards the fans as she moved to the music and joined in with the singing and chanting, Alessia Russo was having a blast.

“I had the time of my life that day,” says the Arsenal forward of the 9km parade through the red smoke-filled streets of north London after Arsenal men’s Premier League triumph and Arsenal women’s Champions Cup success.

It has been a running joke among fans to refer to the 27-year-old as a “childhood Gooner”, which was turbo-charged when the shirt a very small Russo was wearing in a family photo with the FA Cup was changed from a Manchester United one into an Arsenal one.

While she was not a childhood Gooner, she is fast becoming an adult one.

“Since I’ve joined the club and seen the people around the place, it’s impossible to not become a part of Arsenal and to feel like I support Arsenal,” she says. “I want them to do well, I’m backing them every way, and the parade was just one of the most amazing things I’ve experienced. The fans, the atmosphere, celebrating the men winning the Prem, something they’d worked so hard for for so many years, I was just soaking it in, having fun and enjoying myself.

“It was just a really, really special day. It was nice to experience it with Lotte [Wubben-Moy] and Leah [Williamson] who are proper Gooners, but when you come to Arsenal you take on a part of it and start to understand and absorb their love for Arsenal. I definitely feel that and it’s nice to feel like you’re a part of something like that.

“You pick out moments where you win trophies as the main ones that stand out within your career, but that will definitely always stand out for me.”

There were people everywhere, on every balcony, rooftop, bollard and traffic light, of all ages, races and religions. Young boys, but also, in contrast to the Arsenal parades of the 90s and noughties, so many young girls. Cultivating and supporting that fresh generation interested in watching and playing the game is something Russo is passionate about.

View image in fullscreen Top: Arsenal go past fans with the Women’s Champions Cup trophy in May.

Photograph: Steven Paston/PA

Above: Fans celebrate Arsenal men’s and women’s success during the club’s victory parade.

Photograph: Aldo Ciarrocchi/Alamy

That is the reason she launched her own foundation this year and why she helped launch the fifth year of Starling Bank’s Kick On initiative. This partners local businesses with girls’ teams in need of sponsorship and subsidises the front-of-shirt sponsorship.

Starling commissioned surveys of 1,000 adult female players, 1,010 11-17 female players, 501 small- and medium-sized business leaders and 1,092 grassroots football coaches. Nearly every grassroots female football club (97%) said their team needed more funds, with opportunities for girls suffering as a result. The surveys found 76% of female players said they will have to drop out of their team or the sport altogether if more funding is not secured in the next five years, and 40% of female players said their team does not receive the same amount of funding as men’s teams.

“They are quite damning statistics, which is such a shame considering the growth we see in the women’s game,” says Russo. “Over the past five or six years, the growth has just been incredible, but there’s still work to do at the bottom to build it up.”

The risk is that women’s football loses momentum and fails to attract potential star players into the pathway. “I always say you never want to miss out on the next Leah Williamson or Lotte Wubben-Moy, you don’t want to miss out on talented young players just because they haven’t got a local team, or the team that they were at folds,” Russo says. “It seems like such an easy fix as teams don’t need much, but obviously it isn’t because it’s still a problem.

“I look back on all the people I met through my grassroots journey and every single one of them played a part in my career and I’m still friends with many of them. If local businesses can invest in one team, you never know, you might help produce a superstar who goes on to have an incredible career who will always remember you being a part of it.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Russo scored key goals in Champions League last season, including against Chelsea. Photograph: Harvey Murphy/News Images/Alamy

“There’s more to it than just investment, it’s that you can have a say in a core part of these young girls’ journeys and lives.”

With no major international women’s tournament, Russo has enjoyed a rare summer off and she has had the chance to focus on the broader issues she is passionate about, as well as some much-needed rest.

“It was important I did have some proper downtime,” she says. “Over the past few years, the minutes and tournaments have increased, so I needed to look after my body and get myself in a good place mentally. I shut down for about two and a half weeks and just enjoyed time with friends and family, which was lovely, but by the end of it I was ready to start exercising again, I didn’t know what to do with myself.

“I quite enjoy training on my own over the summer, you get to know your best routines and habits. I often go on holiday with my family and train out there, which is nice because everyone wants to get involved.

“I just took time for myself too, being a normal 27-year-old girl, going on holidays. I went to the England v Panama game in New York and got to be a fan and be around that buzz of the World Cup. I had Toonie’s [England teammate Ella Toone] hen do and wedding, which was amazing.”

View image in fullscreen After a few months off, Russo is back at Arsenal for pre-season training. Photograph: Alex Burstow/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

Russo had a standout year in 2025-26; many believe her game moved up a level for club and country. “I’m pleased with my season for Arsenal and England from a personal point of view, but, ultimately, I’ll always judge it on the trophies we win,” she says.

“We’ve learned a lot as a team over the past couple of years at Arsenal, but are hungry for the new season. We’ve made it quite clear we want to do everything we can to be the team most capable of winning the WSL and Renée [Slegers, the coach] has set the standard high this pre-season.

“We’ve got seven new players, we’ve got a squad that’s raring to go, the competition in it is high. I feel happy, but now I want to continue to push on with Arsenal and England and win some trophies.”

Sports.title: Mohamed Salah to earn upwards of £14.5m per season in two-year Trabzonspor deal
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah has signed a two-year deal with Trabzonspor and the Egypt forward will receive €17m (£14.5m) a season.

The ⁠announcement to ‌the Turkish stock ‌exchange came ​as Trabzonspor fans prepared to head to the club’s stadium for a ceremony to mark the 34-year-old’s former Liverpool player’s signing on a free transfer the day after ⁠Salah arrived in Istanbul in the team’s kit.

Thousands of supporters cheered in Trabzonspor’s stadium, waving club flags, holding torches and chanting songs.

At his signing ceremony, Salah said: “The last couple of days, it’s an experience I’ve ⁠never had in my life. I just want to thank every one of you ​for being here today. I am ‌feeling so much love ‌here I never expected that reception.

“I ‌am here to win, I want to win something with this club because you showed me so much love – I appreciate that.”

Salah will receive a 20% share from products sold ‌under his name, plus conditional bonuses each season.

View image in fullscreen Mohamed Salah takes photos of the scenes in the stands after his first taste of life as one of Papara Park’s own. Photograph: Ümit Bektaş/Reuters

Salah left Liverpool after nine years, having scored 257 goals in 442 appearances, winning the Premier League twice and the Champions League. His output waned last season and he was left ​on the bench in European games, leading to a public disagreement with Liverpool’s then manager Arne Slot.
