Sports.title: The task facing Mykhailo Mudryk after his 20-month ban: Rio Ferdinand hit the ground running for Man United, Paul Pogba's fitness woes and Diego Maradona's mixed spell in Spain after their lengthy suspensions
Sports.content:
Mykhailo Mudryk's long-awaited return to football came on Tuesday as Chelsea winger came on as a late substitute in their friendly against Juventus.

Mudryk's brief cameo – a 10-minute appearance – came after his doping ban came to an end this week after a resolution was reached with the Football Association.

The £89million signing had not played since November 2024, when he started and scored away at Heidenheim in the Conference League, after he had been suspended from football after failing a doping test for the banned substance meldonium.

Daily Mail Sport revealed this week that Chelsea have already been approached by clubs to ask about their plans for Mudryk this season.

Whatever outcome is reached, there is an understanding patience will be required with Mudryk having been out of the game for 20 months.

Here, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at previous examples of how other players have got on after returning to the game from long bans from football.

Mykhailo Mudryk made his return to football this week after his 20-month doping ban ended

Clubs are interested in a move for the Chelsea winger with an acceptance he will need time to return to his best after 20 months out of the game

Rio Ferdinand – Eight-month ban

The task facing Mudryk is outlined by Ferdinand's comments after returning from his doping ban in September 2004.

'Physically and mentally is was all new again, eight months out is a long time,' Ferdinand said after making his return.

Ferdinand had been hit with an eight-month ban from football and a £50,000 fine back in 2003. He had been sanctioned after failing to provide a drugs sample following a training session on September 23 that year.

His ban officially began in January 2004, starting days after he had been forced off injured during Man United's 1-0 defeat by Wolves.

Ferdinand, who failed in an appeal against his ban in March, was forced to watch from the sidelines as Man United suffered a dip in form in his absence and ultimately missed out on retaining their Premier League title. The ban also forced him to miss Euro 2004.

He ultimately made his return in September, with Sir Alex Ferguson throwing Ferdinand straight into the starting line-up as Man United hosted rivals Liverpool at Old Trafford.

Ferdinand required an energy bar to help him through the match, having not been able to play in friendlies to get him back up to speed.

Rio Ferdinand returned from an eight-month ban in September 2004 for Manchester United

Ferdinand played the full 90 minutes on his return as Man United earned a 2-1 win over Liverpool

Sir Alex Ferguson hailed Ferdinand's performance as 'superb' in their victory

Ferguson hailed his performance as 'superb' and highlighted how Ferdinand's composure had helped his side, as Man United earned a 2-1 win courtesy of two Mikel Silvestre goals.

'The fans were fantastic as soon as I came out for the warm-up and even after they were brilliant,' Ferdinand told Sky Sports post-match.

'It is just nice to get out there and play, you forget about everything that has gone on beforehand but once you get out there and start warming up and game starts, it is all about football.

'It was never going to be easy, I was under no illusions that I was going to have an easy game. It was nervous energy, I needed some sugar intake and the physio brought around a little bar to chew on. It was obvious needed, eight months is a long time.

'I am not looking back, I am looking forward and continue playing football now and do what I love doing.'

Having made a stuttering start to the season by winning of their opening five matches, Man United's form picked up after Ferdinand's return to action with the defender also immediately earning a recall to the England squad.

Ferdinand was close to being an ever-present for Man United after his return to action, missing just two league matches in the remainder of the campaign.

Eric Cantona – Eight-month ban

One of the most famous bans in football history was handed to Cantona after he kung-fu kicked a Crystal Palace supporter in January 1995.

The Frenchman had launched himself into the crowd having reacted to goading from one supporter, following his red card in the match.

Man United initially suspended Cantona until the end of the season, but the Football Association ultimately extended his ban for eight months.

Cantona returned in stunning fashion on October 1 as Man United faced Liverpool, with home fans at Old Trafford turning up to the clash with French flags adorning his face to mark his comeback.

Eric Cantona was famously banned for eight months after kung-fu kicking a Crystal Palace fan

Cantona scored and assisted in his return as Man United drew 2-2 with Liverpool in 1995

The Man United talisman made an instant impact by setting up Nicky Butt for the opening goal. With Man United having then fallen behind, Cantona then scored from the penalty spot to secure a 2-2 draw.

'It's Eric's stage, Eric's the lead actor and Eric delivers the best lines,' Man United forward Brian McClair reflected to Sky Sports.

'It was as if he'd never been away,' added Steve Bruce. 'It was quite incredible that somebody who had been away for so long could come back and have the impact he did straight away, and it lifted everybody.'

Cantona proved the inspiration for Man United to complete a league and FA Cup double. The Frenchman top scored with 19 goals in all competitions including netting against Liverpool in the FA Cup final, a match where he captained the Red Devils.

He was named as the Football Writers Association's Player of the Season.

Adrian Mutu – Seven-month ban

Mutu was part of the Roman Abramovich led revolution at Chelsea in 2003, with the Romanian among ten players the Blues splashed out on that summer.

The £15.8million signing scored ten goals in 36 matches during his debut season at the club after joining from Parma.

Mutu would ultimately fall out with his new manager Jose Mourinho at the start of the following season amid concerns over his lifestyle. Mutu then tested positive for cocaine use in September 2004 and was handed a seven-month ban from football.

Chelsea sacked the forward as a result with the Blues chasing £15.2million in compensation.

'Taking cocaine during my time at Chelsea was the worst decision I could have made in my career,' Mutu reflected in an interview last year.

'I was alone and sad, but neither depression nor anything else justified my actions. Zero tolerance – that was Chelsea's policy regarding drugs. And I think that's fair.

Adrian Mutu had been one of Chelsea's high-profile signings of the early Roman Abramovich era

Mutu was sacked by Chelsea after a positive test for cocaine, and the club then demanded he paid £15.2m in compensation

The Romanian forward spent a season at Juventus, before rebuilding his career at Fiorentina

'I made a mistake, strayed from the path, and paid the price for it. I was caught off guard. I wasn't used to that life. I was unprepared.

'I arrived at Chelsea during a turbulent time in my personal life, and I found myself caught up in too many excuses and lies. I was too young and too alone.

'I've reflected on that many times. I believe that for more than a season, I was amongst the best players in the world, so I could have won it easily. But bad decisions prevented me from doing so. I try not to beat myself up about it.'

Mutu was handed an almost immediate chance to return to the game with Juventus signing him in January 2005, despite his suspension running until May.

He scored seven goals in 32 league matches the following season as the Old Lady won Serie A – before later being stripped of their title.

Mutu moved on to Fiorentina in the summer of 2006 and spent five seasons at the club, scoring 54 goals in 112 league appearances. This led to Mutu being inducted into the club's Hall of Fame in 2024.

The forward had served a nine-month ban in 2010 after a failed doping test.

Paul Pogba – 18-month ban

Pogba's case represents an interesting comparison to Mudryk's owing to the similar length of time out of the game.

The French midfielder, like Mudryk, was initially facing a four-year ban from football with Pogba having tested positive for the prohibited substance DHEA in September 2023, when he was playing for Juventus.

His suspension was later reduced to 18 months following an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

Pogba told Daily Mail Sport in 2024 that he discovered news of his reduced ban while preparing for a film premiere, adding: 'We went through hell. A time of darkness. But this is my second chance, I have to use it.'

The former Man United star was emotional when he signed for Monaco last summer, describing his comeback as a second chance.

The World Cup winner, however, had already endured a series of injuries during his second spell at Juventus and Pogba's time on the sidelines during his ban also left him playing catch up.

Monaco had given Pogba his own fitness plan and planned to gradually introduce him into the team following his long absence.

Paul Pogba signed for Monaco last summer and viewed the move as a second chance after his 18 month doping ban ended

Pogba, however, spent much of the season on the sidelines amid a series of fitness issues

The 33-year-old managed just 115 minutes last season with Monaco considering his future

The 33-year-old ultimately played just 115 minutes for the Ligue 1 side last season as he struggled for fitness and form, with Monaco considering whether to part ways with him this summer.

Monaco CEO Thiago Scuro said last month: 'It is a complicated topic because we have a lot of respect for Paul, for the person he is. Since he arrived, he has been very positive.

'It is also true that, last year, the project didn't work well because when we started with him in the summer, the expectations were very different to what happened. I think that we have to be fair with him, follow his preparation every week, how he will progress physically and technically and then it will be the manager's decision.

'We have the summer to see what level we will see from Pogba. He could [leave at the end of the summer]. With Paul, it has always been a very open and transparent relationship.

'If, at some point, the expectations of the player are different to the expectations of the club, we will have to speak to find a solution. The performance will give all the answers that we need. Maybe he will stay, maybe he will leave.'

Diego Maradona – 15-month ban

The legendary Argentine was banned from football for 15 months back in 1991 after testing positive for cocaine.

The sanction effectively ended his historic spell at Napoli, who he had inspired to win two league titles, the Copa Italia and UEFA Cup.

Maradona looked to rebuild his career at Sevilla after his ban came to an end, as he joined forces with Carlos Bilardo, who had been Argentine's coach for their 1986 World Cup triumph.

His arrival proved lucrative for Sevilla with the club holding marquee friendlies during pre-season, with the club said to have enjoyed a £2.5million uptick in revenues during his sole year at the club.

Diego Maradona spent a season at Sevilla after serving a 15-month suspension from football

Maradona was initially seen as having a positive impact at the club, despite being overweight after the prolonged spell out of the game. Maradona, who was given the captain's armband after signing, helped the club into the top three of the LaLiga table early on.

The 32-year-old also produced an inspired performance in a 2-0 victory over Real Madrid.

His off-the-field problems, however, derailed Maradona during the second half of the season, leading to Sevilla hiring a detective to track him.

A falling out with Bilardo also contributed to Maradona spending just a single season at Sevilla, who finished seventh in the league, before he returned to Argentina.

Sports.title: Alleged scammer who 'targeted NFL players in million-dollar scheme' found dead in swimming pool at 24
Sports.content:
The alleged mastermind of a million-dollar scam targeting sports stars has reportedly been found dead in a swimming pool.

An investigation has been launched into the death of Mohamed Coulibaly, 24, after his body was discovered at a house in Harrison Township, New Jersey.

According to ABC, police officers visited the home after family members expressed concerns about Coulibaly.

Only last month, the 24-year-old from Philadelphia was named by Barron's as the organizer of an alleged scam that attempted to lure ex-NFL players and other athletes into buying a stake in 'bogus websites.'

According to Barron's, Coulibaly allegedly hoped to dupe the athletes into believing they were investing in successful businesses. Instead, three ex-NFL players claimed to have lost more than $1million combined.

Among those who allegedly fell victim to the scam was former New York Giants linebacker Tae Crowder. He reportedly invested his life savings - worth $500,000 - into one of Coulibaly's ventures.

The alleged mastermind of a scam targeting sports stars has reportedly been found dead in a swimming pool

Among those who allegedly fell victim to the scam was ex-New York Giants star Tae Crowder

'We were just, every day, talking about different investments and different things we could possibly get into. I saw him hanging out with a bunch of different guys that I know, which you know made me feel comfortable,' Crowder recalled, per ABC.

'I would log into the store all the time and just see how it would work and what was going on. I feel like the more I told him about that, as many times I kept logging in, the number started going up.'

But Crowder claims he never saw any return on his investment. 'I don't want anybody else to get involved in anything like this, and whoever has got involved, I just want to come together and make it right.'

According to Barron's, Coulibaly claimed investors had not received any money because he was still waiting for funds himself.

At the time of his death, ABC reports, no criminal charges had been filed related to the alleged scheme.

A GoFundMe page, purportedly created by Mohamed's brother, Badra, has raised nearly $13,000. The family is 'urgently working to bring him home so he can be laid to rest with dignity and peace.' Coulibaly previously told Barron's that he immigrated to the US as a child with his Malian family.

Sports.title: Rangers LOSE first leg of Europa League qualifier: Jagiellonia Bialystok earn shock win in Scottish club's latest European embarrassment - as star's attitude proves costly for Derek McInnes' men
Sports.content:
Six-foot four in his stocking soles, blessed with pace and physicality, there’s plenty which points towards Manny Fernandez being a top defender.

Unfortunately, from Rangers’ perspective, it’s becoming clear that there’s one key part of the jigsaw which is presently missing. His attitude.

At Tannadice last Friday, he didn’t look to have a care in the world when sauntering back up the field as Dundee United scored a goal which ultimately cost Derek McInnes’s side two points.

Any supporter who believed he’d have learned a harsh lesson on that opening night will have been forced to think again after another unconvincing display in Poland.

Twice in eight minutes, he got it all wrong again as McInnes saw a one-goal lead turn into a one-goal deficit and his side enter the danger zone in this Europa League qualifier.

The player’s attempt to readjust his feet and deal with a routine low cross was dismal. One can only imagine that the own goal he chalked up consequently was still running through his head when he slipped while trying to defend a cross from the other flank just before the Poles struck again.

Rangers players appear to be in shellshock as they see their lead very quickly turn into a deficit

To think that back in April the player was being linked with a potential move to Arsenal or West Ham...

At the weekend, former Ibrox midfielder Andy Halliday spoke of individuals presently at the club who didn’t seem to want to defend. He didn’t name names, but he didn’t have to.

At the age of 24, Fernandez doesn’t seem to have realised that showing the right commitment and mindset for 90-plus minutes are non-negotiable. McInnes already must be tired of telling him.

He was not alone in producing an error-strewn display. Having looked capable of being – in his words – ‘the man’ this season on Tayside, Thelo Aasgaard regressed to the player of last term. It was his cheap concession which allowed the Poles to claim the second.

Neither Dan Neil nor Tochi Chukwuani imposed themselves on the contest enough to merit a start in next week’s return leg.

The main positive for McInnes came in the shape of the display from the bench from Findlay Curtis. How the manager could have done with more of his charges showing the kind of courage the teenager exhibited.

The return of Nico Raskin at the break also elevated those around him. But an improved second half display will have come as little consolation to those supporters who made the long trip.

Kacper Szmyt celebrates after putting the home side ahead in the Europa League qualifier

The Poles were competent, yet no greater than that. With another league game against Hibs to come at the weekend, Rangers should have enough to turn the tie around. If they don’t, there will be severe recriminations.

There were only 1,027 Rangers fans inside the Chorten Arena in north-east Poland for what they’d hope to be the first of many foreign adventures this season.

Having made plain his concern over the way his side performed at Tannadice, McInnes shook things up with five changes. There was a debut for Daisuke Yokota following the winger’s move from Hannover. Ross McCrorie effectively replaced the injured Ben Godfrey, Neil and Chukwuani were brought into midfield with Youssef Chermiti tasked with leading the line.

There was a familiar face in Jagiellonia’s line-up. Yuki Kobayashi only managed a handful of appearances in his two years with Celtic, but his weak display in a 3-0 loss at Ibrox in a dead rubber three years ago pretty much sealed his exit. Yet the Japanese was terrific here.

McInnes had identified that the Poles set up with a narrow formation. The onus was on his wide players to manipulate the space on the flanks and ask questions. Inside four minutes, Tuur Rommens and Mohamed Diomande did exactly as he would have demanded.

It was a brilliant exchange between the pair to open the game up. Rommens fed the midfielder then bounded forward to receive an incisive pass. The Belgian’s cross had pace and direction and caught Guilherme Montoia in a state of panic. For reasons only he could explain, the Portuguese fired the ball into his own net.

Having won possession back, Chermiti threatened to find a second until Slawomir Abramowicz got a hand in the way of his strike. But the bright start from the Scots just did not last. They dropped off the game and made elementary errors.

Rangers new boy Yokota helps Rommens celebrate his role in the own-goal opener

Yokota didn’t do nearly enough to stop Kajetan Szmyt pulling the ball back onto his right foot and crossing. All that was required was some assertive defending. Instead, Fernandez had another moment to forget.

Stretching for the ball when he should have sent it back where it had come from, his studs steered it onto the target. Ivor Pandur could only watch on in horror as it crept inside his post. And with that, Rangers lost their shape.

Coming on 21 minutes, the Poles’ second was another horror show from McInnes point of view.

Maybe Aasgaard had read too much of the praise which has been since lavished on him post-Tannadice. An unnecessary flick in a promising position turned the ball over and the home side were on their way.

Down the right-side Nik Prelec went, his run and cross going unchecked. His cross demanded concentration from those in blue but Fernandez lost his footing at the key moment.

It allowed the ball to run through to Jesus Imaz. Pandur got an outstretched hand to the first effort but was a beaten man as Szmyt thumped home the rebound. This one belonged to him.

The hydration break gave McInnes a chance to exchange some words with his players. They wouldn’t have been complimentary.

Rangers manager Derek McInnes tries to get his message across during a hydration break

Another surge from the home side saw Fernandez fail to deal with the situation. This time, Rodrigo Conceicao smashed the ball into the side netting.

Notwithstanding an excellent tackle by Kobayashi to deny Chukwuani, it was all Jagiellonia until the break. Prelec’s deflected shot was beaten away by Pandur. The Croatian also stopped Norbert Wojtuszek’s strike.

Raskin, Cammy Devlin and Findlay Curtis were thrown on for Neil, Chukwuani and Yokota at the break. It became more encouraging.

Devlin’s tenacity on the hour mark presented Aasgaard with a chance to level. The Norwegian’s shot was wayward. Curtis was inches away from turning Raskin’s cross home before Devlin’s shot was tipped over.

For all that, a Rommens’s error led to Imaz steering a cross past the post.

Curtis was bright down the left, a string of crosses begging to be dispatched. McCrorie saw a shot deflected wide by Kobayashi after Curtis’s initial shot had been tipped away.

It wasn’t to be Curtis’s night, though. Deep in injury time, he saw a volley come straight off the post. He deserved more. Rangers did not.

JAGIELLONIA BIALYSTOK (4-3-3): Abramowicz 6.5; Wojtuszek 7, Konstantopoulos 7, KOBAYASHI 8, Guilherme 6.5; Rodrigo Conceicao 6 (Agbonifo 65), Romanczuk 7, Lozano 6.5 (Klynge 65); Szmyt 7, Prelec 7 (Sylla 80), Imaz 6.5 (Drachal 80). Booked: Kobayashi. Manager: Adrian Siemieniec 7.

RANGERS (4-2-3-1): Pandur 5.5; McCrorie 6 (Shankland 85), Sterling 6.5, Fernandez 4, Rommens 6; Chukwuani 5 (Devlin 45), Neil 5 (Raskin 45); Yokota 5 (Curtis 45), Aasgaard 5 (Dragojevic 76), Diomande 6; Chermiti 6. Booked: Rommens, Chukwuani, Raskin. Manager: Derek McInnes 5.

Sports.title: Leeds CONFIRM £45m signing of James Trafford from Man City: England international becomes most expensive British goalkeeper of all time in record deal
Sports.content:
Leeds CONFIRM £45m signing of James Trafford from Man City: England international becomes most expensive British goalkeeper of all time in record deal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Leeds United have confirmed the signing of James Trafford from Manchester City for £40million plus £5m in add-ons.

The England goalkeeper, who went to the World Cup with the Three Lions as third-choice shot stopper, is moving to Yorkshire in a bid for more game time.

Trafford was expecting to take the No 1 jersey when he signed for Pep Guardiola last summer but was sidelined when City seized an opportunity to bring in Gianluigi Donnarumma from Paris Saint Germain.

The 23-year-old ended up playing just four times under Guardiola in the Premier League, although he did feature in a further 13 cup games as they won the FA Cup and Carabao Cup.

Newcastle had spoken to City in recent weeks about Trafford and tried previously to sign him, but ended up exploring other options.

Trafford joined City last summer in a £27m move from Burnley, just two years after City sold him for £14m, and they have made a substantial profit.

Leeds have signed James Trafford from Man City in a record £45million transfer

The 23-year-old England star has become the most expensive British goalkeeper of all time

He is Leeds' third summer signing after the arrivals of Harry Wilson and Tarik Muharemovic and becomes the most expensive British goalkeeper of all time.

The previous highest amount paid was for Jordan Pickford's £30m transfer from Sunderland to Everton in 2017, and Kepa (£68m) and Alisson (£62m) are the only keepers to have commanded a higher fee.

Trafford is also a club record signing for Leeds, surpassing their £35.5m deal for Georginio Rutter in January 2023.

Speaking about his lack of gametime at the Etihad back in February, Trafford had opened up on the difficulties following his move.

'It was nice (to play), it wasn't what I expected coming into the season,' Trafford said after an FA Cup win over Salford City.

'I tried to guard against the situation happening but it's the reality and I know every time I play, I have to give it my best shot and try and win and try and improve.

'It's the current situation I'm in.'

In a separate interview, he added: 'It has obviously been very up and down throughout the season because I haven't played too much and obviously I had a decision to make in the summer.

'Everyone always thinks when you make decisions (for) the best possible outcome and obviously it hasn't been the best possible outcome, but I have just tried to improve every day, stay positive (and) happy. Throughout the year it has been such a big learning experience.'

Trafford, who has won two caps for England, replenishes a goalkeeping department at Elland Road that has lost Karl Darlow and Ilan Meslier this summer.

Sports.title: UEFA ramp up pressure on defiant Gianni Infantino and insist they WILL boycott the World Cup if he refuses to quit - after under-fire FIFA president vowed to fight on
Sports.content:
UEFA is set to continue its boycott the World Cup until Gianni Infantino is removed from his position, Daily Mail Sport understands.

European football’s governing body today issued a statement reiterating that it had lost confidence in the FIFA president in the wake of his aborted World Cup sell-off.

UEFA previously said that Infantino’s proposal would have to be withdrawn and that it would need assurances that such ‘attempts to disfigure the game this way will never be made again’ before it lifted its self-imposed ban.

However, it is believed that – as things stand - anything less than Infantino’s head would not be enough to ensure the likes of champions Spain, England, France and Germany take part in four years’ time.

An international football insider told Daily Mail Sport: ‘This had to be done. He has to go and this is the only way to force him out.’

On Wednesday night, FIFA announced Infantino had the backing of members of the body’s council after crisis talks in Morocco.

The beleaguered Swiss had summoned officials to his hotel as part of what appears to be, for now, a successful attempt to cling to power.

He had faced a major backlash since plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup emerged. But amid widespread outrage and opposition, those plans were dumped. Following the hotel summit FIFA issued a statement saying execs had given their 'full support' to Infantino while acknowledging 'mistakes' in the dropped plan.

UEFA repeated that it has lost confidence in FIFA president Gianni Infantino and reiterated its threat to boycott the World Cup

FIFA said they have now apologised in a letter to the various football associations and that a ‘review’ will be carried out.

Along with UEFA's continued anger, a withering statement from FIFPRO, the global union for professional footballers, hit out at Infantino and the FIFA Forward Enterprise scheme.

It read: 'FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) is gone. The abuse of power that produced it is not. Governance reforms, not a cover-up, are urgently needed.

'The withdrawal of FFE was inevitable. But withdrawing the proposal does not erase what it revealed.

'A plan capable of permanently altering the ownership and governance of the FIFA World Cup, and commercialising the competitions built by generations of players, was conceived in secrecy, negotiated behind closed doors and brought to the brink of agreement before the FIFA Council, the Member Associations, players and football’s recognised stakeholders even knew it existed.

'That is not merely a governance failure. It is a profound abuse of presidential power.'

They also ripped into FIFA's latest update from its meeting in Morocco and called for 'structural safeguards to ensure these events can never be repeated'.

This includes legally binding engagement 'with professional football's stakeholders on decisions of major consequence' and voting rights for them on the FIFA council.

The statement concluded: 'The withdrawal of FFE prevented an irreversible decision. It did not restore the confidence that made such a proposal possible in the first place.

'That confidence has now been fundamentally broken. It cannot be rebuilt through carefully drafted statements, internal reviews or promises to improve processes. Nor can it be restored simply by announcing governance and structural reforms that should always have existed.

'These reforms are now indispensable. But they are the responsibility of the future, not an absolution of the past.

'The players did not create this crisis. They will insist that football emerges from it with stronger institutions, stronger safeguards and leadership worthy of the trust the game demands.'

Infantino is facing mounting pressure over his failed plan to sell off stakes in the FIFA World Cup

Football legend Luis Figo became the latest high-profile individual to call for him to resign, while Arsene Wenger distanced himself from Infantino's plans

UEFA’s initial statement on Saturday had branded Infantino's proposal to flog commercial and event operations as a ‘shabby, back room, opaque deal’.

After Infantino’s apparent vote of confidence, they added: 'UEFA’s associations were very clear about the conditions attached to their non participation in FIFA competitions.

'First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn and secondly, assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.

'These conditions have not been met. In addition, UEFA made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino’s presidency. That position holds.

'Yesterday’s announcement that some people employed by the FIFA President (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing.'

The backing for Infantino from within came hours after Luis Figo became the latest high-profile name to call for Infantino’s head in a blistering attack in Daily Mail Sport.

Figo had described Infantino’s now-aborted plan to flog a stake in the World Cup to private investors as the ‘lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour I have ever witnessed’ and a ‘grubby, underhand plot’.

Figo, the former Barcelona and Real Madrid star, who initially backed Infantino in 2015, branded the Swiss a ‘relic who should have no part in football’s future’ and accused him of ‘a litany of abuses’.

Aside from the World Cup sell-off, he referenced the decision to suspend the ban for USA striker Folarin Balogun after his red card at the World Cup and the half-time show during the final which ‘broke the laws of the game’.

‘Infantino has debased the office of FIFA president he promised to elevate,’ he wrote.

‘He has lied, deceived and tried to feather his own nest at the expense of the game he is supposed to serve.’ Should he survive, Infantino would face re-election in March, and would need 106 votes from FIFA's 211 members to win another term in charge of the global game.

Meanwhile, Infantino did get some backing today, with the Confederation of African Football (CAF) reaffirming its support for the president.

Sports.title: Saffie Osborne heads to Shergar Cup believing big wins ‘prove career has not plateaued’
Sports.content:
Saffie Osborne heads to Shergar Cup believing big wins ‘prove career has not plateaued’

The 24-year-old will make her second appearance at Ascot’s Dubai Duty Free-sponsored team event as captain of the Britain and Ireland team

View 3 Images Saffie Osborne: team captain at the Shergar Cup (Image: Dave Benett)

Saffie Osborne hopes her 2026 successes have proved she is on a path towards a future challenge for the jockeys’ championship.

‌



The 24-year-old will captain a Britain & Ireland team of Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle, both former or present champions, at tomorrow’s Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup at Ascot.

‌



Osborne has climbed to seventh in the jockeys standings with 40 wins this season while her prize-money earnings exceed her 2024 best, thanks to high profile victories in the Weatherbys Super Sprint and Moet & Chandon International.

‌



“Anyone that starts off in this job, not wanting to be champion jockey, shouldn't be doing it because it's so tough and gruelling that if you're not aiming to be at the top, then I don't know why you're really doing it, to be honest,” she said.

Ffos Las race meeting moved to earlier start time to avoid effects of solar eclipse READ MORE :

“In 2024 I rode a large number of winners, but I lacked riding a top quality horse, which is starting to come now.

“Then last year I was just plagued with problems. I got injured twice and I had to cut my season short just as it started to get going again.

‌



“It just felt like nothing was kind of clicking into the right place and then in the back of your mind you're hoping you haven't plateaued or reached the level of where you're going to be. I think this year has proved that's not the case.”

View 3 Images Saffie Osborne: enjoying her best season in the saddle (Image: Dave Benett)

She went on: “It started brilliantly in May when I think I had 20 winners, and it's just gone from strength to strength since. My weight has been so good this year, and that's been a huge help. I've managed to ride so many good horses for really great connections.”

‌



Osborne has a formidable record at Ascot, where she rode two winners on her only previous Shergar Cup appearance, landed her first Group winner at the track and rode a treble on King George day to take her total haul at the course to 21.

“I have had a lot of luck there outside of the Royal meeting,” she said. “Maybe it’s because I’ve been going there since I was in a pram.”

The Shergar Cup features some of the best in the world with Frida Valle Skar and Marie Velon joining Lemaire for Europe, Jerry Chau and Luke Ferraris teaming up with Ho for Hong Kong and India’s Suraj Narredu and legend Yutake Take alongside Melham.

‌



View 3 Images Shergar Cup riders (r-l) Yutaka Take, Jamie Melham, Suraj Narredu, Christophe Lemaire, Luke Ferraris, Jerry Chau

Riders have been allocated rides by drawing lots for all six handicaps with points are awarded from 15 for winning, through 10, seven, five and three for fifth place, with Osborne’s best chance of a win from her five looking to be 7-4 shot Hoseki for William Haggas in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Classic.

As team skipper Osborne is looking to emulate Jamie Spencer as the last captain of Great Britain and Ireland to lift the trophy and competition stalwart Hayley Turner as the last female rider to pick up the top jockey award, even if she is understating her talents ahead of raceday.

Article continues below

“To have Ryan for the first time in 20 years and to have Dylan Browne McMonagle riding for us who was champion jockey last year and who is having an incredible season this year is amazing,” she said.

“Excluding me it is probably the strongest GB and Ireland team they have ever had.”

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua sets out demands to move Tyson Fury fight to New York
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua sets out demands to move Tyson Fury fight to New York

Joshua and Fury signed to fight in the UK but Netflix want the all-British showdown moved to Madison Square Garden in New York

View Image Anthony Joshua wants to fight in the UK

Anthony Joshua will demand a king's ransom to move his fight with Tyson Fury to New York.

‌



The British heavyweights signed contracts earlier this year to meet at home in the autumn. But Netflix, who will broadcast the fight, want it staged at a time suitable for a US audience. That would have meant the first bell ringing as late as 4am if the bout was held at Wembley.

‌



The fight organisers want to stage the showdown on November 20 - a Friday - at Madison Square Garden. Joshua, 36, admitted last month that his legacy would be damaged his biggest fight was shipped abroad. And his promoter Eddie Hearn insists they are not ready to give in.

‌



Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury winner offered world title shot READ MORE :

"I feel like me and AJ are the last two standing on a hill waving the Union Jack," he told talkSPORT. " Anthony Joshua made me insert a clause into the contract that said the fight must happen in the UK so at the moment it can't happen anywhere else. We are under a lot of pressure because it sounds like everyone has agreed they want to do the fight at Madison Square Garden, but we don't.

We want to make it so financially unviable to change the contract that they have no choice but to do it in the UK. I don't know how it's going to play out but we wouldn't have signed the contract under its terms if the fight was going to be in America, so why should we change it now?"

Article continues below

Fury's promoter Frank Warren, meanwhile, refused to be drawn on the fight's date or location. “That will be up to his Excellency (Turki Alalshikh) to announce when he is ready to announce it," he said. “No (deadline). The fighters will just need to get into training some time in September so that is what will happen in early September.

“They will be ticking over at the moment, I’m sure. I can only speak for Tyson but he is with his family. And then as soon as the date’s announced, he will get down to the serious and bring in sparring partners and prepare for the fight. I believe the fight will go on in November.”

Sports.title: Liverpool's firm stance on Djed Spence transfer as Reds battle defensive injury crisis
Sports.content:
Liverpool's firm stance on Djed Spence transfer as Reds battle defensive injury crisis

Andoni Iraola has been hit with a number of defensive injuries during his first pre-season as Liverpool boss, with Tottenham defender Djed Spence touted as a potential solution

View 3 Images England and Tottenham defender has been linked with a move to Liverpool (Image: Eston Parker/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Liverpool have no intention of pursuing a summer transfer move for Djed Spence, despite their recent injury woes.

‌



Spence, who shone for England at the World Cup, faces an uncertain Tottenham future as Roberto De Zerbi continues to overhaul his squad.

‌



Despite his brilliant performances for the Three Lions this summer, he is likely to find himself behind new signing Andy Robertson on the left and World Cup winner Pedro Porro on the right.

‌



Spurs are therefore open to offers on the 25-year-old, who they value at around £35million. Italian giants Inter and AC Milan were both linked earlier in the summer, before Anfield was touted as a possible destination.

Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

Andoni Iraola has seen just two players arrive since he succeeded Arne Slot, with Jeremy Jacquet joining the squad and Spanish winger Victor Munoz.

He has also seen his first pre-season severely hampered by a number of his defenders being unable to participate through the summer.

‌



Virgil van Dijk has been easing back to fitness after his exploits with the Netherlands, Joe Gomez was injured in the first game of pre-season, while Jacquet is still yet to feature after suffering a shoulder injury for Rennes.

Conor Bradley is also still recovering from a serious knee injury, leaving fans seriously concerned ahead of the season opener in just over a fortnight.

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola has seen his first pre-season hampered by defensive injuries (Image: Shaina Benhiyoun/SPP/Shutterstock)

‌



A move for the versatile Spence, who is equally adept on the left and right, appeared to tick a lot of boxes. But the ECHO understands that he is not under consideration and furthermore, the Reds have ‘absolutely no intention’ of making a move for him during the window.

Despite their mounting injury worries, it is suggested that Liverpool are not currently assessing the market for any defensive reinforcements.

Instead, the Reds are prioritising a move for an attacking player as they look to fill the vast void left after Mohamed Salah's departure.

‌



Bradley Barcola has been the big name linked for most of the summer, but Paris Saint-Germain are holding out for more than £100m for the France international.

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola (R) and Ibrahim Mbaye are both wanted by Liverpool (Image: Getty)

In recent days, Barcola’s PSG team-mate Ibrahim Mbaye has emerged as an alternative to Barcola. The teenage winger could be available for a much lower fee and perhaps more importantly could be allowed to leave the European champions.

‌



Liverpool bosses are continuing to leave their options open in the forward department, with a host of names still under consideration.

Brighton's Yankiba Minteh, Said El Mala of Koln and Lille's Matias Fernandez-Pardo are other attackers understood to have been looked at by Anfield bosses.

The Reds have two more friendlies, firstly against Monaco on Sunday and then Como the weekend after, before they kick off their Premier League campaign against Newcastle on August 23.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher hijacks FIFA's Gianni Infantino announcement with 'bribery' dig
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher hijacks FIFA's Gianni Infantino announcement with 'bribery' dig

Jamie Carragher refused to hold his tongue as FIFA announced their decision on the future of Gianni Infantino's FIFA presidency following waves of backlash for controversial World Cup plans

View Image Gianni Infantino has come under criticism (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Jamie Carragher's sarcastic response to FIFA's recent announcement regarding Gianni Infantino's future as World Football's president garnered far more support than the organisation's initial post. The 56-year-old has come under waves of criticism as of recent off the back of a cagey World Cup in North America, as well as controversial plans for the future of the tournament.

‌



Just last week, Infantino announced proposals dubbed the FIFA Forward Enterprise - which would have seen stakes in the World Cup sold off to private investors, should it have been successful. Instead, it was ultimately stopped dead in its tracks in an instant.

‌



Not only did football fans worldwide revolt at the idea of further monetizing what is supposed to be football's most prestigious tournament, but UEFA threatened to boycott the World Cup entirely from an ethical standpoint. As a result, FIFA quickly put the plans on the backburner, with Infantino playing them off as a consultatory process.

‌



Gianni Infantino’s desperate tactics fail as UEFA confirm World Cup boycott STANDS READ MORE :

Inside the murky world of FIFA lobbying as Jamie Carragher reveals World Cup request READ MORE :

A statement from the FIFA president read: "The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.

"And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.

"Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place. Our purpose has always been - and will always be - to unite and improve.

‌



"As a result, this proposal will not proceed. Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that mostly need our support."

However, shelving the plans has not prevented Infantino from seeing calls for his job at the helm of World Football, with an emergency leadership meeting taking place in Rabat on Wednesday to discuss matters. Following talks, FIFA announced that their management board had put continued faith in Infantino.

A statement read: "FIFA leadership holds constructive and positive meeting in Rabat, Morocco. The FIFA Secretary General and members of the FIFA Management Board in attendance reaffirmed their full support for FIFA President Gianni Infantino, as the only official elected by the 211 FIFA Member Associations.

"In turn, the FIFA President reiterated his full support for the FIFA Secretary General and the FIFA Administration for their necessary and outstanding work in the delivery of his vision."

‌



Liverpool legend Carragher, who has since moved into the world of football punditry, was less than impressed by the copy, taking to X to share a GIF of Sepp Blatter infamously having money thrown at him by Simon Brodkin in 2015.

That gesture was in response to a slew of allegations of corruption, before Blatter was handed an eight-year ban by FIFA's ethics committee for signing a contract dubbed 'unfavourable' to World Football, as well as making a 'disloyal payment' to UEFA's Michel Platini.

‌



Social media users were also quick to support Carragher's quip, with his comment boasting more than 7,200 likes to FIFA's 995 at the time of writing. Carragher has been incredibly critical of FIFA's leadership over the years, having also spoken about a recent World Cup initiative he claims he was pressured into supporting.

Speaking on the Football Ramble podcast, Carragher said: "I had a little chat with Arsene Wenger. He was getting involved with FIFA and it was all around this World Cup being every two years. He said, 'I'd like you to come on this other call with other ex-players and we're going to chat about the ideas going forward.' I'm like, 'Brilliant, amazing'.

‌



"We get on this Zoom and it wasn't just English players. It was like [Javier] Mascherano, there were foreign players from all over the world. They're basically talking about the pros of a World Cup every two years. I'm just listening, asking questions. I don't like the idea.

"We finish this Zoom. I haven't said whether I don't like it or it shouldn't happen, I'm just chatting with these ex players. And the guy who was organising the Zoom, then text me and said, 'Okay, can you put this out?' - like supporting it. I was like, 'No, no, no.'

"Just because I came on the Zoom...I don't agree with and I don't want it. I think it's rubbish. This feeling of, 'Once you're in here with us and you're on this Zoom, we're all these ex-players and we're in..

"That was my insight into it with Wenger and Infantino above him, with getting all these ex players in and like, 'This makes us look okay.' Half of these ex players, they don't care. From that, I was like, 'I'm not having this at all.'"

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino’s desperate tactics fail as UEFA confirm World Cup boycott STANDS
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino’s desperate tactics fail as UEFA confirm World Cup boycott STANDS

UEFA previously announced plans to boycott future World Cups in the wake of Gianni Infantino's botched plans to sell off stakes in FIFA tournaments to private investors

View 2 Images FIFA chief Gianni Infantino is still under significant pressure (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

UEFA have dropped a bombshell on Gianni Infantino by confirming their boycott of future tournaments still stands, with the beleaguered FIFA chief clinging onto his position.

‌



Infantino was forced to withdraw plans to sell off future FIFA tournaments to private investors following a furious backlash from football federation's, the vast majority of whom condemned the plans. UEFA provided the strongest rebuttal, insisting it's nations would boycott the next World Cup if the plans were not abandoned.

‌



And they have reaffirmed that European nations will not participate in FIFA's events if their conditions following the scandal are not met, including assurances that such a plot would never be concocted again, after it emerged Infantino retained the 'full sport' of FIFA's board on Wednesday night.

‌



A UEFA statement shared on Thursday afternoon read: "UEFA's associations were very clear about the conditions attached to the non-participation in FIFA competitions.

Fight to oust shameless Gianni Infantino is just starting - UEFA must not let up READ MORE :

Argentina announce national holiday to celebrate England win as Falklands banner plan emerges READ MORE :

"First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn, and secondly, assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.

"These conditions have not been met. In addition, UEFA made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino's presidency. That position holds.

‌



"Yesterday's (Wednesday) announcement that some people employed by the FIFA President (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing."

View 2 Images UEFA are still preparing to boycott future World Cups (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista, Getty Images)

UEFA's latest public attack on Infantino means the significant heat which has been on the Swiss executive in recent weeks is unlikely to subside anytime soon.

‌



Shortly after UEFA's statement was released, the English Football Association officially sent its letter withdrawing support for Infantino's re-election, potentially opening the floodgates for other major nations to follow.

Although UEFA were the only confederation to threaten a complete boycott of FIFA tournaments, Concacaf and the Asian Football Federation also rejected Infantino's plans. Concacaf were the only other confederation to publicly question Infantino, though.

Infantino apologised for "mistakes" in a letter addressing the botched plans, which would have seen national federations bank £30.1million courtesy of the FIFA Forward Enterprise.

Sports.title: Mo Salah is taking a step down with Turkey move but it is about more than just money
Sports.content:
Mo Salah is taking a step down with Turkey move but it is about more than just money

Jamie Carragher has said he was surprised by the Liverpool legend's switch to Trabzonspor but Super Lig clubs are spending big and attracting some top talent

View 3 Images Mohamed Salah has signed a two-year deal with Trabzonspor (Image: OZAN KOSE, AFP via Getty Images)

As usual, Jamie Carragher makes a very valid point when he suggests that Mohamed Salah is still good enough to be playing in a competition of a higher standard than the Turkish Süper Lig.

‌



Salah is certainly good enough to still be a major performer in the Champions League but will have to be content with playing in the Europa League next season, assuming Trabzonspor negotiates the qualifying round.

‌



Let’s face it, Salah is still good enough to be playing in the Premier League but you can assume that prospect was contractually removed when the player and Liverpool agreed to part ways a year early. Anyway, Salah probably could not countenance playing for another Premier League club. Not yet, anyway.

‌



But there must have been interest from some blue-chip Champions League clubs in a 34-year-old all-time Premier League great who, by his standards, had an average time of things last season but was still one of Liverpool’s better performers. Which is why the obvious conclusion is that Trabzonspor are paying fantastic wages.

Jamie Carragher criticises Mohamed Salah's Turkey move after Liverpool exit READ MORE :

Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

That will certainly be the case. The marquee Turkish clubs - Istanbul’s big three, Galatasary, Fenerbahce and Besiktas, plus Trabzonspor - are spending big on players and contracts despite being burdened with heavy debt.

Salah will be playing in a league that will feature the likes of Victor Osimhen, Leroy Sane, Ilkay Gundogan, Leandro Trossard and Nathan Ake this coming season. And there will probably be more to follow.

‌



But it will take many more recruits of that quality to make Turkish club football a major force in European football. Since Galatasaray won the UEFA Cup in 2000, only one Turkish side has reached the semi-finals of a major UEFA competition.

View 3 Images Leandro Trossard left Arsenal for Besiktas earlier this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Opta currently ranks it as the 14th strongest domestic league in world football, behind national competitions in countries such as Denmark and Poland. According to Opta, England’s Championship is stronger.

‌



That would seem to be stretching it a little but there is no doubt, of course, that Salah is taking a significantly-sized step backwards in terms of the overall quality of the league he is operating in. But aside from the considerable financial attraction - his deal is said to be worth around £14million a year - perhaps Salah just wanted a different experience.

For sure, the Premier League is ultra-competitive and generates enormous interest. Stadiums are full and it is a commercial behemoth.

View 3 Images Mohamed Salah was greeted by thousands of Trabzonspor fans when he arrived at the airport (Image: Hakan Burak Altunoz/Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



But sometimes, it feels a little bit too sanitised, a little bit too polished, a little bit too commercial. Tunnel clubs for wealthy fans, hospitality takeovers. And to be honest, even on the pitch, everything has become a little sanitised. Very good but not as edgy as it once was.

Perhaps Salah fancied something a little more visceral, a little more unpredictable, a little more volatile (a lot more volatile), a little more raw. He might have just fancied the cash, of course, but maybe that was not the be-all and end-all.

Yes, you might have expected him to rock up in Serie A but he has made a fascinating decision late in his career. And it will be fascinating to see how it works out.

Sports.title: Scottie Scheffler defended after microphones picked up row with his caddie
Sports.content:
Scottie Scheffler defended after microphones picked up row with his caddie

Two-time Masters champion Scottie Scheffler has been criticised ever since his heated exchange with his caddie at the Memorial Tournament back in June

View 2 Images Scottie Scheffler and his caddie, Ted Scott (Image: Ben Jared/PGA TOUR via Getty Images)

Golf star Min Woo Lee has defended Scottie Scheffler after the two-time Masters champion was involved in a heated exchanged his caddie back in June. Scheffler finished tied-12th at Muirfield earlier in the summer, but caught plenty of attention during the opening round in Ohio.

During the opening round in Dublin, Scheffler hit one of his shots on the 16th hole into the water and was visibly frustrated as he spoke to his caddie, Tedd Scott, as he walked towards the drop zone.

Audio picked up from the microphone showed Scheffler having a heated exchange with Scott as he walked down the fairway, with the four-time major winner being the subject of criticism ever since.

However, Lee has leapt to the defence of Scheffler, explaining why the 30-year-old may have reacted the way he did in that moment at the Memorial tournament.

"First of all, I think that was a tough moment," Lee said on the Life on Tour podcast. "I know he's not like that all the time.

Why Rory McIlroy and Scottie Scheffler aren't playing in Wyndham Championship as stars pull out READ MORE :

Rory McIlroy shows true colours as he's spotted partying at Ibiza nightclub READ MORE :

"It was just a really tough day at Memorial, and Memorial's one of the toughest — I think it's the toughest golf course outside of the majors. So blow-ups happen, and it just looked bad."

Lee added: "I don't think social media and the audience know, 'Is this how he treats his caddie?' I think a lot of players do that, and it's just unlucky that the microphone was right there taking it all in.

"As an audience, you'd like that, you'd want to listen to all that, but as a player and colleague, I wouldn't want a mic that close to me, just because stuff like that can happen. He's one of the best players in the world and he's saying, 'How can the wind be there and not there?'

"I think caddies are very, very strong-skinned, and they've gone through a lot. Sometimes we give them slack and they just have to brush it off.

"Sometimes they want to yell back at us, but it's a tough situation. I'm sure a lot of my caddies have wanted to shout back at me."

View 2 Images Scottie Scheffler and caddie Ted Scott (Image: Mike Mulholland/Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Scheffler was asked about the moment on the 16th hole at Muirfield, where he alsop reflected on his opening round in Ohio.

“That’s just another really good iron shot, and the wind switched from down off the right to pretty significantly in off the right,” Scheffler said after his first round on June 4.

“If it’s down off the right, that ball’s probably where I hit my wedge shot to. So just don’t really know what I’m supposed to do there outside of trying to hit a good shot, and then it’s frustrating when it doesn’t work out, especially when it doesn’t work out in that direction.

Article continues below

“I would rather get gusted in off the left, not in off the right there. All you can do is just try to hit good shots.

“It can be very frustrating sometimes when you feel like you’re hitting good shots and then you’re going to the drop zone.”

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
