Pero le preocupa el papel que los servicios de inteligencia cubanos puedan tener en estos momentos. Para contrarrestarlo, la Agencia Central de Inteligencia (CIA) ha aumentado sus recursos operativos en la isla durante los últimos meses para intensificar la operación que facilite el cambio de liderazgo, según adelantó The New York Times. Cuba ha sido declarada “prioridad 1″, junto a China, Irán y Rusia, en un reciente documento sobre los objetivos principales de los servicios secretos.

“En lo que respecta a operaciones de espionaje e influencia, Cuba es una verdadera superpotencia en estos ámbitos”, aseguró hace unos días el secretario de Estado de Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, durante una entrevista en el canal conservador de noticias Fox News para explicar la importancia de los servicios cubanos de inteligencia. “Si analizamos la historia del espionaje en Estados Unidos, Cuba es el único país que ha infiltrado y ocultado espías en nuestro sistema de forma sistemática, sin siquiera pagarles”, agregó.

La Casa Blanca lanzó una campaña contra el régimen cubano hace algo más de seis meses. Ha impuesto un estricto embargo petrolero que tiene sumida a la isla en la oscuridad y ha aprobado varios paquetes de sanciones para bloquear los activos y bienes de decenas de organismos públicos y altos cargos cubanos. La escalada es tal que los hoteles extranjeros, la principal fuente de riqueza que tenía la isla, han tenido que cerrar y poner fin a sus operaciones mientras se prolongue la situación de asfixia sobre Cuba.

“Las instituciones militares y de inteligencia de Cuba son los principales agentes de la represión interna y nodos de la cleptocracia, especialmente a través del conglomerado militar GAESA”, señaló este jueves Marco Rubio a través de un comunicado para anunciar las nuevas sanciones impuestas por Washington a autoridades y organismos públicos cubanos “involucrados en la cooperación militar extranjera y la adquisición de equipamiento militar destinado al régimen cubano”. Las sanciones afectan a cinco empresas cubanas y ocho funcionarios, entre los que se encuentra Roberto Legrasotolongo, jefe del Estado Mayor General de las Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias y primer viceministro del Ministerio de las Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias cubano (MINFAR).

En las últimas semanas, Rubio ha expresado su preocupación por la fiabilidad de la información que Washington tiene sobre Cuba por la infiltración de espías cubanos en la Administración estadounidense. “Tuvimos un embajador estadounidense, que resultó ser un espía cubano y fue condenado recientemente. Hemos tenido infiltraciones en los niveles más altos de la Agencia de Inteligencia de la Defensa. [La analista de ese departamento] Ana Belén Montes fue uno de los mayores fallos de inteligencia por parte de Estados Unidos y una de las mayores infiltraciones que jamás hayamos sufrido en nuestro sistema”, dijo el secretario de Estado en la Fox.

“Los situaría [a la Dirección de Inteligencia de Cuba, DI] probablemente como el servicio de inteligencia más complicado contra el que he trabajado. No solo porque sean tan astutos y despiadados, sino porque son extraordinariamente buenos”, según describe James Olson, exjefe de contrainteligencia de la CIA en un informe titulado Cuba, la capital del comunismo del siglo XXI, publicado por el Departamento de Estado hace tres semanas. Olson señala en el informe: “Los cubanos siguen infiltrados en nuestro Gobierno... Les garantizo que solo conocemos la punta del iceberg. Son mucho mejores que el KGB”. El documento, de 100 páginas, acusa al régimen cubano de “respaldar una ola sin precedentes de terrorismo de izquierda en Estados Unidos”. Desde que lo publicó el pasado 20 de julio, el Departamento de Estado lo ha retuiteado varias veces cada semana junto a mensajes sobre la situación de Cuba.

Rubio, de origen cubano, está liderando las acciones dentro de la Administración estadounidense para propiciar el cambio político en la isla caribeña, situada a apenas 135 kilómetros de Florida. El secretario de Estado considera al país como “un Estado fallido” y “una amenaza para la seguridad nacional de Estados Unidos”.

Una calle de La Habana, el miércoles durante un apagón. FELIPE BORREGO (EFE)

Washington aumenta la presión sobre el régimen castrista al tiempo que la isla está al borde del colapso, como consecuencia del estricto cerco petrolero. Apenas tiene suministro eléctrico; los cortes de energía son diarios, hay desabastecimiento de productos básicos y la isla está a un paso de una crisis humanitaria.

La CIA tiene un grupo operativo secreto en la isla desde hace casi dos años, pero ha aumentado sus recursos con la incorporación de analistas de inteligencia, agentes de contravigilancia y otros miembros de la agencia para introducirse en los niveles más influyentes de la sociedad cubana y convencerlos de la necesidad de cambiar a los dirigentes de línea dura por otros más abiertos al cambio, según los medios estadounidenses.

También están captando nuevos informantes para aumentar el flujo de datos por si la Casa Blanca barajara finalmente una posible operación militar al estilo de la que realizó en Venezuela a principios de este año para capturar al expresidente Nicolás Maduro y situar a Delcy Rodríguez en el poder bajo un sistema de tutela desde Washington.

La agencia de espías ha enviado nuevo personal a Cuba para intensificar sus operaciones, según confirmó también Politico. Washington se está posicionando sobre el terreno para aumentar la información sobre la situación real de la isla. El Gobierno de Donald Trump revisó hace pocas semanas el Marco Nacional de Prioridades de Inteligencia (NIPF, en sus siglas en inglés) e incluyó a Cuba como “prioridad 1”.

La escalada contra la isla se aceleró con el regreso de Donald Trump a la Casa Blanca. El mandatario republicano ha puesto a Marco Rubio al frente de la operación para propiciar un cambio político. Como prueba del renovado interés sobre Cuba, Washington envió el pasado mayo a La Habana al director general de la CIA, John Ratcliffe, para reunirse con autoridades del régimen cubano, entre los que se encontraba Raúl G. Rodríguez, conocido como El Cangrejo, nieto y guardaespaldas de Raúl Castro.

Ratcliffe, el miembro de mayor rango del Gobierno estadounidense en pisar la isla desde que empezó la campaña de Trump, transmitió varios mensajes. Por un lado, advirtió a La Habana de que deje de colaborar en asuntos de inteligencia con China y Rusia. Además, mostró su admiración por los servicios de inteligencia cubanos, a los que ofreció colaboración si se producía un cambio de régimen; por último, trasladó un ultimátum para que Cuba emprenda las reformas políticas y económicas que demanda Washington.

La presencia de la CIA en el país caribeño no es nueva. Desde los años sesenta ha tenido una presencia más o menos constante. En los últimos años, la agencia desclasificó algunos documentos secretos sobre el papel de sus espías en la isla, durante el episodio de Bahía Cochinos (1961), entre otros.

Durante el primer mandato de Donald Trump, varios agentes estadounidenses de inteligencia sufrieron unos extraños problemas de salud en lo que denominaron como síndrome de La Habana. Así que el republicano redujo al mínimo la presencia de espías hasta hace seis meses, cuando lanzó la dura campaña de presión para controlar el poder en su vecino.

World.title: Dos nuevos casos de peste porcina africana eleva a 375 los positivos en Cataluña
World.content:
Jabalíes REMITIDA / HANDOUT por Generalitat de Catalunya Fotografía remitida a medios de comunicación exclusivamente para ilustrar la noticia a la que hace referencia la imagen, y citando la procedencia de la imagen en la firma 30/07/2026

Cataluña ha registrado esta última semana dos nuevos casos de peste porcina africana (PPA) en jabalíes dentro de la zona de alto riesgo, elevando así a 375 los positivos detectados desde el mes de noviembre de 2025. Los nuevos positivos de PPA se han localizado concretamente en Barcelona y en Sant Just Desvern (Barcelona), según el balance semanal publicado este jueves por el Ministerio de Agricultura, Pesca y Alimentación.

Desde la detección del primer brote, las autoridades han analizado un total de 10.700 jabalíes, de los que 10.325 han dado negativo, y no se ha detectado ningún caso positivo en cerdo doméstico. Los casos se concentran en 19 municipios de la zona de alto riesgo.

El Govern ha destacado que siguen desarrollándose “intensas labores de búsqueda de cadáveres de jabalíes”, así como las actuaciones para reducir las poblaciones de esta especie en la zona, principalmente mediante el empleo de trampas de captura y el control poblacional realizado por agentes rurales y cazadores formados.

De igual modo, se continúa trabajando en la instalación y supervisión de medidas de aislamiento, se han reforzado los vallados y otro tipo de barreras, priorizando el control en corredores de uso de jabalíes, que se van adaptando a la evolución de la situación epidemiológica.

El primer caso de jabalí infectado por peste porcina africana (PPA) se confirmó el 28 de noviembre de 2025. El animal fue localizado en Cerdanyola del Vallès. Tras aquella detección comenzaron las restricciones de acceso al medio rural. Desde entonces, solo han hecho que ampliarse. Por ese motivo, entidades y particulares se han unido en una plataforma bautizada como Collserola Oberta (Collserola Abierta) con una única petición: “Hace meses que Collserola está sometida a restricciones de acceso. No negamos la peste porcina africana ni los riesgos que comporta. Exigimos transparencia, resultados medibles y un plan de reapertura progresiva”.

World.title: El Govern admite errores de cálculo en las oposiciones de 400 plazas de personal educativo
World.content:
El Departament de Educación de la Generalitat ha admitido “errores de cálculo” en la contabilización de los méritos el listado provisional de las oposiciones de 400 plazas de Personal de Atención Educativa (PAE), según ha avanzado Nació Digital y confirmado este diario con fuentes del Departamento. La consejería de Esther Niubó tiene previsto publicar este jueves la nueva lista con los fallos ya corregidos.

Educación ha vivido este verano dos procesos diferentes: por un lado, el concurso de traslados del personal PAE que se resolvió el pasado 24 de julio con la reasignación de puestos de trabajo. Una vez solventado, quedaron 400 plazas libres que se adjudicaron con la oposición. La lista provisional se publicó el 30 de julio y en ella se incurrieron en fallos en el recuento de méritos.

Según fuentes oficiales, el departamento ha comunicado a los sindicatos los errores en un procedimiento que asegura que es habitual, dice que no tiene nada que ver con la adjudicación de plazas por error hace un año y asegura que no se trata de miles de personas afectadas que han tenido ahora que reorganizar su vida por la asignación de una plaza por error sino que son 400 y que no afecta a los plazos previstos.

El secretario general de Junts, Jordi Turull, ha criticado el enésimo episodio en el que se ha visto envuelto Educación. “Cuando creías que la incompetencia del Govern había tocado fondo, siempre hay nuevos episodios que te recuerdan que no. Y siempre en los ámbitos más sensibles para el país”, ha afirmado ironizando: “Es bien bien el desgobierno de tothom”.

La consejería vive en una crisis permanente y que ha alcanzado el punto culminante este verano tras el escándalo del informe Pisa en el que Cataluña queda fuera de la evaluación al haber excluido al 23% del alumnado frente al 5% como estaba estipulado. El Govern conoció la decisión en marzo y lo divulgó a final de julio. El president Salvador Illa afirmó que no se informó porque se estaba averiguando qué había pasado y que la investigación no ha concluido.

World.title: De “dame más gasolina” a “no me quiten el perreo”: dos demandas contra Bad Bunny dan la batalla de las mujeres que ponen voz al reguetón
World.content:
El artista se enfrenta al pago de hasta 49 millones de euros por el uso de sendas notas de voz en sus canciones, práctica habitual en el género de la que a menudo no se benefician las intérpretes

Cada vez que Bad Bunny cantó en directo EoO, de su disco DeBÍ TiRAR MáS FOToS (2024), en su recién acabada gira europea, la música se detuvo antes del puente. Miles de personas quedaban expectantes y un sonido irrumpía de forma robótica, una voz que decía “Pe“, pero se corta. ”Pe... Pe... Pe...“, se repetía cada vez más rápido mientras en la pantalla aparecía la palabra que no se termina de pronunciar: PERREO. Tras unos segundos de tensión, por fin, el audio sonaba completo. Una mujer que reclama: ”Mira, puñeta, no me quiten el perreo”, con acento boricua. Esa voz está hoy en el centro de una demanda contra el cantante por 16 millones de dólares (14 millones de euros).

Quien la pronuncia es Tainaly Serrano Rivera. Ella demandó a Benito Antonio Ocasio Martínez, nombre real de Bad Bunny, en enero, alegando falta de consentimiento para el uso de su voz en dos canciones: Solo de mí, del disco X 100pre (2018), donde se escucha la frase entera al final de la canción, y EoO, en la que aparece alrededor del primer minuto, aunque no se acaba de oír la palabra “perreo”. La grabación se utilizó “sin compensación, sin atribuirle su reconocimiento legal o derechos para las canciones, promociones, discos, conciertos en el mundo entero y plataformas sociales y musicales, televisión y radio, entre otras cosas”, según el documento presentado ante un tribunal de Puerto Rico.

Ella no es la primera en demandar a Bad Bunny por algo similar, pues este también se encuentra en una batalla legal con su exnovia, Carliz de la Cruz, por una grabación en la que ella dice: “Bad Bunny, baby“, y que el cantante utilizó al inicio de su carrera, cuando eran pareja. Por ejemplo, en Diles, uno de sus primeros éxitos, de enero de 2016, aparece el audio en los primeros segundos. En este caso, De la Cruz se queja de que también se utilizó en dos temas sin su consentimiento tras el fin de su relación: en el sencillo Pa’ Ti, que se publicó en diciembre de 2016, y la canción Dos mil 16, del disco Un Verano Sin Ti (2022). Por ello le reclama nada menos que 40 millones de dólares (35 millones de euros).

“Carliz nos llamó para revisar unos contratos que le habían hecho llegar de parte del sello de Puerto Rico Rimas Entertainment y de Bad Bunny para que cediera los derechos sobre su imagen”, explica Joanna Bocanegra Ocasio, una de las abogadas que maneja ambos casos. “Lo que pasa es que prácticamente enseguida, dos días después, ya había salido publicada la canción con su voz sin que se hubiese llegado a ningún acuerdo por escrito”.

Según la ley de imagen en Puerto Rico, el consentimiento debe darse por escrito y por un tiempo determinado, explica José Marxuach Fagot, otro de los abogados que defienden a Tainaly y a Carliz en sus demandas. Y si se quiere reclamar un uso incorrecto, el tribunal ha determinado que el tiempo límite no tiene que ver con la fecha de publicación de la obra, sino con el conocimiento de la persona afectada, es decir, la fecha en la que se entere de que su imagen, en esta circunstancia su voz, ha sido utilizada sin permiso. Desde ese momento, tiene un año para demandar.

En el caso de Carliz, la defensa de Bad Bunny sostiene que incluir su voz dentro de una canción no equivale a usar su imagen. Según ellos, una canción es una obra artística (aunque genere ingresos) y por eso alegan que la ley de imagen no debe aplicarse. Sin embargo, el Tribunal Supremo de Justicia de Puerto Rico admitió la demanda porque entiende que la grabación concreta de la voz podría tener protección y determinó en julio que existen suficientes indicios para seguir investigando, aunque acotando el caso solo a la canción Dos mil 16, pues al momento de presentar la demanda ya había vencido el plazo para reclamar por la canción Pa’ Ti. Ambos casos están a la espera de que empiecen los primeros pasos para determinar quién tiene razón.

Mientras tanto, los abogados de estas mujeres creen que hay mucho desconocimiento sobre el tema de los derechos de imagen en la industria de la música, y que hay quien se aprovecha de eso. “Por ejemplo, el hecho de que se haya dado un consentimiento en un momento determinado no hace que ese consentimiento sea perpetuo”, aclara Bocanegra. “Esa voz no se puede utilizar permanentemente, salvo que haya un contrato de cesión que así lo determine”. Y eso no ocurrió en ninguno de los dos casos.

Esa ambigüedad de no especificar por escrito para qué se van a utilizar las grabaciones que hacen las llamadas “vocales” —mujeres que graban frases cortas, a veces melódicas, en el reguetón— ha sido una práctica habitual desde el nacimiento del género. “Hay mucha juventud que ha caído en esa movida. Se les vendió un sueño, que iban a ser grandes. ¿Y quién se lucró? Yo, no”, dice Irenis Cruz, que fue conocida a principios de los 2000 por cantar varios éxitos junto a DJ Joe en la serie de discos Fatal Fantassy. Ella asegura que hay una canción de Bad Bunny en la que se puede escuchar su voz diciendo “¡Ay!” y otros monosílabos en tono sexy, grabados 20 años atrás sin haber firmado contrato que lo permita: “Usan mi voz, claro que sí. Pero a estas alturas de mi vida, no me importa”. Le gusta que sus nietos escuchen su voz cuando salen de fiesta, y aunque reconoce que nunca se le pagó lo que merecía, se aleja de la vía legal después de varias experiencias negativas.

“Dame más gasolina”

Para evitar situaciones similares, otras artistas se han cuidado de firmar antes de grabar: “Yo siempre he sido solista, desde que esto era underground”, recuerda Glorimar Montalvo Castro, mejor conocida como Glory, que grabó junto a Daddy Yankee, Don Omar o Héctor y Tito en canciones como Gasolina, Dale Don Dale o Baila Morena. Es la voz de frases como “dame más gasolina”, “dale, papi, que estoy suelta como gabete” o “dale, moreno, que nos fuimos afuegote”, entre otras.

Glory junto a Héctor, Tito y Don Omar en un fotograma del vídeo para la canción 'Morena'.

“Éramos súper pocas mujeres al principio. Es un género que está altamente dominado por varones. Y a mí me decían: ‘Ya viene esta con sus papeles’, cuando me veían con mis documentos para firmar. A veces esos comentarios también intimidan, incluso tienen la intención de intimidarte”. Pero aclara: “No estoy diciendo que eso sea lo que ha ocurrido en el caso de otras compañeras porque no lo sé. Sería bien interesante hacer una reunión y escuchar esas experiencias, porque yo cuando grabo digo: ‘Somos panas y todo, pero esto es negocio”. Glory ha mantenido su carrera hasta hoy, y aunque no tiene tanta fama como sus compañeros, es muy reconocida en la industria. Este año ha lanzado un EP con cinco canciones nuevas.

También es importante recordar que estas situaciones no ocurren solo en canciones de reguetón. Las demandas en cuanto a derechos y copyright son usuales en Estados Unidos, país que rige una parte sustancial del sistema jurídico de Puerto Rico. Cualquier género en el que haya un desequilibrio de poder entre los artistas famosos y los que están tratando de abrirse camino es susceptible a estos desencuentros. “Los nuevos a lo mejor piensan que pueden tener una gran oportunidad y no se asesoran legalmente”, añade la abogada Bocanegra.

Ella y Marxuach tampoco creen que solo les pase a las mujeres, pero sí admiten que desde que se hicieron públicas las demandas contra Bad Bunny han tenido que luchar contra una narrativa en la opinión pública: “Hay quien piensa que las motivaciones de ellas como mujeres son otras, en el caso particular de Caliz por ser exnovia. No creen que realmente quieran vindicar su derecho. Desde nuestra perspectiva, puede que Bad Bunny sea el artista más famoso del mundo, pero nuestro enfoque siempre ha sido no atacar ese aspecto del caso. Si utilizaron la imagen, la voz de las chicas, sin un consentimiento escrito, ellas tienen derecho a demandar”.

World.title: La misión imposible de ascender en la Seguridad Social: solo 27 funcionarios aprueban para casi 1.000 plazas de promoción interna
World.content:
La Seguridad Social acaba de hacer pública una resolución con el listado de aprobados para su proceso de ascensos al Cuerpo de Gestión de este organismo: solo 27 funcionarios han pasado la prueba para ocupar una de las casi 1.000 plazas de promoción interna convocadas (927 plazas generales y 68 para personas con discapacidad). De esta forma, el porcentaje de aprobados ha sido tan solo del 2,7% y la práctica totalidad de las plazas para ascender han quedado vacantes, una cifra excepcionalmente baja.

Así lo ha denunciado esta semana la Federación de Servicios Públicos (FSP) del sindicato UGT, cuyos responsables consideran que estas las tasas de aprobados “son un claro síntoma de que el sistema necesita cambios”. “No nos explicamos qué ha podido pasar; el año pasado ya hubo muchas vacantes pero no fue tan desastroso”, señala el coordinador de UGT en la Seguridad Social, Pedro Carrasco, en ese mismo comunicado.

El hecho de que cada año queden plazas de promoción interna vacantes es especialmente preocupante en el caso de las distintas Entidades Gestoras y servicios comunes de la Seguridad Social, donde el 71% de sus trabajadores tienen 50 o más años y, por tanto, están más próximos a la jubilación. Este porcentaje de empleados entrados en la cincuentena representa el 57% de la plantilla de la Administración General del Estado y el 33% en el mercado laboral en general en España, según el último Estudio sobre el envejecimiento de las plantillas de la administración estatal en 2025 con proyecciones hasta 2035 que elabora el Ministerio de Función Pública.

En opinión de FSP-UGT las bajas cifras de aprobados no pueden explicarse únicamente por el nivel de exigencia de las pruebas o por el esfuerzo de las personas aspirantes. El sindicato culpa al propio diseño del proceso selectivo, que consiste en un concurso-oposición, en el que, para que cuenten los méritos y la experiencia, se debe superar previamente una oposición, un proceso memorístico muy similar al de quienes se presentan al turno libre para ingresar por primera vez en la Administración.

“Es cierto que el temario puede ser algo menor para la promoción interna, pero luego debes desarrollar preguntas para las que debes saber cosas de los temas que se exigen para el turno libre, con lo que en la práctica la oposición no es más fácil a pesar de llevar varios años ya trabajando para la Seguridad Social y sabiendo cómo se hacen las cosas”, se queja Carrasco.

Además, el responsable de UGT insiste en las dificultades de los empleados del organismo para preparar una prueba así: “Son todo gente que ya trabaja sus ocho horas diarias y a los que no se tiene en cuenta su saber hacer si no aprueban un examen memorístico previo”. Por ello, el sindicato asegura que estos procesos de selección para la promoción interna “no responden al objetivo para el que fueron creados, sino que están dificultando el acceso a la promoción de profesionales con experiencia, capacitación y un firme compromiso con el servicio público”.

En este caso, en el que la promoción era del cuerpo C1 al A2, para el que ya se exige tener una titulación, se suma otra circunstancia poco común: ni siquiera se ha cubierto el número de solicitantes para las 995 plazas de promoción interna que se ofertaban. El número de personas que se presentaron no llegaba a las 700. Esto es para Carrasco una prueba más del desánimo que genera el actual diseño de los procesos para ascender dentro de la Seguridad Social. Además, precisa que tampoco el incentivo salarial opera para este tipo de promoción, porque al subir del cuerpo C1 al A2 se pierde un complemento, con lo que si el funcionario pasa al nivel más bajo del nuevo cuerpo, apenas gana entre 50 y 80 euros más al mes, dependiendo de la retención de IRPF que se le aplique en la nómina.

En opinión de los responsables de FSP-UGT, los procesos de selección de promoción interna deberían ser “totalmente diferentes”. En concreto, reclaman que en lugar de los actuales concursos oposición —los procesos que solo tienen en cuenta los méritos sin examen memorístico son excepcionales en la Seguridad Social y en el resto de la Administración General del Estado— se establezca un sistema de cursos o módulos, que se superen con un examen concreto para estas formaciones. Estos, además, deberían estar relacionados con las labores concretas que se realizan en los puestos de trabajo. De hecho, otra de las quejas de Carrasco es que las pruebas actuales “no tienen nada que ver con el trabajo que realizan los funcionarios”, a pesar de que se les exige tener una antigüedad de al menos dos años en la Administración para poder optar a la promoción interna.

World.title: Pistas para un viaje de verano a Portugal: de las playas del Algarve a los azulejos de Lisboa
World.content:
Ciudades y pueblos llenos de encanto, pistas para comer bien y barato y algunos trucos para descubrir el país

Año tras año, Portugal es un destino de vacaciones recurrente. Pero decir Portugal puede tener muchos significados: están las playas del Algarve que acogen a los amantes del surf, los pueblos del centro del país llenos de encanto y calles empedradas o los paisajes que dejan el Duero y el Tajo a su paso por el país vecino. Además del magnetismo de Lisboa y Oporto, dos ciudades llenas de vida y de historia.

Esta es una guía de destinos para quienes este verano viajen a Portugal.

Además, dos pistas gastronómicas para saber dónde comer y qué pedir en Lisboa y Oporto. Así como una visita cultural imprescindible en la capital lusa.

Y la experiencia viajera en primera persona de Paco Nadal, dispuesto a regresar una y otra vez al país.

World.title: Kodai Sano joins PSV in biggest Eredivisie move of the summer
World.content:
PSV Eindhoven are in a race against the clock to complete the signing of NEC Nijmegen midfielder Kodai Sano before the first match of the Dutch league season after the clubs agreed a fee of €14.5 million.

The deal, a record sale for the Nijmegen club, left a bitter aftertaste after Sano pulled out of the squad for the midweek Champions League match against Olympiakos despite travelling to Greece.

Director of football Carlos Aalbers said the 22-year-old, who was instrumental in the club’s third-place finish last year, was sent home from the team hotel because “agreements were breached”.

“Sano didn’t want to play and we didn’t want a player in the team who didn’t want to play,” he said.

The champions could be set to offload striker Couhaib Driouech to Rangers before the end of the transfer window. Dutch media report that the two clubs have agreed a price of around €8 million for the 24-year-old Morocco international, but no formal bid has been tabled.

PSV are also believed to be close to completing the signing of Serbian international Filip Kostic, who spent two seasons at Groningen earlier in his career. The arrival of the 33-year-old has fuelled speculation that Croatian veteran Ivan Perisic is on his way out of Eindhoven, most likely to join Inter Milan.

Reserve goalkeeper Joël Drommel is leaving PSV after five years, returning to Twente, the club where he made his professional debut in 2015. “It feels like coming home,” said Drommel, who spent last season on loan at Sparta.

Tadic returns

Another Serbian veteran, former Ajax striker Dusan Tadic, is back in the Netherlands after joining NEC on a three-year contract. “The Netherlands is my second home,” said the 37-year-old, who has also played for Groningen and Twente.

Feyenoord look set to hang on to 20-year-old defender Givairo Read after turning down bids from AS Roma and Nottingham Forest.

Neither club was prepared to match the asking price of €25 million plus €4 million in bonuses for Read, whose current contract runs to 2029.

The Rotterdammers and PSV both want to sign former Feyenoord defender Lutsharel Geertruida from RB Leipzig, but neither club is willing to match the Bundesliga club’s €20 million asking price. Leipzig also say they are not interested in a loan deal.

Ajax loan signings

The biggest name to join Ajax so far under new head coach Míchel is goalkeeper Marc-André ter Stegen, who is moving from Barcelona on a season-long loan.

The 34-year-old, who won the Champions League and seven La Liga titles with the Catalan side, spent part of last season on loan at Girona, Míchel’s previous club. “When I first spoke with [Ajax’s director of football] Jordi Cruyff, I immediately felt it was the right option,” he said.

Another experienced German moving to Amsterdam is 30-year-old midfielder Julian Brandt, who arrives on a free transfer from Borussia Dortmund.

The Amsterdammers are believed to be in contact with Napoli about bringing Noa Lang back to the club if, as expected, Belgian striker Mika Godts leaves for Paris Saint-Germain before the end of the month. The clubs are understood to be negotiating a five-year deal, but PSG are haggling over Ajax’s €60 million price tag.

Torrents as cover

Ajax have also signed 19-year-old midfielder Jofre Torrents on loan from Barcelona as possible cover for Owen Wijndal, who is rumoured to be seeking a move out of Amsterdam. If Wijndal stays, Torrents is likely to turn out for the youth team in the Keuken Kampioen Divisie.

Midfielder Kian Fitz-Jim is definitely leaving after Ajax agreed to sell the 23-year-old, who spent part of last season on loan at Excelsior, to Torino.

Calvin Stengs is back at AZ Alkmaar after four years, after being released from his contract at Feyenoord, while Republic of Ireland striker Troy Parrott is said to be considering a move from Alkmaar to English Championship with West Ham United.

Elsewhere in the Eredivisie, Excelsior have signed 20-year-old striker Aymen Sliti on loan from city neighbours Feyenoord.

Swedes at Groningen

Groningen have signed 18-year-old Swedish midfielder Alvin Nordin from Helsingborgs on a four-year deal. Nordin played 28 first-teammatches for the Swedish club after making his debut at 16. Another Swede, defender Malcolm Jeng, is moving to the Euroborg on loan from Stade de Reims.

The northerners have also turned down a bid from AZ for striker Thom van Bergen. “We’ve made it clear Thom is not for sale,” managing director Frank van Mosselveld told RTV Noord.

Newly promoted Willem II have acquired 29-year-old midfielder Hidde ter Avest from English third-tier side Oxford United.

Telstar have strengthened their midfield with the signing of 20-year-old Harrie Kuster from Twente, 20-year-old Isiah Ahmed from Heerenveen and 23-year-old Gabi Caschili, who was released by Cambuur Leeuwarden a year ago after he was involved in a brawl during an amateur match.

World.title: Dutch rights group COC wins Pride Award for 80 years of work
World.content:
Dutch campaign group COC Nederland, the oldest surviving LGBTQI+ rights organisation in the world, has won the International Pride Award at the WorldPride Human Rights Conference in Amsterdam.

The awards, a joint initiative of the United Nations Development Programme and ILGA World, were presented to five “equality champions” at a ceremony in the Beurs van Berlage on Wednesday. Amsterdam is hosting WorldPride, the global LGBTQI+ event, for the first time this year.

The COC, founded in 1946, was recognised in particular for its support for people in countries where homosexuality is banned or even punishable by death, director Marie Ricardo, who accepted the prize, told broadcaster NOS.

“We support them with coaching, we help them think about how to bring about change in their own surroundings, and we support them with money,” she said.

Ricardo called the award “a recognition of the work we have been doing for 80 years, and the 40 years we have been supporting movements internationally”.

Other winners include South African deputy minister Mmapaseka Steve Letsike and Ugandan transgender pastor Aggie Dennett Harmon.

World.title: Dutch state close to breaking even on ABN Amro bailout
World.content:
The Dutch state is close to recouping the full cost of the 2008 nationalisation of ABN Amro, after a share price rally took the bank’s stock above €40 this week, according to calculations by the Financieele Dagblad.

The finance ministry had long assumed the rescue would be a loss-making operation. In late 2023 it told MPs it was “not realistic” that the state would break even in the short term, projecting a shortfall of almost €7 billion.

Since then the shares have tripled in value, from €13.20 at the time to just over €40 on Thursday. The state, which still owns 20.5% of the bank has now recouped €14.2 billion through staged sell-offs, and its remaining stake is worth some €6.7 billion, the FD said.

That brings the total close to the €21.7 billion the ministry says has been pumped into the bank since 2008.

Slow sell-off

The state bought ABN Amro, Fortis Bank Nederland and the insurer now known as ASR in October 2008 for €16.8 billion to stop parent company Fortis collapsing in the credit crisis, and injected roughly €8 billion more into the banks in the years that followed.

ABN Amro returned to the stock market in 2015, but the share price languished for years and the sell-off repeatedly stalled. Former D66 finance minister Sigrid Kaag restarted the sales in 2023, and every tranche since has fetched a higher price.

Interest paid on the money borrowed for the rescue has been roughly cancelled out by dividend income over the years, the FD said.

Cost cutting

Morningstar analyst Johann Scholtz told the FD the share price rise is partly due to the state selling its stakes and the bank therefore having more freedom to cut costs, along with investors speculating about takeovers in the European banking sector.

The windfall will not plug the cabinet’s budget gaps, however, as one-off share sales cannot be counted towards the deficit under EU rules.

World.title: Jetten thanks firefighters on visit to site of Limburg wildfire
World.content:
Prime minister Rob Jetten has visited the site of a wildfire that has been raging in Limburg for four days, destroying around a square kilometre of woodland.

Jetten thanked emergency workers for their efforts to contain the blaze in the Boshuizerbergen, in a social media video showing “the huge damage to nature and to the animals and people who have had to be evacuated”.

An emergency order banning people from the area remains in force, but limited train services resumed between Venray and Boxmeer on Thursday morning. Arriva had to lay on buses for commuters after the line through the fire zone was closed.

Firefighters said on Wednesday they had brought the blaze under control, only for it to flare up again twice during the night.

Chinook helicopters dropped 900,000 litres of water on the fire in the first two days, drawing it from the Maas in giant buckets containing 7,600 litres.

Efforts to contain the fire have been complicated by the fact that the area contains unexploded Second World War munitions, which bomb disposal specialists have had to make safe.

“In the next few days the fire service and [nature management service] Limburgs Landschap will focus on completely putting out the last sources of the fire. After that we can make a plan to restore this area,” Jetten said.

“I want to thank in particular everyone who has worked so hard in the last few days to deal with this crisis.”

World.title: Vollering closes in on Tour de France lead with stage five win
World.content:
Demi Vollering closed the gap on Tour de France leader Marlen Reusser to just 12 seconds as she edged out her rivals to claim victory in the fifth stage.

Vollering broke away on the final climb of the 140km stage from Mâcon to Belleville-en-Beaujolais before crossing the line just ahead of Reusser and Kasia Niewiadoma.

Reusser, who took the overall lead in Wednesday’s individual time trial, retained the leader’s yellow jersey, but Vollering reduced the Swiss rider’s lead by claiming the bonus seconds for the stage win.

The trio are the only realistic contenders left for the title after the other hopefuls, including defending champion Pauline Ferrand-Prévot, who lost two and a half minutes on the day and is back in 17th place, five minutes behind Reusser.

Dutch veteran Anna van der Breggen’s hopes of adding a Tour de France Femmes win to her four Giro d’Italia titles also appear to have been dashed after she crossed the line with Ferrand-Prévot to drop back to 12th place with a deficit of just over four minutes.

The next placed Dutch rider is Femke de Vries, Ferrand-Prévot’s team-mate at Visma Lease-a-Bike, in eighth place, 3 minutes 11 seconds back.

It is the fourth stage victory for 29-year-old Vollering in the women’s tour, which has only existed as a separate race since last year. In 2023 she won the mountain stage to Tourmalet, while the following year she won the time trial in Rotterdam and the climb to the summit of Alpe d’Huez.

“I’m so incredibly proud of this victory,” said the FDJ team leader. “Everyone in the team played their part, which makes it all the sweeter.”

On Thursday the riders will tackle the 153km stage from Montbrison to Tournon-sur-Rhône, with the high point, the 1,099m Col de Lalouvesc, coming at the 105km mark.

World.title: Two explosions at Amsterdam nursery, minors arrested
World.content:
Police have arrested two minors after a second explosive device went off at a children’s nursery in Amsterdam West within a week.

The first blast at the nursery on Bos en Lommerweg happened at around 4am on Saturday morning. The second went off at roughly the same time on Wednesday morning. Nobody was hurt and damage was limited in both cases, broadcaster NOS reported.

Officers detained the two suspects nearby shortly after the second explosion. They are being held under full restrictions, meaning they may only have contact with their lawyers and their parents.

Police said all scenarios are being examined, including whether the two incidents are connected. No motive has been established, broadcaster AT5 reported.

A nursery worker said staff had been badly shaken but that it would stay open as normal.

World.title: Dutch houseboat owners left high and dry by falling river levels
World.content:
Low water levels in the Rhine delta are causing problems for owners of Dutch houseboats, with no sign of an imminent end to the drought.

Some houseboats and static barges have been standing dry for over a month, resting on platforms that are not designed to support them out of the water or the exposed riverbed.

The Rhine sank to its lowest recorded level last week of 6.46 metres at Lobith, where it enters the Netherlands from Germany, while the flow in the river is one-third of its normal level for July because of low rainfall further upstream.

“We’ve seen these water levels more often in recent years, but usually not until September, and then it gets better after a few days’ rain,” Peter Broekmeulen, board member of the houseboat owners’ association LWO told broadcaster NOS.

The problems for dried-up houseboat owners go further than being stuck above dry land. Several homes have tilted, causing doors and windows to jam and cracks to appear in walls.

Power cables become strained and water pipes crack as they are stretched by the sinking houseboats.

But the biggest challenge is drainage, as residents have had to create improvised systems to deal with waste water that usually flows into the river.

“Open septic tank”

“When the water is there it flows away, but now they’re standing dry it ends up on the land and you get a kind of open septic tank, which is unacceptable from a public health point of view,” Broekmeulen told DutchNews.

Paul van de Veen, who has lived on Rosandepolder in Arnhem, for 40 years, told NOS: “In the early years our boat once had to be towed away by a sailing boat because the water was too high. Now we’re seeing the other side of the coin.”

Van de Veen’s house is still floating after the council dredged his side of the river in February. “We still have a margin,” he said. “The water around us is around a metre deep.”

His neighbours across the water are less fortunate. Marloes Kraal, whose houseboat is in the neighbouring municipality of Renkum, is on a section of river that dried up months ago. “We have cracks in the wall and the roof and there are more appearing,” she said.

The LWO is calling for councils to be more consistent in their policies for houseboats to avoid postcode lotteries arising. Arnhem paid the dredging of the river bank in February from public funds, but in Renkum owners have been told that removing the clay from the riverbed is their own responsibility.

“They are paying the same rent but get much less value for money,” Broekmeulen said. “Legally the council are in the right, but if one council dredges and the other doesn’t, that leads to inequalities.”

Wild west situation

“That’s the wild west situation that we’re up against. We want it to be better regulated nationally for everyone who has to deal with low water levels.”

Owners also face problems when the river levels rise again, as exposed houses can become stuck to their bases, causing them to flood rather than float.

Gert Schols, shipping expert at insurance company EOC, said: “We advise houseboat owners not to go on holiday in periods of extreme drought or arrange a housesitter. You need to keep an eye on what’s happening when the water rises.”

Without action from the government, living on Dutch houseboats risks becoming unappealing in the long term as droughts become more frequent, Broekmeulen warned: “If your house is lying off centre for six months, you’re going to start thinking about moving into one that stands upright.”

World.title: End of a cycling empire? Bike maker Accell at risk of bankruptcy
World.content:
Accell, one of the Netherlands’ biggest bicycle groups, has been granted protection from its creditors to hold off the risk of bankruptcy.

The move will give the company court-approved breathing space to try to restructure its debts but leaves its future in doubt.

It is not yet clear how this will impact people with an Accell bike, or for the shops that sell and service them. Neither the company nor the courts have said anything about warranties, spare parts, or outstanding claims from the 2024 recall of tens of thousands of bikes, which were pulled from sale over cracking frames.

Accell owns some of the most well-known names in Dutch cycling – Batavus and Sparta city bikes, Koga touring bikes, and the Babboe and Carqon cargo brands – as well as Raleigh, Lapierre, and the German marques Haibike, Winora, and Ghost. It employs around 3,700 people in 15 countries.

Four difficult years

The company was publicly listed in Amsterdam until private equity group bought it for €1.56 billion in 2022.

It has struggled ever since the covid pandemic. Demand for bikes surged during the pandemic but parts were hard to get, and by the time supply chains recovered Accell was left with a mountain of unsold stock. Revenues fell 22% in 2024 to just over €1 billion.

A series of cutbacks followed: its warehouse network was reduced from 85 sites to 28, its Turkish factory was sold, and its Heerenveen plant closed last spring, ending its bicycle manufacturing in the Netherlands. Production moved to Hungary and France.

Earlier this year Accell struck a deal with its creditors, who took ownership of the company. That was always a stopgap, and a search for a new owner began. Accell said it held talks with several interested parties, assessed a number of bids, and sought regulatory approval for a possible merger, but no workable solution emerged.

Poland’s power grid operator, PSE, has, for the second time in three days and third time this summer, invoked emergency measures to ensure supply amid an ongoing heatwave. Before this summer, it had only done so twice in the eight years since such powers were introduced. However, following a meeting with PSE and other state energy officials, Prime Minister Donald Tusk has assured Poles that, despite “a very difficult period”, the “situation is under control” and power supplies are secure, thanks in part to the growth of renewables in recent years. ❗️PSE ponownie ogłaszają okresy przywołania na rynku mocy❗️ To już 3. raz w tym roku, kiedy operator sięga po to narzędzie. W historii zdarzyło się to tylko 5 razy, wliczywszy 3 przypadki tegoroczne, co pokazuje wyjątkowość roku 2026 dla energetyki. pic.twitter.com/DbCPnpyae4 — Jakub Wiech (@jakubwiech) August 6, 2026 PSE has called on contracted electricity generators to increase output and large consumers to cut use to help balance the grid on Thursday between 5:00 p.m. and 10:00 p.m., as temperatures have this week approached 40°C (104°F) in many parts of the country. The same measures were introduced on Tuesday, as the heatwave pushed up electricity consumption, partly due to increased use of air conditioning and refrigeration. Participants in Poland’s capacity market are paid for maintaining standby capacity and fulfilling their obligations when called upon by the operator. According to PSE, the mechanism is “a remedial measure” used when the generation capacity available to the operator falls significantly below the required safety level. Previously, the measures were invoked in June this year, amid another heatwave that saw Poland hit its highest-ever recorded temperature of 40.5°C. But before that, they had only been used twice since being introduced in 2018. Temperatures in Poland have reached the highest level on record, with a figure of 40.3°C (104.5°F) recorded this afternoon, as the heatwave that has hit Europe this week moves eastwards https://t.co/eRhRxiuCGq — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 28, 2026 Poland’s weather institute IMGW issued heat warnings on Thursday for 13 of the country’s 16 provinces, with daytime temperatures forecast to reach between 33C and 38C. High temperatures and prolonged drought conditions have also pushed water levels in many rivers to extremely low levels, with the Vistula, Poland’s longest river, only 5 centimetres above the historic low of 4 centimetres it fell to in Warsaw last year. Some other parts of the river have hit all-time record lows, reports Polsat News. One result has been a disruption of cooling supplies to Poland’s power sector. State energy firm Enea this week announced reduced operations at two of its coal-fired plants that are cooled by water from the Vistula. Around 1.1 gigawatts (GW) of capacity (just over 1% of Poland’s total) has gone offline. On Wednesday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk convened a meeting of a government crisis team, including PSE’s deputy president, to discuss the current heatwave and its potential impact on the power sector. However, afterwards he assured that “the situation is under control” and that the fact that Poland now has “a lot of energy from solar panels and wind turbines makes our system relatively secure”, reports the Polish Press Agency (PAP). Poland’s renewable sector has expanded rapidly over the last decade. Last year, it provided just over 29% of the country’s power, with onshore wind supplying 14% of the energy mix and solar 12%. Renewables generated 29.4% of Poland's electricity in 2025, almost exactly the same figure as in 2024, ending a period of strong growth since 2021. Coal (52.2%) remained the dominant source, though its share declined. Poland’s top administrative court has upheld a decision by the finance ministry to withhold state subsidies from the national-conservative opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party due to campaign finance irregularities. The decision was welcomed by the government, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk saying that there will be “no money for grifters”. PiS, however, argues that the money is being withheld for political reasons and accuses the authorities of “Russian standards”. Naczelny Sąd Administracyjny oddalił w środę kasacje ws. dotacji i subwencji dla PiS. – Miażdżący dla PiS wyrok podtrzymany! – stwierdził szef MF Andrzej Domański https://t.co/bcL18WbiYf — OKO.press (@oko_press) August 6, 2026 The dispute dates back to August 2024, when the National Electoral Commission (PKW) rejected PiS’s financial report for the previous year’s parliamentary election campaign after identifying around 3.6 million zloty (€838,000) in unauthorised expenditure. As a result, the PKW ordered that PiS should lose 10.8 million zloty from the state subsidies that political parties in Poland receive based on their level of electoral support. The party would normally have received 25.9 million zloty based on its 2023 election result. The decision triggered months of legal wrangling, with PiS arguing that the funding should be restored after the Supreme Court upheld its complaint against the PKW’s decision. However, finance minister Andrzej Domański refused to release the money, saying there were unresolved legal doubts over the ruling. The finance minister has refused to comply with the electoral commission's decision to pay out subsidies to the opposition PiS party He says there are "legal doubts" over the issue. But PiS says he is obliged to pay and will be held criminally responsible https://t.co/ZwIZRqn5tp — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 9, 2025 Those doubts stem from a broader dispute over the controversial and contested judicial reforms implemented by PiS when it ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023. The chamber of the Supreme Court that ruled in PiS’s favour was created as part of those reforms. It has previously been found to not be a legitimate body by both the European Court of Justice and European Court of Human Rights because it contains improperly appointed judges. After the Supreme Court chamber’s ruling, the PKW initially said it would not recognise the decision until the chamber’s legal status was clarified. Two weeks later, however, it reversed that decision and approved PiS’s financial report. Domański still declined to restore the subsidy, arguing that the PKW’s resolution was internally contradictory. While it approved the payments, it also stated that the chamber’s ruling should come from a body recognised as a court and that it was not determining whether the chamber met that standard. PiS challenged Domański’s decision. However, its case was initially rejected by a lower court in June last year, and that decision has now been upheld by the Supreme Administrative Court (NSA), which is the final court of appeal for administrative issues. The NSA found the minister had acted lawfully in withholding the funding. It also said the Supreme Court chamber’s ruling had no legal effect because it had been issued by a body that was not a properly constituted court, reports news website OKO.press. The ruling was welcomed by Domański, who called it a “crushing blow to PiS” and said that “yet another PiS lie has been exposed”. However, PiS has always argued that the decision was a political one, implemented at the behest of the new Tusk government in order to undermine the main opposition party. After a ten-year-long investigation, prosecutors have concluded that Poland’s government in 2010 – which was led by current Prime Minister Donald Tusk – was not guilty of “diplomatic treason” in its response to the plane crash in Russia that killed President Lech Kaczyński. The national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party – which ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023 and is led by Lech’s twin brother, Jarosław – has always rejected the findings of official Polish and Russian investigations into the crash, which found it to have been an accident. Instead, PiS claims that the disaster, which claimed the lives of 96 people, many of them senior Polish state officials, was caused deliberately by Russia and then covered up with the help of Tusk’s government. However, while PiS launched various investigations during its time in power, it has never substantiated its claims. And prosecutors now say that there is no evidence that diplomatic treason, a crime that carries a potential prison sentence of up to ten years, took place. He condemned the “Smolensk liars”, such as Jarosław Kaczyński, who he suggested had exploited the tragedy for their own benefit. “They brainwashed millions of people, divided families, stirred up hatred within the nation,” he wrote. “They’ll burn in hell for it. But the power, money and satisfaction they gained from spitting on their rivals – that’s theirs.” The idea that Smolensk was an assassination of Lech Kaczyński has been a core part of PiS rhetoric. In 2022, for example, Jarosław Kaczyński said that the decision was made “at the highest level of the Kremlin” and Tusk’s government then “covered up” the incident as part of a “macabre reconciliation with Russia”. Smolensk was an “attack decided at the highest level of the Kremlin”, says Jarosław Kaczyński ahead of the 12th anniversary of the crash. Donald Tusk's government then “covered up” the incident as part of a “macabre reconciliation with Russia”, he adds https://t.co/5ae0gHJj3B — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 4, 2022 The investigation into diplomatic treason – a crime consisting of acting to the detriment of Poland while authorised to represent the country in relations with foreign states or organisations – was launched in August 2016, less than a year after PiS had come to power. Among the individuals who had formally notified prosecutors of a potential crime was PiS deputy leader Antoni Macierewicz, who from 2015 to 2018 served as defence minister. He has been the foremost proponent of conspiracy theories around the Smolensk air disaster. In their notifications to prosecutors, Macierewicz and the others accused Tusk and other officials of, in their relations with Russia, deliberately choosing a legal basis for an investigation into the crash that was unfavourable to Poland by giving it no real influence over how it was run. However, prosecutors now say that, after ten years in which they questioned 488 witnesses, gathered extensive documentation and requested legal assistance from several countries, they have “concluded that no crime of diplomatic treason was committed”. In a statement explaining the decision, the National Prosecutor’s Office said that the legal basis chosen for cooperating with Russia on an investigation – Annex 13 of the Convention on International Civil Aviation – was, in fact, “the most advantageous solution” for Poland. It ensured the participation of Polish representatives in the Russian-led investigation, including access to the wreckage and crash site. Other legal options would have offered no greater benefits and involved significant risks, concluded the Polish prosecutors. They acknowledged that Russia “subsequently failed to fulfil some of its obligations arising from the adopted procedure”, but said this should have no bearing on assessing the decisions that were previously made on setting up the investigation. The defence ministry will notify prosecutors of 41 suspected crimes linked to a commission established by the former PiS government to investigate the 2010 plane crash in Russia that killed President Lech Kaczyński https://t.co/aEAlmk9lDM — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 24, 2024 The prosecutors also found that, not only did Polish officials choose the best legal solution, but there was also “no evidence indicating that individuals authorised to act on behalf of Poland, including the prime minister and members of the Council of Ministers, acted with the intent to harm Poland”. Given that the crime of diplomatic treason requires intent, this finding further reinforced the decision to drop the investigation. However, the prosecutors note that their decision can still be appealed. At the time of writing, neither Kaczyński, Macierewicz, nor other senior PiS figures had commented on the prosecutors’ announcement. However, it is likely they will point to the fact that the current national prosecutor was appointed by Tusk’s government after it had removed the previous PiS-era incumbent in a legally questionable move. The Supreme Court has issued a ruling that effectively found that the government unlawfully replaced a senior prosecutor earlier this year However, the justice minister says the ruling has no legal force as it was issued by illegitimately appointed judges https://t.co/9fCE6d18uy — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 27, 2024 In 2020, in a separate civil case, a court ordered Jarosław Kaczyński to apologise for accusing Sikorski of “diplomatic treason” in relation to the Smolensk crash. Two years later, after Kaczyński had refused to comply with the ruling and Sikorski published the apology himself, Kaczyński was ordered to pay the costs. In 2024, an investigation by Tusk’s government found that the PiS administration had wasted tens of millions of zloty on a commission, headed by Macierewicz, that was tasked with re-investigating the Smolensk disaster. It notified prosecutors of dozens of suspected crimes relating to the functioning of the commission. Macierewicz, however, accused the government of spreading “lies and disinformation” designed to “protect Putin”. Jarosław Kaczyński has been ordered to pay 700,000 zl (€150,000) to publish an apology to ex-foreign minister @sikorskiradek. Kaczyński has yet to comply with a 2020 order to apologise for accusing Sikorski of "treason" in relation to the Smolensk crash https://t.co/o0XkTWFgDR — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 3, 2022 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. Poland has urged the European Union to adopt tougher measures in response to the recent migration crisis in Spain’s African exclave of Ceuta, including making migrants who enter the bloc illegally ineligible for obtaining residence rights. During a special meeting of EU interior ministers on Tuesday, Poland shared its own experience of dealing with “weaponised” migration from Belarus, which prompted the Polish government last year to restrict the right to asylum for people who cross irregularly. 🔵 KOMUNIKAT | Polska przedstawiła swoje stanowisko ws. migracji na nadzwyczajnym posiedzeniu Rady JHA w sprawie ostatnich wydarzeń w Ceucie 🇵🇱🇪🇺 Wiceminister spraw wewnętrznych i administracji @MaciekDuszczyk wziął udział w odbywającym się we wtorek (4 sierpnia br.)… pic.twitter.com/glfyiu5ZW3 — MSWiA 🇵🇱 (@MSWiA_GOV_PL) August 4, 2026 Last week, tens of thousands of migrants entered Ceuta, most of them by swimming there from neighbouring Morocco. Dozens died while trying to cross. Among those who managed to enter Ceuta, Spain says that the vast majority have been returned to Morocco. The incident prompted expressions of concern from many European leaders, including calls to restrict Spain’s participation in the Schengen free movement zone (despite the fact that anyone leaving Ceuta for the European mainland is subject to identity checks). Among those to speak out was Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, who on Friday called on Spain to “follow our example if Schengen is to survive”. Poland has tightened asylum laws, border procedures, and has built effective barriers on its border with Belarus, which is the eastern border of the EU. We have invested billions of euros and engaged thousands of soldiers, police officers and border guards. Spain must follow our… — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) July 31, 2026 That was a reference to Poland’s response to a crisis on its eastern border, where since 2021 Belarus has encouraged and assisted tens of thousands of migrants – mainly from Asia and Africa – to try to cross irregularly into the EU. Both Poland and the EU have accused Belarus and its ally Russia of deliberately “weaponising” migration in an attempt to destabilise European societies as part of Moscow and Minsk’s broader “hybrid threats” against the EU. Tusk noted that, in response, Poland has restricted the right to asylum, invested billions in strengthening physical and electronic barriers along the border, and has deployed thousands of soldiers, police officers and border guards there (who have also been given expanded rights to use firearms). A court has ruled that Poland's recently introduced partial suspension of the right to asylum is justified and lawful. It rejected a complaint by a Sudanese man who had been denied the right to claim asylum after crossing irregularly from Belarus https://t.co/jx3s1AxRgG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 10, 2025 On Saturday, Tusk and 21 other EU leaders jointly signed a letter expressing “serious concern” at the situation in Ceuta and warning that the EU “cannot allow uncontrolled mass border crossings, the instrumentalisation of migration, or other hybrid threats to create the impression that illegal entry…is possible”. While they welcomed Spain’s cooperation with Morocco to send most of the migrants back, they also called for an extraordinary meeting of EU interior ministers to “agree on a coordinated European response, including the rapid mobilisation of available EU instruments and the necessary support to Spain”. At that meeting, which took place on Tuesday, Poland’s interior ministry said that it had expressed the view that “illegal entry into the European Union should automatically exclude the possibility of obtaining residence permits, and therefore the possibility of permanent stay in the future”. While Poland’s statement did not mention it directly, earlier this year Spain’s government launched an amnesty that allowed undocumented migrants to apply to legalise their stay in the country. Over one million people had signed up for the scheme by the time it closed at the end of June. In its statement, Poland’s interior ministry warned that “migration must be fully controlled”, as otherwise it can “be used against the values that guide the EU”. It also called for the “official recognition of migration as a challenge directly linked to security”. It added that during Tuesday’s meeting it had “presented its own experiences with border protection in the context of the instrumentalisation and weaponisation of migration and adapting law to migration challenges”, including restrictions on asylum claims. “The example of Ceuta clearly demonstrates that absolute access to asylum is impossible to maintain in the face of such real threats,” wrote the interior ministry, which said that it “welcomed the shared perspective on migration among a growing number of member states”. In a statement of its own, the European Council noted that there had been a “common understanding of the need to continue relentlessly fighting migrant smuggling networks, to reinforce returns, to strengthen EU borders, to build deep partnerships with third countries, and to improve foresight.” It added that member states “were united in expressing strong solidarity with Spain”, appreciated its “swift and effective efforts” to deal with the crisis, and had also expressed their condolences for the people who died while attempting to cross from Morocco to Ceuta. ESPAÑA: CEUTA PIDE CERRAR LA FRONTERA POR LA LLEGADA MASIVA DE MIGRANTES DE MARRUECOS Más de mil jóvenes marroquíes se congregaron en la frontera con Ceuta para intentar ingresar al enclave español, y cientos lograron superar las barreras de protección, que en ese momento no… pic.twitter.com/Mx0LuQwMW2 — Clarín (@clarincom) July 30, 2026 When the migration crisis on its border with Belarus broke out in 2021, Poland recorded almost 40,000 attempted illegal crossings that year. Despite efforts to discourage and prevent crossings, the figures remained high, with just under 30,000 attempted crossings recorded in each of 2024 and 2025. However, those figures have fallen dramatically this year, with only 235 attempted crossings recorded in the first half of 2026. Meanwhile, the estimated number of successful crossings has been falling, from 12,000 in 2023, to 5,000 in 2024, 1,700 in 2025, and zero in the first half of this year, according to the Polish interior ministry. Last August, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen visited Poland’s border with Belarus, where she thanked the Polish authorities for defending Europe from “cynical hybrid attacks” orchestrated by Belarus and Russia. The number of attempted illegal crossings by migrants from Belarus to Poland fell from 15,500 in the first half of 2025 to 235 this year – a drop of over 98% Poland also now claims a 100% success rate in apprehending migrants who manage to cross illegally https://t.co/RFZkd7CeIk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 20, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Unexploded WWII ordnance discovered under busy Warsaw street
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Part of central Warsaw was shut down today after unexploded ordnance from World War Two was found buried under a major road during construction work. The discovery, which came just days after the city commemorated the anniversary of its wartime uprising against Nazi-German occupation, led to traffic being diverted and residents being warned to stay away from their windows and avoid going outside while bomb disposal experts worked to safely remove the item. W Al. Solidarności znaleziono niewybuch, najprawdopodobniej z czasów II wojny światowej. ℹ️ Czytaj więcej: https://t.co/Fv6oe84XiM pic.twitter.com/BfjQPZveYZ — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 4, 2026 The object, reportedly around 70 centimetres long, was found early on Tuesday morning on Solidarity Avenue, a major thoroughfare, during modernisation work on tram lines. “We were digging a trench and I literally just touched it with the tip [of my digger],” the operator of the excavator who found it told broadcaster TVN. Staff working at the site were immediately evacuated to a safe distance. Police later confirmed that the item is unexploded ordnance, and that initial findings indicate it dates from World War Two. Bomb disposal experts arrived at the scene in the afternoon. However, they have not confirmed precisely what type of ordnance was discovered or its origin, reports Polsat News. Warsaw was the site of major fighting during World War Two, beginning in 1939, when Nazi Germany invaded and occupied Poland. In 1943, the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, the largest single act of Jewish resistance during the war, took place. On 1 August 1944, the Polish underground Home Army launched the Warsaw Uprising, which was the largest single act of armed resistance anywhere in German-occupied Europe during the war. In response, the Germans destroyed much of the city, around 85% of which lay in ruins by 1945. Warsaw’s historic Old Town was meticulously rebuilt after the war. But many other parts of the city were redeveloped by the newly installed communist authorities, including Solidarity Avenue (which during the communist era was named after Polish-Soviet Red Army General Karol Świerczewski). Thousands of vehicles drove over the unexploded ordnance every day for decades. “Warsaw is marked by history, and there are many such surprises,” Witold Urbanowicz, spokesman for the city’s tram operator, told news website Interia. After the fall of the Warsaw Uprising – which began 80 years ago today – the German occupiers expelled the city's entire population. However, some survivors decided to remain among the ruins. They became known as "Robinson Crusoes" and this is their story https://t.co/UuVbfbcpQ4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 1, 2024 Unexploded ordnance is regularly found in Poland. In May this year, around 200 anti-personnel mines dating from World War Two were discovered at the construction site of a student dormitory at Kraków’s Jagiellonian University. In October last year, two men were hospitalised after an artillery shell that one of them had brought home from a forest exploded in his apartment while the pair were under the influence of alcohol. Earlier that year, wild boars unearthed 21 mortar shells buried in a forest since the war. In 2023, 72 unexploded artillery shells were discovered during renovation work at a primary school and four pieces of World War Two ordnance were found in the walls of a church undergoing renovation. Wild boars dug up 21 mortar shells from World War Two that had been buried in a Polish forest. The unexploded ordnance has now been safely removed without harm to either the animals or humans https://t.co/W9kaPr1BNw — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Russia condemns Poland’s “sacrilegious” demolition of Soviet monument
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Russia has criticised the demolition of a Soviet-era monument in Poland, calling the decision “sacrilegious” and a “flagrant violation” of an agreement between the two countries on respecting places of remembrance. However, Poland’s state Institute of National Remembrance (IPN), which financed the demolition, says that the monument was a “Soviet propaganda object” that was removed under a law requiring the “decommunisation” of public spaces. On Friday, around 150 residents in Pyrzyce, a town of 12,000 in northwestern Poland, gathered to watch the demolition of a monument to the Red Army that had stood there for decades. Initially, a memorial had been established in the town alongside a cemetery for Red Army soldiers in the immediate aftermath of World War Two, when the Soviets had driven the Nazi German occupiers out of Poland but then introduced a new communist government of their own. However, the soldiers’ remains were later moved to a military cemetery elsewhere in the region and the monument itself was redesigned and moved to another location within Pyrzyce. Its final form, created in 1984, was a huge rectangular concrete structure weighing several hundred tons and featuring a relief depicting the head of a Soviet soldier. A plaque said “Eternal glory to the fallen heroes 1941-1945” (a timeline that ignores the Soviet invasion and occupation of parts of Poland in 1939). Such Soviet monuments remained in many Polish towns and cities long after the fall of communism in 1989. In 2016, the then-ruling national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government introduced a law requiring local authorities to “decommunise” public spaces by removing objects and names that “propagate communism”. However, only in 2022, after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, did the removal of Soviet-era monuments gather pace, with dozens demolished since then. Those efforts were led by the IPN, in particular during the time that the institute was headed by Karol Nawrocki between 2021 and last year, when he was elected president of Poland. Another Soviet memorial has been demolished in Poland – the 43rd since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. "We say ‘no’ to Russians who believe these lands somehow belong to their sphere of influence,” declared the Institute of National Remembrance https://t.co/aG9VQVlUQI — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 12, 2025 At the start of this year, the local authorities in Pyrzyce began public consultations on removing their Soviet memorial, finding that a majority were in favour of the move, according to the IPN. In February, the town council voted to remove the monument. It will now be replaced with a new one commemorating Polish independence. “We are aware that this change evokes various, often very strong, emotions among residents,” wrote the local authorities on social media. “We respect both the voices of those supporting the actions taken and those who differ in their assessment of the current monument and its place in the history of Pyrzyce.” “We hope that independence – as a paramount value for all Poles – will unite residents beyond differences of opinion and assessment of the past. We want the emerging space to be a space of shared remembrance, reflection, and a dignified celebration of the most important national ceremonies.” The removal of the monument drew condemnation from the Russian embassy in Warsaw, which announced on Monday that it had lodged a formal protest. It called the decision the “latest sacrilegious step by the Polish authorities” and said that it “constitutes a direct and flagrant violation” of a 1994 agreement between Poland and Russia on respect for graves and other places of memory. “The illegal dismantling of monuments is an overt attempt to falsify history, to erase from the consciousness of the Polish nation the memory of the heroism of Soviet soldiers,” added the embassy. ⚡️Komentarz Ambasady Rosji w Polsce 31 lipca 2026 r. w Pyrzycach (województwo zachodniopomorskie) na podstawie decyzji władz polskich został przeprowadzony demontaż pomnika ku czci poległych w latach 1941–1945 bohaterów – żołnierzy radzieckich. ❗️Ten kolejny świętokradczy krok… pic.twitter.com/cKhfFxIL9s — Russian Embassy, PL (@rusemb_pl) August 3, 2026 In response to such complaints from Russia, Poland has regularly pointed out that the 1994 agreement relates to graves and war cemeteries, not separate monuments and symbols, which can be legally removed. The IPN notes that such monuments were “Soviet propaganda objects”, designed to support the Moscow-backed communist regime, rather than genuine places of commemoration. Attending the demolition ceremony in Pyrzyce on Friday, IPN deputy president Karol Polejowski pointed out that the final version of the monument had been established in 1984 shortly after the period of martial law in Poland, when the authorities brutally clamped down on the democratic opposition. “Local communist activists, eager to curry favour with their Soviet masters, erected a monument honouring the Soviet army. This is not a symbol of liberation – it is a symbol of enslavement!” he declared, as the monument was torn down. 💪 Sowiecki obiekt propagandowy zostanie zastąpiony przez Pomnik Niepodległości, a przestrzeń wokół nowego monumentu stanie się godną sceną dla uroczystości patriotycznych. pic.twitter.com/5x4KEzG3Vb — Instytut Pamięci Narodowej (@ipngovpl) July 31, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland’s WIG20 stock market index hits record high
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s blue-chip WIG20 stock market index hit its highest ever level on Monday, surpassing a record that had stood for almost 19 years. The WIG20 has been Europe’s best-performing major blue-chip index so far this year. According to market monitoring website MarketScreener, the index has gained just under 25% since the start of 2026, ahead of the Dutch AEX (16.9%) and Sweden’s OMX Stockholm (14.9%). The WIG20, which tracks the 20 largest and most liquid companies on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (GPW), climbed to 3,963.21 points on Monday, breaking its previous record of 3,940.53 points set in October 2007. It continues a rally that began in October 2022, since when the index has almost tripled in value. “The market continues to be supported by solid economic growth, rising consumer spending, and the prospect of further EU investment,” commented analysts from BNP Paribas, a bank, quoted by business daily Parkiet. “However, after such strong gains, we do not expect the pace of appreciation to remain as high as in recent years,” they added. On Monday, the biggest boosts to the WIG20 index were provided by PGE, Poland’s biggest power producer, and KGHM, a Polish multinational mining company, with their shares rising 3.3% and 1.6%, respectively. The surge was also supported by improving risk appetite across global markets following signs of a de-escalation in tensions in the Middle East. This has pushed WIG20 above the levels last seen 19 years ago, just before the index plunged almost 70% during the 2008 global financial crisis, and then suffered another sell-off during the euro zone debt crisis in 2011. Reform of one of the pillars of Poland’s pension system in 2014, which reduced the role of open pension funds, ushered in years of market stagnation and left the index struggling to meaningfully rebound in the following years. Another decline came during the COVID-19 pandemic and then in the aftermath of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. In October 2022, however, the WIG20 started its rebound, rising by 195% since then. More than 30 Polish-listed companies have doubled in value over the past three years, including large-cap stocks such as Orlen, PKO BP, Bank Pekao, KGHM and Tauron, according to an analysis by economic journalist Rafał Hirsch published by news service WNP. Polish state energy firm Orlen has seen its market valuation rise to its highest ever level, and surpass Russia’s Gazprom for the first time https://t.co/w3po4izshJ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 12, 2026 BNP Paribas’s analysts, however, note that, “despite a long-term upward trend and reaching record highs”, the Polish stock market “is still valued below many other European markets”. “Our stock market…remains significantly cheaper than the US market and most European markets, but at the same time, when viewed against its own historical performance, it is now relatively highly valued,” they said. Poland’s main stock index, the broader WIG, also closed on Monday at a record high of 148,428 points, having hit several records in recent months. Poland’s benchmark WIG stock index has passed the 100,000-point mark for the first time. Meanwhile, the Warsaw Stock Exchange has been the world’s best performing so far this year "It is a clear signal of the strength of our economy," says the PM's office https://t.co/fIgGWOLLn8 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 25, 2025 Analysts warn, however, that unlike in the case of WIG, the WIG20’s record may prove short-lived because the benchmark is a price index, which excludes dividends. When companies in the index pay dividends, their share prices usually fall by about the same amount, which automatically pulls the index down even if nothing has changed in the companies themselves. Monday was the last day investors could buy shares in PKO BP and qualify for this year’s dividend. From Tuesday, the bank’s shares will trade ex-dividend, a move expected to reduce the WIG20 by about 0.8% because of PKO BP’s large weighting in the index.
