World.title: Kosovo Serb Businessman and Politician Radoicic Indicted for War Crimes
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip



Milan Radoicic. Photo courtesy of N1.

Kosovo’s Special Prosecution on Thursday said it has filed an indictment charging 20 people it suspects of committing war crimes against civilians in the western town of Gjakove/Djakovica during 1999.

BIRN has learned that Milan Radoicic, a well-known Kosovo Serb businessman and politician, is among the suspects.

The prosecution said that, according to the indictment, during the 1998-1999 war in Kosovo, the suspects, operating in different capacities of the Serbian Interior Ministry, “are accused of participating in the killing of 107 civilians during a large-scale military-police operation.

“During this operation … the defendants initially separated the women and children from the men. The women were robbed, taking their gold jewellery, money and other valuables, while the men were executed, some in their homes and yards, some at a location known as ‘Taliqi Bridge’. The houses were also burned,” the Prosecution added.

It proposed a trial in absentia for the defendants since they are all out of reach of Kosovo’s authorities.

In April 2025, the Pristina Basic Court issued an arrest warrant for Radoicic and 19 others suspected of war crimes in May 1999 in Gjakova/Djakovica.

The court said the Special Prosecution was investigating suspicions that from May 7 to May 10, 1999, the suspects were among uniformed Serbian military and police forces who “entered houses and using force and threats took everyone present out of their homes and separated the men from women and children. Later they killed 106 civilians of Albanian nationality.

“After the war, their bodies were found in a mass grave in Batajnica in Serbia,” the court added.

The court said it suspected that Radoicic and the 19 others “arrested and imprisoned 300 other civilians from the Albanian community and other ethnic communities, who were first kept in improvised prisons” and treated inhumanely.

Many of these prisoners were transferred to prisons in Kosovo and eventually to Serbia, to be released after June 1999 with the assistance of the international community, the arrest warrant notes.

“All the Albanian civilians and civilians and of other nationalities who lived in Gjakova were barred from their home via force and threats. First, all the houses of Albanians in Gjakova were robbed and then burned, causing material damage,” it added.

The court noted that the suspects do not have addresses in Kosovo and are not accessible to the Kosovo authorities.

Charged multiple times

Radoicic is well known to the Kosovo authorities. They have charged him with multiple crimes, or listed him as the main suspect a number of times, but have not so far been able to bring him to court.

Together with 42 individuals, he was charged with terrorism and endangering the constitutional order of Kosovo over the attack by armed Serbs on a police patrol in the Kosovo village of Banjska in September 2023, which left one police officer dead.

Only three Kosovo Serbs have been arrested related to the attack. They have pleaded not guilty. Radoicic, who since fled to Serbia, took responsibility for leading the assault but insisted he did so without informing the authorities in Belgrade.

At the time of the attack, Radoicic was deputy leader of Srpska Lista, the main Serb party in Kosovo, which operates closely in line with Serbia’s government,

Serbia launched an investigation into Radoicic in September 2023, when the Belgrade Higher Prosecutor’s Office said it was probing him for organising an armed group, the unauthorised amassing of a large cache of weapons, which he transported to Kosovo, and for “serious crimes against general security”.

Belgrade prosecutors questioned him in October 2023, when he reportedly claimed innocence.

In April 2024, the Kosovo authorities seized most of Radoicic’s property in the country.

Prosecutors there also implicated him in a corruption scam in Brezovica in the Sharr Mountains National Park. He narrowly avoided arrest in 2022 when he tried to cross from Serbia into Kosovo, but turned back at the last second.

Commenting at the time on the warrant issued against him, Radoicic suggested he was a victim of a campaign against Serbs in Kosovo.

Radoicic was earlier named as the main leader of the criminal group that organised the murder of the Kosovo Serb politician Oliver Ivanovic, in 2018, together with businessman Zvonko Veselinovic. The men were never charged.

In an interview with BIRN a few months before his murder, Ivanovic named Radoicic as the real power-holder in the Serb-majority north of Kosovo.

World.title: Bulgarian Man Killed After Being Lured to Meet Teenager, Police Say
World.content:
Plovdiv’s historic old town area. Photo: Wikimedia Commons/Klearchos Kapoutsis.

Police in Bulgaria’s second biggest city, Plovdiv, said on Thursday that they have made eight arrests over the death of a man who was lured by teenagers to a meeting with “a 17-year-old girl, posing as a 15-year-old” and then severely beaten up.

Police told a press conference that the teenagers had concocted a scheme to track, lure and then attack alleged paedophiles, and then livestream the beatings.

Their victim, who was assaulted on Tuesday at a site near Youth Hill, a location near many of the tourist sights close to the centre of Plovdiv, has been named as Georgi Kuzev.

After being assaulted, Kuzev was discovered by passers-by and taken to hospital. Nova TV said he had suffered a severe brain injury and various fractures. He died several hours later.

The incident was initially reported by media as having potentially been a homophobic attack, after other such attacks in Plovdiv in 2020, sparking outrage from LGBTQ+ rights groups.

But the announcement at Thursday’s police press conference caused a U-turn in speculation around the case.

Atanas Kalchev, mayor of Krichim, a small town near Plovdiv, said the victim was originally from Krichim.

“The case is extremely serious and is characterised by a high degree of public danger due to the cruelty of the crime committed,” Kalchev said in a statement on Wednesday before the police announced the circumstances of the attack.

“Even if the initial theories [about a homophobic attack] don’t get confirmed, this doesn’t take away from the weight of the crime,” Kalchev added.

World.title: Romanians Urged to Use Less Electricity in Heatwave as Danube Levels Drop
World.content:
The Romanian government on Thursday urged households and businesses to reduce electricity consumption between 7 p.m. and 11 p.m. until the end of the month, to ease pressure on the power system during the ongoing heatwave.

“Keeping electricity consumption as low as possible during the evening hours will not affect essential services, such as healthcare,” Romania’s interim Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan said.

“We are going through a difficult period that could last another one to two weeks, and we are compelled to take these measures,” he added.

The capital, Bucharest, has already reduced street lighting by one-third in the evenings and switched off illumination at landmark buildings and museums overnight to save electricity. Other cities have introduced similar measures.

Earlier this week, the country’s largest energy-intensive companies, including car manufacturers, steel producers, fertilizer plants and other major industrial consumers, suspended operations or scaled back production to reduce pressure on the power grid.

A prolonged heatwave and record-low water levels on the Danube have forced Romania to restrict water use for agricultural irrigation, disrupting river transport, tourism and the energy sector. The authorities have also shut down one reactor at the country’s only nuclear power plant, at Cernavoda, which relies on Danube water for cooling.

Low water levels on the Danube are expected to continue affecting operations at the Cernavoda nuclear plant at least until mid-August. The government declared a nationwide energy alert on July 31, which will remain in force throughout August.

World.title: Kosovo Delays Speaker’s Election Amid Coalition Talks Uncertainty
World.content:
Vetevendosje leader Albin Kurti addresses Kosovo’s parliament in its inaugural session, August 6, 2026. Photo: BIRN.

The leader of Kosovo’s ruling party, Vetevendosje, Albin Kurti, on Thursday asked parliament for more time before proposing a name for the new speaker, after MPs elected in the June 7 polls took their oath at the assembly’s inaugural session.

Kurti, who is also caretaker Prime Minister, had been expected to submit a name for the proposed speaker, but instead called for more time “to give the talks for an agreement on a new president a chance”.

Kurti is in the midst of negotiations to form a coalition government, which also involve deciding on a name to put forward to parliament as Kosovo’s next president. If no president is installed by MPs, the country will have to hold general elections yet again, according to the constitution.

“The inauguration of parliament this time should not be [a step] towards another dissolution and snap elections, which are unjustifiable and unnecessary for citizens and harmful for the economy,” Kurti said in a short speech.

However, his announcement sparked angry reactions from opposition MPs in the chamber.

In the June elections, Kurti’s Vetevendosje Movement won 53 of the 120 seats, down four from the last December 2025 election, but well ahead of the Kosovo Democratic Party, PDK, which won 22 seats. The Democratic League of Kosovo, LDK, which is Kurti’s most likely coalition partner, won 18 seats.

A repeat of the parliamentary deadlock that paralysed the country for much of 2025, when no party had enough seats to elect parliamentary officials and form a government, has likely been avoided – but only when it comes to the election of a speaker and a government, for which the winning party needs only a bare minimum of 61 votes.

Kurti will likely obtain a simple majority to form the next government by again relying on the support of MPs from various ethnic minority communities – Roma, Ashkali, Egyptian, Turk, Bosniak – plus one of the Serb MPs.

However, the wider crisis that led to the June 7 snap elections has not been solved; the parties still need to come to an agreement to elect a new President. Failure to do this within two months of the inauguration of the new parliament would trigger another election.

The opposition PDK in a statement criticised the latest development as “a continuation of the institutional blockade by Kurti, in contradiction with the obligation set by the Constitutional Court” – which set a 30-day deadline for the election of a parliamentary leadership from certification of the election results on July 8.

“This is a sign of the lack of seriousness and responsibility from the biggest party [Vetevendosje],” Bedri Hamza, head of the PDK, said.

As his only potential partner for a coalition, Kurti has so far twice met LDK leader Lumir Abdixhiku – but without managing to get a deal on a new President.

Kurti insists the new President should be unaffiliated with any party. Abdixhiku, however, maintains that the post of head of state belongs to the LDK.

“I hope and trust that we can have a positive move during the day but it remains to be seen,” Armend Zemaj, an LDK MP, said on Thursday, after the interruption of session.

He voiced concerns about constitutional deadlines for the parliament, which cannot be considered inaugurated until the speaker and five deputies are elected.

World.title: Police Probe Homophobia Motive for Murder in Bulgarian City
World.content:
Media reports say police in Bulgaria’s second biggest city, Plovdiv, have made several arrests after man in his thirties died after apparently being lured via to a meeting via dating app then beaten up in what has been described as a “cruel” and possibly homophobic attack.

The victim was reportedly lured via a dating app to a site near Youth Hill, a location near many of the tourist sights close to the centre of Plovdiv, on Tuesday.

The man was then badly beaten and later discovered by passers-by and taken to hospital. Nova TV said he had suffered a severe brain injury and various fractures. He died several hours later.

The age of the victim has been reported by some sources as 37 and by others as 31. Some reports claimed the perpetrators were teenagers, both males and females, who livestreamed the beating on TikTok.

The name of the victims has not yet been confirmed by the authorities. However, Atanas Kalchev, mayor of Krichim, a small town near Plovdiv, said the victim was originally from Krichim.

“The case is extremely serious and is characterised by a high degree of public danger due to the cruelty of the crime committed,” Kalchev said in a statement on Wednesday.

“Even if the initial theories [about a homophobic attack] don’t get confirmed, this doesn’t take away from the weight of the crime,” he added.

Bulgarian LGBTQ+ rights NGO GLAS (Gays & Lesbians Accepted in Society) called for a “prompt, thorough and impartial investigation”.

“Investigators are examining whether the crime was motivated by hatred related to the victim’s sexual orientation,” GLAS said.

It noted that in 2023, sexual orientation was included in the Bulgarian Criminal Code as a factor in hate crimes. “If the investigation finds that the motive was indeed hatred based on the victim’s actual or perceived sexual orientation, the law should be applied to its full extent,” GLAS urged.

In 2020, there were a series of homophobic attacks in Plovdiv, also connected to young members of anti-LGBTQ+ groups.

This week’s case echoes the murder of 26-year-old Mihail Stoyanov back in 2008, who was killed in a park in Sofia. It became one of the most high-profile homophobic crimes in the country’s history and in 2022, the European Court of Human Rights censured Bulgaria over the case.

World.title: ‘Our Parents Carried us to Safety’: Disabled Kosovo Children Recall Escape in 1999
World.content:
Her father recalls: “They took my car because they liked it. It was a [Volkswagen] Golf Mk2,” he says. His disabled children were “left in the mud” by the side of the road, he adds.

“We had no wheelchairs,” Ganimete notes. “My mother and father carried us everywhere.”

One by one, Sali carried each of the children onto a village bus that was already crowded with other displaced Kosovo Albanians. “We spent the whole night in there,” he recalls.

“There must have been more than 100 people in that bus,” says Ganimete. “My father held my two brothers on his lap, and my mother held me.”

As the bus waited to leave, she watched Serbian forces separate young men from the crowd. “They took them to a garage and beat them. We could see it from the bus.”

She also remembers police demanding money and gold jewelry from refugees.

After spending the night on the bus, they were ordered to head towards Malisheva the next morning.

“When we arrived, Serbian police and paramilitaries had set up a checkpoint. I saw people being killed there. I thought: ‘This is where our lives will end,’” says Sali.

As they travelled through Kosovo, scenes of destruction unfolded around them. “We saw houses burning the entire way. We saw bodies lying by the roadside,” he adds.

A shocking memory that has stayed with him is of a young man trapped beneath his overturned tractor trailer in Rahovec: “I could hear him screaming, but nobody could help him. Today, there is a memorial to him there.”

At the border with Albania, the Serbian police became suspicious of one of Morina’s sons.

“They told me: ‘This one is wounded. Where are you taking him? He’s a KLA soldier.’ I explained that he had a disability and couldn’t walk. I pulled up his legs so they could see,, he says.

That moment remains among Ganimete’s worst memories: “I’ll never forget how my father lifted my brother to show his legs. The policeman narrowed his eyes, lowered his head, and walked away.”

“My older brother walked until he was four,” Ganimete recalls. “Then he developed a fever and was diagnosed with muscular dystrophy. My younger brother was born with the condition. I also walked until I was three or four before developing symptoms. Our other brother and sister do not have the disease.”

After being displaced from their home, their parents had to carry all three children around. “For our family, carrying us was an extra burden compared to everyone else,” she says.

Holding back tears, she says that as a child, “I often thought that maybe it would have been easier if one of us three had died, just to make things easier for our parents.

“What would life have meant for us if our father had been killed?” she asks.

Without their parents, she says, the three children could not have catered to their own most basic needs. “Our parents are irreplaceable,” she observes.

Finding refuge in Albania

World.title: Serbia’s Vucic Accused of “Vote-Buying” With Cash Pledges
World.content:
Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic has announced a set of financial payments for all adult citizens in Serbia, alongside subsidies for various groups – leaving critics wondering whether the measures are an attempt at vote-buying.

In early July, Vucic announced during an appearance on RTS that the state would likely provide financial assistance to all citizens aged 18 or older, emphasising that the funds would not come from the state budget. Two weeks later Vucic gave more detail during a Morning programme on TV Prva, announcing two payments for adults scheduled for September.

“Payments will be made to pensioners and to those entitled to benefits under the pensioners’ welfare system. Separate payments will be made to those receiving social benefits. On top of all that, we are also proceeding with this payment from the Share Fund for all adult citizens, which we would not be able to do without adding around 150 million euros from the budget,” Vucic said.

World.title: IVF for Single Women Raises New Conflict of Interest Questions for Czech PM
World.content:
Bringing IVF to single women

The ethics committee’s inconclusive discussions did not prevent Health Minister Vojtech – a member of the ruling ANO party and close ally of Prime Minister Andrej Babis – from continuing to push his draft bill and taking it to the next step for discussion.

Compared with most of Europe, Czechia’s reproductive policies remain relatively strict to this day. It is also one of the few EU member states where women without a male partner cannot access artificial insemination techniques – along with the likes of Slovakia, Poland, Lithuania and Italy – thus making them only available, on paper, to heterosexual couples.

“There is a large group of single women who are secure and would like to have a child, but they cannot legally have one in the Czech Republic,” said Nicole Mardesicova, vice-chairwoman of the assisted reproduction department at the Czech Gynaecological and Obstetrics Society.

The draft amendment, submitted on June 24 for interdepartmental consultation by Health Minister Vojtech together with the government’s human rights commissioner, Tatana Mala, would update the Act on Special Health Services, which many have long criticised as outdated. It states, for example, that “artificial insemination may be performed on a woman of childbearing age… upon a written request from the woman and man who intend to undergo this heath service together.”

In its current form, the reform would merely abolish the requirement for a man’s written permission, opening up assisted reproduction to single women and, implicitly, to lesbian couples.

It would, however, keep other regulations in their current format: only women up to 49 years old can access those services, and public health insurance only covers their reimbursement for women under 40 and for a limited number of attempts.

Based on the Health Ministry’s proposal, women making the request alone would, however, not be covered by health insurance and should cover the costs on a self-pay basis regardless of age or number of attempts. This, in turn, raises another question on whether the access will be de-facto reserved for wealthier women who can afford it.

“There are women who, for various reasons, do not have a partner. What is important to me is that they are here, they are interested, and I do not think that the state should prevent them from having a child if they are able to take care of it,” reasoned Vojtech.

“Moreover, the need to have a partner is already being circumvented: they can come with any acquaintance or friend who declares themselves as their partner, and the centre providing artificial insemination has no way of verifying this,” he added.

World.title: Estonian defense tech firm Hevi Optronics to build new factory near Tallinn
World.content:
Estonian tech firm Hevi Optronics is building a new factory near Tallinn, anticipating expansion within the defense sector.

Hevi Optronics develops and manufactures electro-optical intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance systems, including drone countering systems.

The new building, to be erected in Tabasalu, just west of Tallinn, will not only increase production volume but also create the capacity to develop, test and mass-produce new products, the company says.

Hevi Optronics' production manager, Lauri Valdmann, said the changed security situation in Europe has created a significant need to expand defense capabilities. "At the same time, we do not view the investment in the new production facility solely in the context of the current geopolitical situation. Electro-optical systems are becoming increasingly important on various platforms on land, at sea and in the air," Valdmann said.

Valdmann noted the company has grown very rapidly in recent years, adding its production and development facilities, currently spread across several buildings, had hampered further development. "We will bring all our development and production capabilities together under the one roof in the new building. In addition to assembling electronics and systems, we will significantly boost our in-house precision mechanics manufacturing capacities, and create a more modern testing and development environment," Valdmann continued.

With the expansion will come job creation, primarily in production and engineering positions, Valdmann added. "We need more mechanical, electronics and software engineers, production and quality specialists, CNC workers, and people involved in system assembly and testing."

Modern unmanned systems, surveillance solutions and other defense platforms require increasingly advanced sensors, stabilization, image processing and automation, the company says, adding a long-term need has emerged in Europe to expand local defense industry production capacities and reduce dependence on supply chains beyond Europe.

Hevi Optronics mostly exports, but the primary focus of its future growth is Europe. The company's customers and partners are system integrators whose solutions incorporate the electro-optical systems and components developed and manufactured by Hevi Optronics.

At the same time, the domestic market is important too, Hevi says, including the overall defense industry ecosystem.

Hevi Optronics last year reported a nearly three-fold sales revenues growth to €27.15 million, compared with €9.94 million in 2024. The company currently employs more than 30 people.

The Tabasalu plant was designed by Kontsept Arhitektuuribüroo, and Mapri Ehitus is the primary construction contractor.

World.title: Study: Estonia's unique trilingual emergency alerts are speeding up
World.content:
Estonia's location-based SMS alert system is unique in the world in being able to reach users in three different languages, depending on their preference.

Improvements to the system in the past year or so have made these warnings get delivered to phones quicker, and usually in the recipient's language of choice – out of three options.

Previously, emergency alerts in Estonia were sent as a single SMS message, usually in three languages: Estonian, Russian and English.

While this trilingual message helped reach different language groups, it also created issues which could be serious in a real emergency, according to a new study by Stella Polikarpus, a population protection researcher at the Estonian Academy of Security Sciences (Sisekaitseakadeemia).

The messages were found by many to be too long, hard to read, and their length meant they also took a longer time to deliver. Also, the alerts were often split across several SMS segments, increasing the load on mobile networks and further delaying the delivery of warnings, and making them more complex for end users to digest.

Kadi Luht-Kallas, project manager for the EE-ALARM language preference project, noted: "Testing and research on emergency alert language preferences carried out in 2022 and 2023 showed that trilingual SMS alerts were too long and difficult to grasp in emergency situations, reducing their effectiveness. We needed a solution that takes people's language preferences into account."

Language plays an vital role in emergencies. If the public do not understand the content of a warning, it naturally can reduce their ability to respond in time. It is also vital the language in question is accurate. According to Luht-Kallas, automatic translation can also convey the content of an emergency alert incorrectly.

The language of emergency alerts is particularly important in Estonia given the multilingual nature of the populace, both citizens and residents. In addition to Estonian, Russian and English are widely spoken. Receiving a warning in a single language helps reduce confusion and speeds up understanding of the information.

The new solution takes language preferences into account.

Polikarpus' study, published in the International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction, is based data from the nationwide emergency alert test conducted on May 14, 2025. During the exercise, SMS alerts were sent twice, to nearly 1.5 million SIM cards. This was also the first nationwide emergency alert test to include sirens.

SMS and app threat notification alert tests are accompanied by siren warnings. The public is given advance warning that the tests are going ahead, and are encourage to provide feedback to the kriis.ee site. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

A total of 24,787 people responded to a feedback questionnaire published on the website kriis.ee.

Since 2023, Estonia has been developing the EE-ALARM emergency alert system, which allows warnings to be sent in a person's preferred language. Language preference is first and foremost determined using mobile operator data. If the operator has no information on the user's language of choice, the user will receive a dual-language message in Estonian and English. Such cases accounted for 14 percent of the 2025 test, though this proportion has fallen this year.

"The share of people whose language preference is unknown has been falling over time. For example, in the 2026 test they accounted for only about 7-8 percent of SMS recipients," Luht-Kallas noted.

This solution significantly reduces message length and consequently the number of SMS segments, improving readability and speed. The trials conducted in May last year showed that the alerts were delivered successfully. Almost everyone, at 97.8 percent of respondents, said they had received the text message.

While sirens and mobile apps also attracted people's attention, 68.3 percent of respondents said they noticed the SMS before these.

The technology also overcame language barriers effectively, with 95.6 percent of respondents saying they were able to read the key information immediately in their preferred language. The speed of alert delivery also improved significantly. Under the previous trilingual system, sending the same number of messages would have taken several hours and required nearly 12 million SMS segments. With the new system, the alerts reached people in about 40 minutes, using 2.4 million SMS segments.

A comparison with other emergency alert channels, including mobile apps, television and sirens, showed that SMS remained the channel most frequently spotted first by respondents. Also, according to the authors of the study, a location-based SMS alert system that takes language preferences into account is unique in the world.

At the same time, the study also highlighted areas for further development. The accuracy of the system depends on how up to date users' language preference data are. The biggest problems were seen when sending SMS messages to phones using foreign SIM cards, as the system often could not confirm whether roaming users had received the messages.

Alert sent in March stating a drone threat had passed. This was a real-life alert and not a test. Source: EE-ALARM

The study also examined cell broadcast tech, which would enable emergency alerts to be delivered more quickly and allow danger areas to be defined more precisely. According to the authors, however, the solution still requires further development, and even with the introduction of the new technology, it must be ensured that alerts continue to reach people in their preferred language.

The researchers have concluded that EE-ALARM should continue to be developed, including by expanding the range of emergency alert channels and improving the quality of language preference data. This would ensure that warnings reach residents quickly, and in a language they understand.

The original study by Stella Polikarpus is here.

The May 14, 2025 test was the first of its kind in Estonia, and further similar tests have been carried out, with issues arising being addressed. The most recent of these tests came in June. Incidents involving stray drones during Ukraine's strikes on Russian infrastructure in the spring also brought real-time opportunities to test the system. The alert system can cover all types of emergencies including, for instance, natural disasters.

World.title: Inventor of the snail trap: nine 3D printers in the garage make the trap houses
World.content:
Local resident Hendrik Võrno of Viimsi Parish was overwhelmed by Spanish slugs overrunning his garden, so he designed a trap that lures them in and feeds them poison. Demand for his invention has grown so quickly that nine 3D printers now run in his garage to keep up with orders.

"For me, it all began four years ago when we moved to Viimsi and I had heard that there were a lot of slugs here, but it seemed exaggerated. At some point I stepped onto my terrace and discovered that all my beautiful petunias were completely dead. When I lifted the edge of the plant, I found the pot full of slugs and everything eaten," Võrno recalled.

Investigating further, he found slime trails everywhere. "Especially in the corners of the garden, in shadier spots, there were slugs in thick numbers. We're talking about hundreds of slugs across the property," Võrno added.

Alternative to expensive solution

At first, Võrno tried killing the slugs with poison. "But it's quite expensive and you need a lot of poison. At peak times, it could cost 130–150 euros a month. I started looking for alternatives to serve the poison in smaller quantities than just scattering it in the garden, and so that birds and rain wouldn't destroy it."

The solution was a bait house for slugs. "The trap works so that the inner cylindrical part holds a mixture of dry yeast and sugar, which starts to ferment due to moisture, and that smell attracts the slugs inside. A lower‑rimmed container holds the slug poison. The slug comes for the smell, puts its head through the door, and since it can't see much, it eats everything it encounters. It fills its stomach with poison and goes on its way," Võrno explained.

The inventor made an Instagram video to bring viewers to his channel, but dozens of people began writing to him wanting the trap for themselves. "Forty‑eight hours later I had a company. I started with one printer and today I have nine 3D printers. Orders come from all over Estonia," Võrno said.

Placing the trap correctly

One house is not enough. "I always recommend placing them around the perimeter at about five‑meter intervals, because you don't want them entering your garden at all. It only works if you're willing to put in the effort and deal with it."

Inside the trap, Võrno places a bait mixture, then the lid goes on. "You place the trap, and finally you drive a stake through the lid into the ground. The stake keeps the box in place and the lid on," Võrno explained. "So hedgehogs, birds and other animals can't reach the contents."

At peak season, Võrno adds bait every three to four days. "Some traps are visited less. Slugs have paths where they move more."

Võrno works daily with electric vehicles, and 3D printing has helped him for a long time. Before making snail traps, he used a 3D printer to quickly prototype something or make a tool.

Now nine 3D printers in his garage produce the trap houses. "If everything runs smoothly and there are no problems, 150 traps a day is doable. But you won't get rich with this business," Võrno said.

World.title: Banned sex crimes database creators have little faith in ministry's criminal records reform
World.content:
Content creator Mallukas, whose self-created public criminal registry was shut down by the state, said she has little faith in the Ministry of Justice's plans to reform the criminal records database.

Justice Minister Liisa Pakosta (Eesti 200) said that direct links to criminal records often made it possible to identify victims, leading to their revictimization.

"Because the full case description was also published, victims were often identifiable through those details. Unfortunately, the overwhelming majority of these cases involve domestic violence or offenses between relatives or acquaintances," Pakosta said.

"Imagine a victim's name suddenly becoming public for anyone to see and browse. Failing to take victims' basic needs into account led to victims contacting victim support services while experiencing suicidal thoughts," she added.

In April, Pakosta proposed making the state's criminal records database more user-friendly. The draft legislation containing the changes is expected to enter the interagency review process soon and be submitted to the Riigikogu this fall. Among other things, it would make employers' background checks on employees automatic.

"The issue arose after the Ihaste equestrian center failed to carry out the criminal records check required by law on a man volunteering there. The Child Protection Act requires employers to check the criminal records of anyone who will have contact with children," Pakosta said.

"That is a legal obligation. What we're proposing is simply an easier way for employers to comply by allowing the checks to be automated," she explained. Pakosta said the changes would also add ID document photos to the records of people convicted of serious crimes and review the fee charged for criminal record searches.

Content creator Mallu Mariann Treimann-Legrant, who launched the website ettevaatust.ee, said she has little faith in the minister's proposal.

"I know exactly how long it takes the state to get things done, how much time it takes and how many obstacles there are. My husband built ettevaatust.ee in a single day. We'll see how many years it takes the state to do this, and I don't think it actually ever will," Treimann-Legrant said.

"I think some enthusiasts — ordinary citizens — will get there first again. Making all of this so complicated is, in effect, protecting pedophiles," she said. She also criticized what she described as the lack of transparency and consistency surrounding the publication of personal data.

"It's worth asking who exactly the state is protecting here, because, interestingly, all these other registries that likewise disclose people's personal data remain freely accessible," she added.

The website ettevaatust.ee compiled profiles of people convicted of sexual offenses and domestic violence, allowing users to view information about offenders through direct links to the national criminal records database. On Tuesday, web hosting provider Zone disabled access to the site, which was created by blogger and content creator Mallukas, whose legal name is Mallu Mariann Treimann-Legrant, and her husband, Tomas Märten Legrant, following an order from the Data Protection Inspectorate (AKI).

World.title: Tiny quake near island off Estonian coast reveals seismic fault in bedrock
World.content:
A magnitude 0.5 earthquake near Naissaar on Monday turned out to be a rare natural tremor, revealing the seismic behavior of granite buried beneath Northern Estonia.

The waters off the coast of Tallinn and around Naissaar are well known to Estonian geologists and seismologists. As the Estonian Navy regularly discovers and safely detonates old wartime sea mines still littering the Gulf of Finland, seismic signals in the area are often assumed to be caused by humans.

Monday's tiny quake, however, was recorded just off of Naissaar at 5:21 a.m., well outside typical detonation hours.

After the Navy confirmed no explosions had taken place, Estonian seismologists analyzed the data with colleagues in Helsinki and concluded the event was natural.

According to the Estonian Geological Survey (EGT), the earthquake originated in rapakivi granite buried beneath Estonia's sedimentary rock. The ancient granite, formed deep inside long-extinct volcanoes, is known to fracture relatively easily when geological stresses build up.

Epicenter of the 0.5-magnitude quake. August 3, 2026. Source: Heidi Soosalu

Such granite can be found below Southeastern Finland, where the Wiborg rapakivi granite batholith extends east well beyond the border with Russia and small, shallow earthquakes occur relatively often.

Unlike Estonia's larger historic earthquakes, these events tend to happen in clusters and are caused by the granite itself fracturing under stress rather than by a sudden release of tectonic energy along a major fault.

"We haven't observed this type of event in Estonia before, even though the same rapakivi granite lies beneath our feet," said EGT seismologist Heidi Soosalu.

Million times weaker than record Osmussaar quake

Estonia's strongest recorded earthquake to date was a magnitude 4.5 event off the northwestern coast, near the island of Osmussaar, in 1976.

That quake, which could be felt in Estonia, Finland and even Sweden, resulted from tectonic stresses transmitted across Northern Europe as the Eurasian and North American plates continue to slowly move apart beneath the Atlantic Ocean.

The 0.5-magnitude Naissar quake as recorded by three seismic stations in Paldiski, Hiiumaa and Pärnu County. August 3, 2026. Source: Heidi Soosalu

"The Osmussaar earthquake released a full million times more energy than this Naissaar event," Soosalu said, adding that earthquakes that strong are extremely rare in the Baltic Sea region.

Monday's quake occurred only about 3 kilometers below the surface. While Estonia's modern network of seismic stations picked up the tremor, it was far too weak to be felt by humans, even directly above the epicenter.

In general, people begin noticing earthquakes only when magnitudes approach 1.

While not dangerous, scientists say events like the Naissaar quake are still valuable because they reveal hidden fracture zones beneath Estonia's thick sedimentary layers. Each precisely recorded tremor also helps improve maps of the country's bedrock.

"Unexpected bits of information like this may one day help us locate mineral resources or better understand how potentially hazardous geological processes work elsewhere," Soosalu added.

World.title: Economists warn of uneven demand as Estonia's manufacturing declines
World.content:
The decline in industrial production in June was driven mainly by reduced output in shipbuilding and ship repair, electronics manufacturing, food production and the furniture industry, says Swedbank chief economist Tõnu Mertsina.

In June, the growth of sales revenue in manufacturing also slowed — in the first half of the year, sales revenue increased by one percent, but compared with last year's growth, this was a significantly weaker result, Mertsina noted.

According to Statistics Estonia, industrial companies produced 4.6% less output in June 2026 at constant prices than at the same time last year. Statistics Estonia lead analyst Riin Kadarik noted that manufacturing output decreased for the fifth consecutive month. "The largest manufacturing activity, wood processing, fell by 2%. In June, food production also declined again, decreasing by 3.3%."

Mertsina said that changes in manufacturing output in recent quarters have not aligned with the value added recorded for the sector in GDP.

"In the first quarter, despite stagnant manufacturing output, the growth of value added in GDP terms was strong and accounted for more than half of all value added created in the economy," Mertsina said.

Põltsamaa kurkide purki Panemine Autor/allikas: Olev Kenk/ ERR

Overall confidence shows improvement

Although confidence among Estonian industrial companies has not changed in recent months, compared with the beginning of the year it still shows improvement, and confidence is also much stronger than a year ago, he noted. For example, assessments of orders and expectations for output volume have improved.

"Manufacturing companies in the euro area as a whole have also become more optimistic," Mertsina said.

Although moderate recovery is visible in European manufacturing, demand remains uneven, and investment decisions continue to be affected by geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions and uncertainty about the global economic outlook.

"Uncertainty in trade policy and companies' desire to increase inventories amplify these effects. Tariffs and possible new trade restrictions have pushed companies to reorganize production and supply chains and to bring imports forward, adding extra pressure on logistics systems," Mertsina added.

According to him, European companies increasingly prefer to diversify suppliers, increase inventories and bring part of production closer to end markets, which improves security of supply but often means higher production costs.

"Estonian manufacturing operates in an environment where competitiveness depends not only on productivity and labor costs but increasingly on the ability to adapt to rapidly changing global conditions. The strength of Estonian industrial companies lies in flexibility, export experience and the ability to adjust quickly," Mertsina said.

Mait Palts. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

Palts recommends companies invest in long‑term strategy

Director General of the Estonian Chamber of Commerce and Industry Mait Palts said that companies succeed in export markets when they make long‑term plans and follow through on them.

"A great deal comes down to consistent work and determination. Companies that are active in export markets and can invest long‑term and act strategically often end up more successful," Palts said.

According to Palts, entering export markets is more difficult for smaller companies because it involves greater risks. "Success does not appear within months but often only after a couple of years, because everything requires resources and investment certainty," he said.

Henrik Välja. Source: ERR

Välja: success comes from higher‑value products

Henrik Välja, head of the Estonian Wood Industry Association, said that shifting sales portfolios toward higher‑value products helps companies grow revenue.

Välja noted that companies need at least an equivalent business environment to that of competitors in neighboring countries to remain competitive. In his view, requirements in Estonia restrict the wood industry more than in nearby countries, increasing costs and reducing competitiveness.

"To compete in export markets, domestic restrictions cannot be significantly more extensive than in neighboring countries, but unfortunately today they are. Estonia's domestic policy plays a major role in supporting competitiveness," Välja added.

World.title: Tallinn's new route network results in technical glitches and confusion at stops
World.content:
Technical issues and missing route signs have frustrated passengers following changes to Tallinn's public transportation network that took effect on August 1.

New battery-powered trolleybuses began operating in Tallinn's public transportation system at the beginning of August, alongside network changes affecting roughly one-third of the capital's transit routes. While city officials said the first weekend passed without any major disruptions, everyday operations have highlighted shortcomings in the information available to passengers.

One public transportation user, for example, said the route information at the Vineeri stop had not been updated to reflect the new bus services. Bus No. 14 no longer stops there, having been replaced by routes 1 and 19.

"They've put up the new timetables, but the schedule for bus No. 1 makes it look like it only runs around 5 or 6 a.m., even though the app still shows the normal schedule," the resident said.

At the start of the week, bus stops along the entire length of Liivalaia tänav also lacked updated route markings.

Deputy Mayor Kristjan Jesse acknowledged that replacing the signs is a time-consuming process and asked passengers to be patient.

"There are around 500 bus stops and route maps need to be updated at roughly 1,000 stops. We placed stickers at the stops to draw attention to the fact that the route network was changing and passengers should continue to keep that in mind," Jesse said.

"Since the previous bus schedule remained in effect through the end of July, it wasn't possible to begin much earlier because that would have caused confusion. That's just the nature of a transition period. Because there are so many stops where signs need to be replaced, some work began before August 1, but some is still being completed. I believe it may still take another week or two at some stops, but we hope everything will be finished as quickly as possible. The contractors have promised they are working very actively," he added.

An articulated Tallinn city bus in the city center. Photo is illustrative. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

Beyond incomplete updates to passenger information signs, the new route network has also been affected by technical issues involving the new vehicles. Problems have included displaying route numbers on both the new trams and battery-powered trolleybuses, while drivers have also needed time to adapt to the new equipment.

"There have been some technical issues with the route number displays on the trams and trolleybuses. Some have already been resolved, while work is still ongoing on others affecting the trams. There have also been some issues with the battery-powered trolleybuses. Every new vehicle is also new for the drivers. It takes some practice and time to get used to the new vehicles, to develop the feel for operating them properly and entering the correct settings while on the route," the deputy mayor explained.

"There may still be some technical issues that need correcting, fine-tuning or adjustment, but overall things have gone well. I also have to say the drivers have done an excellent job. They've familiarized themselves with the new routes and there have been virtually no mistakes while operating on the routes," the official said.

Lack of power supply keeping electronic timetables out of stops

The city has also previously faced criticism over the lack of electronic passenger information displays at several major transit hubs, including Hobujaama and Keskturg, where passengers still cannot see real-time bus and tram departure information. Even the newly completed Bussijaam tram shelter lacks such a display.

Jesse said the main obstacle to installing the displays is inadequate electrical infrastructure. Many stops receive power only through street lighting, which is switched on after dark, meaning they do not have an independent 24-hour electricity supply.

"People sometimes see that there's electricity at a stop in the evening because the lights are on, but that power comes from the street lighting cable. During the day, power to streetlights along roads and main thoroughfares is switched off and then turned back on from a designated control point. Installing a passenger information display requires a continuous power supply at the stop," Jesse said.

Electronic bus timetable in Tallinn. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

He added that new electrical connections are being installed and systems are gradually being upgraded to address the lack of passenger information, though the process will take time.

In the coming weeks, the deputy mayor advised residents to plan their journeys carefully and check schedules at transport.tallinn.ee.

World.title: Women bikers from 25 countries gather in Estonia for WIMA rally
World.content:
Around 300 women bikers from over 20 countries, including even Australia, Japan and Curaçao, were in Pärnu this week for an international motorcycle rally.

Organized by the Estonian chapter of the Women's International Motorcycle Association (WIMA), the event attracted women motorcyclists from a wide range of ages, backgrounds, and nationalities, not to mention motorbike type preferences. As well as the bikes, the attendees got a good introduction to Estonia.

"Including Estonia, we have participants from 25 countries. Of the neighboring countries there are Lithuania, Finland, Sweden and Norway, and from farther afield the United States, Australia, Curaçao and Japan. Yesterday was Estonia Day, when we showcased Estonian food and traditional folk costumes, and Estonian folk dancers performed. We also went on an excursion to Soomaa. Tomorrow we're planning to visit Kihnu," Marju Uusküla, a WIMA Eesti member, told "Aktuaalne kaamera".

The riders crossing the new Pärnu bridge. Source: ERR

On Wednesday, the women rode in convoy from their campsite at Valgeranna, just outside Pärnu, to the town center for the parade, while they will be exploring Estonia by bike for the whole week.

For some of the riders from overseas, renting a bike was the way to go. "Our motorbikes can't go over the ocean, so we had to rent motorbikes in Latvia, in Riga," said Cheryl Woodsom, a motorcyclist from the U.S.

It was Woodsom's first time in Estonia, but after just a couple of days she said she had already been left with an extremely positive impression. "The people are so kind and generous, and when we were riding in today, I had tears in my eyes because everybody was waving excited to see people coming through, and that made me really happy."

Women riders from the WIMA rally meet in Pärnu. Source: ERR

Veteran British rider Sheonagh Ravensdale pointed out the event, held in a different country each year, had returned to Estonia.

"WIMA is now 76 years old, it was founded in America, and every year we have a rally in a different place, a different country, and this is the second in Estonia - the first time was 2017," Ravensdale said.

As for motivation, bike riding brings one a feeling of freedom and independence, Ravensdale went on. "You feel the air, and it's completely different from being in a box, so we all love it. I've ridden for 50 years and I'm still riding - we just love it.

The next WIMA meet takes place in Italy.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate continues to rise in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,523.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,520.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,530 Iraqi dinars and 1,520 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,525.5 and 1,525 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq to increase production from Kirkuk oil fields
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair announced on Thursday plans to increase oil production from the Kirkuk oilfields.

The decision intends to capitalize on a recent agreement with Turkey for exporting oil to the port of Ceyhan.

This move also aims to circumvent the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and increase Iraq’s oil exports via ports on the Mediterranean.

The instruction utilizes the recently expanded Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline deal, with the goal of increasing exports from 180,000 barrels per day to approximately 750,000 barrels per day.

Khudair stated that increasing production lays the groundwork for boosting export volumes through Turkey to 1.5 million barrels per day.

Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO) has officially partnered with British Petroleum (BP) to bolster cooperation in oil and natural gas projects in Kirkuk oilfields.

In 2025, BP reached a deal with Iraq’s North Oil Company (NOC) to develop oil fields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk, with investments projected to reach $25 billion.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s attempts to optimize energy sector investments, increase oil output, and minimize gas flaring.

The enhanced output directly addresses the Iraqi government’s growing deficit as a result of continued maritime restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

By producing more petroleum from Kirkuk, Baghdad reduces internal shipping expenses from southern fields while increasing supplies to global markets via outlets on the Mediterranean.

World.title: Iraqi Prime Minister orders higher military readiness as security tensions rise
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces Ali Al-Zaidi has directed all security and military formations to raise their operational readiness and combat preparedness, according to the Security Media Cell.

The directive aims to maintain a high state of preparedness across Iraq’s security forces through intensified training exercises and operational movements designed to strengthen national security and protect public interests.

In a statement, the Security Media Cell said the Commander-in-Chief instructed security and military forces to increase their level of readiness while conducting training exercises and field movements.

The measures are intended to ensure that all security formations remain fully prepared to carry out their assigned duties and respond to potential security developments.

According to the statement, the directive is part of ongoing efforts to maintain continuous operational readiness across Iraq’s armed forces.

The Security Media Cell said the enhanced readiness program is designed to reinforce Iraq’s security framework and improve the capabilities of military and security units.

Officials stated that maintaining high readiness contributes to:

Strengthening national security.

Preserving public stability.

Protecting Iraqi citizens.

Safeguarding public institutions and national interests.

The government has increasingly emphasized preparedness amid evolving regional security challenges.

The announcement comes during a period of elevated security concerns in Iraq following recent regional developments and heightened tensions involving armed groups.

The official statement, however, does not specify any particular threat or military operation linked to the readiness order.

Some media reports and political analysts have suggested the move may be connected to broader security developments or precautionary planning ahead of upcoming government deadlines. These assessments are analytical interpretations and were not included in the official Security Media Cell statement.

The latest directive reflects Baghdad’s continued focus on ensuring the operational effectiveness of Iraq’s security institutions.

By ordering additional training activities and maintaining high alert levels, the government aims to preserve stability while ensuring security forces remain prepared to respond to any developments affecting the country’s security environment.

World.title: Iraqi Drilling Company completes well rehabilitation at West Qurna 1 oil field
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Drilling Company (IDC) has successfully completed the rehabilitation of oil well WQ1-132 at the West Qurna 1 oil field, marking another step in Iraq’s efforts to enhance oil production efficiency and support the long-term development of its energy sector.

The project was carried out as part of the company’s operational program to improve well performance and maintain sustainable crude oil production.

According to a statement issued by the Iraqi Drilling Company, the rehabilitation work was completed in line with directives from Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair Al-Abadi and under the supervision of the company’s Director General, Mohammed Hantoosh Asad Al-Azirjawi.

Technical and engineering teams carried out the operation using the company’s specialized expertise and equipment.

The company said the rehabilitation project forms part of its broader strategy to improve the efficiency of existing oil wells while supporting sustainable production across Iraq’s major oil fields.

Restoration work on producing wells helps maximize output, extend operational life, and improve field performance without the need for entirely new drilling operations.

The Iraqi Drilling Company emphasized that the successful completion of the project reflects the capabilities of its engineering and technical staff, who continue to execute specialized rehabilitation operations according to approved operational plans.

The company noted that relying on local expertise strengthens operational efficiency while supporting the continued development of Iraq’s oil infrastructure.

West Qurna 1 is one of Iraq’s largest producing oil fields and plays a significant role in the country’s crude oil output.

Ongoing rehabilitation and maintenance projects are designed to ensure production stability, improve operational reliability, and meet the technical requirements of field development programs.

The completion of well WQ1-132 is expected to contribute to maintaining efficient production operations within the field as Iraq continues investing in the modernization of its energy sector.

World.title: Iraqi PM, Kurdistan president discuss Erbil-Baghdad cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and the president of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Nechirvan Barzani, discussed on Wednesday the country’s political, economic, and security situation.

During their meeting in Baghdad, the two leaders indicated that it is important to boost cooperation between the federal government and the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) to enhance stability, address challenges, and serve the interests of the Iraqi people, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Al-Zaidi affirmed the government’s commitment to resolving outstanding issues in line with the constitution, preserving Iraq’s unity, and strengthening national partnership.

Barzani stated that it is important to continue dialogue between national parties. He added that the KRG supports the federal government’s efforts to enhance stability and promote national development.

The discussions focused on approaches to secure the success of the government’s national agenda.

This high-level meeting comes after al-Zaidi’s trips to Turkey and Iran, where he met top officials, and Barzani’s visit to Damascus, where he met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa.

World.title: Iraq wins legal case in Jordan for Samarra Pharmaceutical Company
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Justice has announced a legal victory before the Jordanian judiciary after securing a final court ruling in favor of the State Company for Drug Industries and Medical Appliances in Samarra, a subsidiary of the Ministry of Industry and Minerals.

The ruling requires a Jordanian company to pay financial compensation following a dispute over the supply of medical materials that failed to meet agreed specifications.

According to a statement from the Ministry of Justice, the ministry’s Legal Department successfully represented the Iraqi pharmaceutical company throughout all stages of the legal proceedings before Jordanian courts.

The case involved a supply contract under which the Jordanian company was expected to provide metal covers for medical supplies. However, the supplier allegedly delivered products that did not comply with the contractual specifications.

Director of the Legal Department, Haitham Mohi Radi, said the final judgment issued by the Jordanian Court of Cassation, and upheld by both the Court of Appeal and the Court of First Instance, ordered the Jordanian company to pay financial amounts to the Samarra-based pharmaceutical company.

The ruling concludes a lengthy legal process aimed at protecting the contractual rights of the Iraqi state-owned enterprise.

The Ministry of Justice described the outcome as an important achievement in safeguarding Iraq’s financial interests abroad.

Officials said the successful litigation reflects the ministry’s continued efforts to defend state institutions before international courts and judicial authorities while protecting public funds from contractual violations.

The ministry added that the case demonstrates the expertise and professionalism of Iraq’s legal teams in handling international commercial disputes.

By successfully pursuing the claim through multiple judicial levels in Jordan, the Legal Department reinforced Iraq’s commitment to enforcing contractual rights and ensuring accountability in cross-border commercial agreements.

The decision is expected to strengthen confidence in the government’s ability to defend the interests of Iraqi public institutions through legal channels.

World.title: Ammar Al-Hakim and Iranian Science Minister discuss academic cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The head of Iraq’s National State Forces Alliance, Ammar Al-Hakim, met with Iranian Minister of Science, Research and Technology Hossein Simaei Sarraf in Baghdad to discuss expanding academic cooperation between Iraq and Iran through university partnerships, knowledge exchange, and joint educational initiatives.

The meeting focused on strengthening higher education ties while emphasizing the role of universities in addressing labor market needs and societal challenges.

According to a statement released by Al-Hakim’s office, the two sides reviewed opportunities to deepen cooperation between Iraqi and Iranian universities by promoting twinning agreements, expanding academic collaboration, and exchanging expertise.

The discussions highlighted the importance of strengthening institutional relationships to support scientific research and educational development in both countries.

During the meeting, Al-Hakim stressed that university graduates should possess skills that match the demands of today’s job market.

He also urged academic institutions to prioritize scientific research that offers practical solutions to national challenges and contributes to sustainable development.

Al-Hakim emphasized the importance of equipping university students with strong scientific knowledge to prepare them for future professional opportunities.

The Iraqi political leader underscored the role of research institutions in supporting innovation and policymaking.

He noted that universities should focus on producing research capable of addressing economic, social, and developmental issues while enhancing academic excellence.

The discussion reflected a shared interest in strengthening educational cooperation as part of broader bilateral relations.

The meeting also touched on the annual Arbaeen pilgrimage, with Al-Hakim praising the hospitality shown by Iraqis toward visitors traveling to commemorate Imam Hussein.

He said the event demonstrates positive values of solidarity and cooperation, while calling for stronger ties between societies based on shared humanitarian and religious principles.

The visit concluded with discussions on enhancing educational cooperation alongside broader people-to-people engagement between Iraq and Iran.

World.title: Iraq’s State Administration Coalition warns armed groups after September 30
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s State Administration Coalition has reaffirmed its support for restricting all weapons to state control, warning that any armed activity outside the authority of the government after September 30, 2026, will be treated under the country’s Anti-Terrorism Law.

The position was announced following the coalition’s 37th regular meeting, hosted by Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi, with the participation of Iraq’s senior political and constitutional leaders.

According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office, the meeting brought together the President of the Republic, the Speaker of Parliament, the President of the Supreme Judicial Council, the President of the Kurdistan Region, and leaders of the State Administration Coalition.

Participants reviewed Iraq’s political, security, economic, and public service developments, as well as regional events and their impact on the country.

The coalition reiterated its backing for the government’s efforts to ensure that all weapons remain under state authority, in line with the government program approved by the Iraqi Parliament.

The coalition stressed that Iraqi territory must not be used as a launchpad for attacks against neighboring countries or for actions that could draw Iraq into regional conflicts.

It warned that individuals or groups engaging in such activities would be committing crimes that threaten national security.

According to the statement, after September 30, 2026, any armed activity conducted outside the state’s legal framework will be dealt with under Iraq’s Anti-Terrorism Law.

Officials also cited constitutional provisions prohibiting the formation of armed organizations outside the official security forces.

Prime Minister Al-Zaidi briefed coalition members on government efforts to strengthen security, improve public services, implement the ministerial program, and address Iraq’s financial and economic challenges.

The coalition emphasized the need to:

Maintain national security and stability.

Protect essential public services.

Diversify Iraq’s oil export routes.

Increase non-oil revenues.

Combat corruption, smuggling, and financial waste.

The meeting highlighted the government’s commitment to protecting citizens’ interests while strengthening economic resilience.

On regional affairs, coalition leaders expressed support for diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing tensions across the Middle East.

The meeting reaffirmed Iraq’s rejection of resolving disputes through military force and emphasized Baghdad’s willingness to play a constructive role in promoting dialogue between regional parties.

Participants also discussed border security, counterterrorism cooperation, combating drug trafficking and organized crime, and strengthening relations with neighboring and international partners based on mutual respect and national sovereignty.

At the conclusion of the meeting, the State Administration Coalition called for accelerating the completion of the government formation process and submitting the government’s official program to the Council of Representatives for discussion and approval.

The coalition said completing these constitutional steps remains essential for advancing Iraq’s political stability and governance agenda.

World.title: Need to seal alliance deal with SP soon for UP polls, MPs tell Congress leadership
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress MPs from Uttar Pradesh have told the party leadership that there should be an alliance with the

for the 2027 assembly elections, brightening the prospects of a joint challenge to the governing BJP amid continuing pinpricks from local Congress functionaries.

Sources said Rahul Gandhi called a meeting with UP Congress MPs on Tuesday, where he sought the views of Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha members on the upcoming assembly polls. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra sat with Rahul during the session.

Sources said the MPs expressed a unanimous view that there should be an alliance with SP, and it should be clinched quickly. The urgency shown by the members ties in with the growing perception that the posturing by local functionaries and their angry exchanges are sending out a negative message of discord to supporters.

SP and Congress together bested BJP in UP in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls.

However, sources said, the MPs also underlined that the Congress leadership should secure âquality seatsâ from SP. The stress was as much on winnable seats as on numbers.

The meeting was attended by Pramod Tiwari, Rajiv Shukla, Imran Pratapgarhi, Kishori Lal Sharma, Ujjwal Raman Singh, Rajesh Rathore, Tanuj Punia and Imran Masood.

World.content:
NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha on Thursday cleared the Appropriation Bill, 2026, which authorises withdrawal of funds from the Consolidated Fund of India to cover excess expenditure of around Rs 54,067 crore incurred on certain services during the financial year that ended on March 31, 2023.

The bill was returned to Lok Sabha after the members' approval through a voice vote - completing the parliamentary process for a Money Bill.

During the day, RS saw multiple adjournments, as the opposition members demanded home minister

's presence in the House, leading to RS chairperson C P Radhakrishnan asking parliamentary affairs minister,

to convey their sentiments to Shah.

In the morning session, the upper House saw two adjournments amid the opposition members also demanding that the chairperson allow the leader of the opposition,

, to speak. Amid repeated appeals of the chair to the opposition MPs to go back to their seats before he could call LoP, Rijiju raised a point of order.

Citing rules, he said Kharge has been saying the same thing every day, and that is a rule against repetition.

When the House reconvened at noon, protests continued. Heeding the opposition's request, the chairperson asked Kharge to speak. But the treasury benches objected to this. World.title: Land-grab case: Supeme Court grants interim bail to Abhishek's PA
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

World.title: UPI charges: Lok Sabha passes bill for government to make changes
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha on Thursday passed a bill that seeks to ease tax rules to attract investments and remove the existing legal provision that prevents banks and payment service providers from charging Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on notified electronic payment modes.

The bill â passed without discussion amid din â also proposes to remove the linkage between the Payment and Settlement Systems Act and the I-Tax Act and give legal backing to the government to modify the zero-MDR framework on UPI and RuPay card transactions. Outside the House, however, there was an exchange between FM

âMore importantly, the UPI and services steering committee headed by NPCI is yet to decide on the MDR. This will happen after Parliament passes the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026... All this could have been discussed on the floor of the House if your party @INCIndia (Congress) engages constructively in Parliament when the bill was/is tabled,â she said.

While leaving person-to-payments outside MDRâs ambit, banks and fintechs may be permitted to charge 0.25% to 0.4% on payments to businesses in excess of Rs 2,000 with an overall ceiling on how much can be charged.

Officials have argued that the levy will be lower than what is charged on credit and debit cards, and most merchants will not pass it on to consumers.

World.title: 15 Indian seafarers killed in West Asia and Black Sea conflicts: Regulator
World.content:
Following shipping minister's directions, DGMA has put in place a mechanism to track every Indian seafarer operating in high-risk water

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea have claimed the lives of 15 Indian seafarers, while two remain missing in 57 separate incidents over the past three months, India's maritime regulator, the Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA), said Thursday, describing the current geopolitical situation as "extremely challenging".Addressing the National Port Security Conference in the national capital, DGMA Shyam Jagannathan said drone and missile attacks on defenceless merchant vessels had become rampant in parts of the Black Sea. "Piracy off the coast of Somalia is reappearing. The Houthi security threat, which accounted for more than 154 incidents in 2024, has resurfaced," he said.Jagannathan said the conflicts had significantly increased global logistics costs. He said since the end of Feb, the DGMA has been in an extremely high state of alert.The regulator said it had strengthened coordination for rescue operations, vessel movements and issuance of advisories, while ensuring compliance with best management practices for piracy response, validation of citadel preparedness and coordination among multiple security agencies.Following directions from shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal, the DGMA has also put in place a mechanism to track every Indian seafarer operating in high-risk waters, making the administration accountable for their safety, security and early repatriation.Speaking at the conference, Sonowal said as India's maritime footprint expands, "responsibility to secure it grows".

World.title: Rahul ignored plan to end my fast, says Sonam Wangchuk
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

said his wife Gitanjali had tried to get

to offer him juice to end his 26-day hunger strike at Jantar Mantar but received no positive response, leaving him disappointed with the Congress leader and other political parties.

"We were pondering on breaking my fast through Rahul Gandhi ji and Gitanjali was working on that," Wangchuk said. "She was working hard to see if Rahul ji could break my fast. She didn't get a positive response".

Wangchuk also accused Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh of breaking a promise not to release photos of them offering him soup until he could announce the end of his fast with opposition and student leaders represented.

"They pledged they won't release it and they broke the promise. So I have lost trust in all these leaders," he said.

Wangchuk said his wife's subsequent criticism of Rahul had stemmed partly from his own disappointment. He also said netas had come to the Jantar Mantar agitation in small numbers and late. "Similarly, as I said, at Jantar Mantar very few and very late came, so this disappointment caught on her when she made a single comment about them," he added.





Gitanjali was targeted online after questioning Rahul's decision to stage a protest outside the PM's residence. Wangchuk said she had made several strong comments against BJP and Hindutva forces as well, but while they kept quiet, the Congress "ecosystem" turned on her for criticising Gandhi.

World.title: Purandeswari condemns attack on PG medical student in Rajamahendravaram
World.content:
Rajamahendravaram MP Daggubati Purandeswari has condemned the brutal act of two youths, who allegedly rammed their car into a two-wheeler and grievously injured a PG medical student, Priyanka, who was pillion-riding, on August 3.

According to the police, the accused, N. Daswanth and Andrew Joseph, rammed their car into the two-wheeler, while its rider and Dr. Priyanka were returning from a cinema hall, on A.V. Appa Rao Road under Prakash Nagar police station limits.

Dr. Priyanka suffered critical head injury, and was rushed to a private hospital, where her condition was stated to be critical. A native of Hyderabad, the victim was studying in a medical college in Rajamahendravaram.

In a release on Thursday, Ms. Purandeswari expressed concern over the attack, and assured to take stern action against the accused.

World.title: Moderate rain in north A.P. barely enough to bridge deficit in State
World.content:
Several districts in the northern part of Andhra Pradesh, including Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram, Anakapalli and Parvathipuram-Manyam, received moderate rain on Thursday. But, it is barely enough to bridge the rainfall deficit recorded in these districts, which ranges from 40% to 60%.

On Thursday, the day’s highest rain between 8.30 a.m. and 7 p.m. was recorded in Dattirajeru of Vizianagaram district at 82.7 mm.

Other places that received moderate rain on Thursday are: Salur of Parvathipuram Manyam (65.75 mm) , Butchiraju Palem of Visakhapatnam district (58 mm), Parvada of Anakapalli district (56.75 mm) , Kotapadu of Anakapalli (55.5 mm), Commonpoint area of Visakhapatnam district (53.75 mm) and Vijayarampuram in Srikakulam district (40.5 mm).

Other places in these districts received rain below 40 mm. However, it was not enough to bring down the deficit percentages, as Srikakulam recorded a deficit of 55.1%, followed by Parvathipuram-Manyam (49.3%), Anakapalli (41.8%) and Vizianagaram (42.4%).

As of August 6, the overall deficit in Andhra Pradesh stands at 49.1%, a slight fall from July 31 when it stood at 52.4%. So far, the State has received 146.1 mm of rain as against the normal of 286.9 mm between June 1 and August 6, according to the Directorate of Economics and Statistics (DES).

Annamayya district, with 71.7%, leads the State with the steepest rainfall deficit, followed by Chittoor (64.1%), Prakasam (60.6%) and Visakhapatnam by 60.3%.

According to the updated forecast issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) on Thursday, there may not be much rain in the State this week, until August 13.

According to the IMD’s rainfall outlook for August, a few stations in the State, especially coastal areas and those sharing a border with Telangana and Karnataka, may receive normal to above-normal rain. However, the State may see above-normal daytime temperatures and minimum temperatures this month.

World.title: Justice for AgriGold victims brooks no delay, Naidu officials
World.content:
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Thursday directed officials to expedite measures to ensure early justice for victims of the AgriGold scam and warned against attempts to delay the process through legal interventions.
